sections.title: Judges: what each one decides and how a call runs
sections.summary: Describes the 10 judges, the forced decide call, the three attempts with back-off, the failure result of each judge, routed answers, decision override, and the native-only judge route.
sections.body:
## Why the engine calls judges

A session needs a few decisions that no fixed rule can make. Examples are the category of a request, the question whether research is enough, and the place where a typed answer goes. Without a judge, the planner would need a hard-coded rule for each case, or it would ask the user every time.

A judge is one model call that returns JSON that matches a schema. The runner stores the JSON as a `DecisionMade` event with a `reason`. The module comment of [`crates/ostra-engine/src/judge.rs`](crates/ostra-engine/src/judge.rs) states the rule: judge calls are the only places where a model makes an orchestration decision. The planner (`next_steps`) still decides when to call a judge and which gate to open. A judge only answers the question that the planner asks.

This page covers the ten judges, one call from start to end, the failure result of each judge, routed answers, decision override, and the judge route. The page "Gates: the 14 kinds, their answers, and YOLO" covers the gates that some judges help to answer. The page "The planner, steps, and the drive loop" covers how the planner emits `Step::Judge`.

## The ten judges

`JudgeKind` in [`crates/ostra-core/src/event.rs`](crates/ostra-core/src/event.rs) has ten variants. The event log stores a variant in snake_case, for example `route_answer`. `JudgeKind::as_str` gives the kebab form, for example `route-answer`. That form names the prompt file `assets/judges/<name>.md`.

The `subject` string of a `Step::Judge` names what the decision is about. The runner builds the step key `judge:{kind}:{subject}`. Because of this key, the runner never runs two equal judge calls at the same time.

| Judge | The planner asks when | Subject | The judge decides |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `classify` | The session has no category and no classify decision. | none | Category, projects in scope, first research tasks, opt-ins for tests and docs, title. |
| `sufficiency` | Every research task ended, some `not_covered` items are not judged, and fewer than 3 rounds ran. | Task indexes, comma separated | Which uncovered items need more research. |
| `stakes` | An `IMPLEMENT` request on the full track has an approved spec and no stakes decision. | none | `low`, `medium`, or `high`. |
| `track` | An `IMPLEMENT` request finished research and has no track. | none | `light` or `full`. |
| `route-answer` | A gate answer has content, or added context waits. | Gate ID or `amendment:{i}` | Route, disposition per item, extra research, notes to forget. |
| `feedback` | A feedback round at the implementation review has no route. | Round index | Route, and one target for each project that changes. |
| `rescue` | A work loop got the status `STUCK` from an agent. | Execution ID | `explore`, `rerun`, or `gate`. |
| `resolve-review` | A review loop reached its cap under YOLO. | `phase:N` or `phase:N:tests` | `fix` with instructions, or `block`. |
| `yolo-answer` | YOLO is on and an open gate needs judgment. | Gate ID | The answer of the gate. |
| `completion` | Nothing runs, every created project finished init, no ask is open, and no completion decision exists. | none | The Markdown of the completion report. |

## What each judge sees and decides

The function `judge_input` in [`crates/ostra-engine/src/judge_input.rs`](crates/ostra-engine/src/judge_input.rs) builds the user message of each judge from the folded session state. It returns the message and a short summary that the runner stores with the decision. A file excerpt in a message has at most `FILE_EXCERPT` = 24,000 characters. The text `(truncated at 24000 characters)` marks a cut. A file that the engine cannot read becomes the text `(could not read <path>)`.

### classify

The input holds the full request (with the lists of attached files and uploads), the toggles of the New task form (tests, docs, yolo), the pinned projects, and every workspace project with its path, stack, init status, and module-map areas. When the user pinned projects, the input shows only those projects.

The output has `category`, `projects`, `explore_tasks`, `opts_in`, `reason`, and `title`. The category is one of `RESEARCH`, `SPEC`, `PLAN`, `IMPLEMENT`, `VERIFY`, `TEST`, `DOCS`, `PROMPT`, `QUICK_CHANGE`, and `QUICK_ANSWER`. The fold method `apply_classify` in [`crates/ostra-engine/src/state.rs`](crates/ostra-engine/src/state.rs) applies the output:

- Pinned projects replace the projects that the judge picked (Rule O6).
- A project key that does not exist is dropped. If the scope is empty, the first project joins it.
- `RESEARCH`, `SPEC`, `PLAN`, and `IMPLEMENT` always get research. If the judge gives no task, the engine makes one task for each project in scope with the full request (Rule D1).
- `clean_title` makes the title one line without wrapping quotes or a final period, and cuts it to `TITLE_CHARS` = 60 characters.

The prompt tells the judge to choose by what the request asks Ostra to produce, not by its first verb. If two categories fit, the judge picks the one that runs more of the pipeline. The reason is that a stage that the request did not need costs one round, and a skipped stage that it needed gives a wrong result.

### sufficiency

The input holds the request, the result of each research task (scope, findings, document path), and the `Not covered` items of the tasks under judgment. For each item the output gives `needed`, a `reason`, and, when needed, a `task` with a project and an instruction. The fold turns each needed item into a research task with the origin `Sufficiency`. It skips a task when an unfinished task with the same project and text exists (Rule D2). The prompt tells the judge to mark an item as needed when it is not sure, because a wasted research round costs less than a wrong spec.

### stakes

The input holds the request, the approved spec (deliverable count, requirement count, summary, and an excerpt), and the projects in scope. When the output is `low` and the category is `IMPLEMENT`, the fold skips the plan stage and creates one inline phase for each project. The prompt tells the judge to resolve doubt upward, because a skipped plan also removes the phase review.

### track

The input holds the request, the scope, and every research task with an excerpt of its document. A track excerpt has at most `TRACK_EXCERPT` = 12,000 characters. The output `light` builds one reviewed phase for each project from the research. The output `full` runs spec, fact-check, approvals, and plan first. The default is `light`. If the New task form forced `options.track`, the planner never calls this judge.

### route-answer

The input depends on the subject. For a gate, it holds the request, the session facts (category, track, projects, research, spec, plan phases, kept notes), the gate (kind, title, explanation), and the user answer. For an open-questions gate, each question appears with its options numbered as the user saw them. For an amendment, it holds the added text and the list of work that Ostra interrupted. The section "Routed answers and dispositions" below explains the output.

### feedback

The input holds the request, the track, the scope, the spec excerpt (or a note that no spec exists), the phases with their report paths, the research facts, the kept notes, and the feedback text. The schema requires at least one target (`minItems` 1), and the runner rejects an output with no target. The output also carries `items`, `research`, and `forget`, which work like the output of `route-answer`.

### rescue

The input holds the request, the stuck agent and its project, the phase, the diagnostic and the need text from the agent, and the earlier rescue decisions of the session. The prompt mentions recalled lessons, but `judge_input` does not add them. The three actions are:

- `rerun`: the judge knows the missing fact and writes it in `fact`. The loop runs again with that fact.
- `explore`: a research task finds the fact, then the loop runs again.
- `gate`: only the user can give the fact, so the engine opens a `stuck` gate.

The prompt tells the judge to choose `gate` after two rescues of the same phase with the same diagnostic. The code does not enforce this rule.

### resolve-review

The input holds the loop state (review passes, resolution rounds), the open findings, the review ledger, and the phase file. With `fix`, the fold sends one instruction for each finding to the fix agent, adds 1 to `extra_cap` for one verification review, and counts one resolution round. With `block`, the phase becomes blocked. The loop returns to the judge only while the open count falls.

### yolo-answer

The input holds the request, the gate title and explanation, the gate payload as JSON, and extra context for three gate kinds: research findings for open questions, a spec excerpt for a spec approval, and a plan excerpt for a plan approval. The output schema embeds the answer schema of the gate. The page about gates lists the gate kinds that use this judge.

### completion

The input holds the request, the category, the YOLO flag, and a state summary: research, spec, plan or stakes, each phase with its outcome, LOW findings left open, open BLOCKER findings, test and docs status, closing choices and format result of each project, the decisions that YOLO made, and the session notes. For a `QUICK_ANSWER` session, the input holds only the request and the category. The output `report_markdown` becomes the completion report. The prompt orders the sections: Summary, Phases, Checks, Not run, Blocked, Decided for you.

## One judge call from start to end

### Sequence of one judge call

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Planner as next_steps
    participant Driver as drive loop
    participant Runner as perform_judge
    participant Input as judge_input
    participant Services as Services judge
    participant Provider as providers structured
    participant Log as event log and fold
    Planner->>Driver: Step Judge with kind and subject
    Driver->>Runner: perform step
    Runner->>Input: judge_input of state snapshot
    Input-->>Runner: user message and summary
    Runner->>Services: judge with route system input schema Effort Low
    Services->>Provider: structured with forced decide tool
    Provider-->>Services: tool input and usage
    Services-->>Runner: value and usage
    Runner->>Log: append DecisionMade
    Log-->>Driver: wake and plan again
```

The runner does these steps in `perform_judge` and `call_judge` in [`crates/ostra-engine/src/runner.rs`](crates/ostra-engine/src/runner.rs):

1. Take a snapshot of the state and build the user message with `judge_input`.
2. Build the output schema with `output_schema(kind, answer_schema)`.
3. Read the system prompt with `SpawnFactory::judge_prompt(kind.as_str())`. A missing prompt gives the error `No prompt for the <kind> judge.`
4. Resolve the route (see "The judge route" below).
5. Call `Services::judge` up to 3 times. Each call is a forced `decide` call.
6. Check the output with the validator of the kind. A valid output becomes a `DecisionMade` event with the output, the `reason`, the subject, and the summary.

The server implements `Services::judge` in [`crates/ostra-server/src/services.rs`](crates/ostra-server/src/services.rs). It finds the provider for the model and calls `ostra_providers::structured`. That function sends the schema as the input schema of a tool named `decide` and sets `tool_choice` to that tool. Because the model must call the tool, the engine gets JSON and never parses prose. The system prompt is cached, and `max_tokens` is 16,000.

If the model does not call the tool, `structured` adds one reminder turn: `Call the decide tool now with your decision. Do not answer in text.` If the second turn also has no tool call, it returns the error `the model did not call the decide tool`. A refusal returns an error at once. One attempt of the runner can thus use 2 model turns.

### The retry loop

```rust
for attempt in 0..3 {
    match self.services.judge(&route, &system, &input, schema.clone(), Effort::Low).await {
        Ok((value, usage)) => {
            *lock(&self.judge_cost).entry(session.clone()).or_insert(0.0) += usage.cost_usd;
            if validate(&value) { /* append DecisionMade and return */ }
            last = "the answer did not match the schema".into();
        }
        Err(e) => last = e,
    }
    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(500 * (attempt + 1))).await;
}
```

After a failed attempt, the runner waits 500 ms, then 1,000 ms, then 1,500 ms. The wait also follows the third attempt, so a call that fails 3 times takes about 3 seconds of waiting before it returns the error `The <kind> judge call failed: <last error>`. The runner adds the cost of each call that returns a value to `judge_cost`, even when the output fails validation.

### The validators

| Judge | The output is valid when |
| --- | --- |
| `classify`, `sufficiency`, `stakes`, `track`, `route-answer`, `rescue`, `resolve-review`, `completion` | It deserializes into the `*Out` type of the judge in `judge.rs`. |
| `feedback` | It deserializes into `FeedbackOut` and `targets` is not empty. |
| `yolo-answer` | Always. The engine checks the answer later with `yolo_answer_from_judge`. |

## The judge route

The judge route is the route key `judge` (`JUDGE_ROUTE` in `crates/ostra-core/src/agent.rs`). The runner resolves it on every call with `resolve_route(global, workspace, RouteQuery::new(JUDGE_ROUTE, Tier::Advanced))`. The effort is `Effort::Low`. Because the engine reads the settings on every call, a change to the model route applies to the next judge call without a restart.

The judge route always uses the native executor. `resolve_executor` in [`crates/ostra-core/src/config.rs`](crates/ostra-core/src/config.rs) returns `ExecutorKind::Native` for this key. The reason is that a judge call is an engine call and not an agent execution, so it has no harness process, no sandbox, and no tools. The validation of workspace settings rejects the key `routing.executor.byAgent.judge` with the message `Judge calls always run natively; remove this route.`

A judge call does not take an execution slot, because it is short. The budget guard does not count its cost. The session cost in the session list includes the judge cost. If the provider has no working API key, every judge call fails (see the next section).

## When a judge call fails

The runner handles a failed call after 3 attempts. A missing prompt and a route that does not resolve fail in the same way, but without attempts.

| Judge | Result after the failure |
| --- | --- |
| `completion` | The runner appends a fallback `DecisionMade` with the summary `Fallback after a failed judge call`. Its report starts with `# Session complete` and says that the completion judge failed. Then it lists the state facts. The session still completes with a report. |
| `yolo-answer` | The runner appends a `Note`: `YOLO could not answer "<title>": <error>. The gate waits for you.` The gate stays open for the user. |
| `classify`, `sufficiency`, `stakes`, `track`, `route-answer`, `feedback`, `rescue`, `resolve-review` | The runner appends `SessionFailed` with the error text and `Check that the judge route has a provider with a working API key.` The session ends. |

Two more cases exist for the YOLO judge. If the output fails `yolo_answer_from_judge`, the runner appends a `Note` that starts with `The YOLO answer was refused:` and the gate waits. If the fold gets a classify output that does not match `ClassifyOut`, the session fails with `The Classify judge returned output that does not match its schema.` The runner validates first, so this case is rare.

### What happens when the state changes during a call

A judge call can run for seconds. The fold ignores a decision that no longer fits the state:

- A `rescue` decision applies only if the loop is still in `LoopNext::Rescue` for the same execution.
- A `route-answer` decision applies only if a held answer or a waiting loop for that gate exists, or if the amendment is still pending.
- A `feedback` decision applies only if the round has no route.
- A `resolve-review` decision applies only if the loop is still in `LoopNext::Resolve`.

## Routed answers and dispositions

A routed answer is a gate answer or an amendment that waits for the `route-answer` judge (or the `feedback` judge) before any agent sees it. The reason is the rule of Rule J1: an answer reaches a later agent only if it lands in the artifact or the input that this agent reads. The plan agent reads the spec and nothing else. A typed answer such as `use sqlx` can be an instruction for a later stage, a requirement change, or an order to ignore the text. Only a judge can tell which one.

The flag `routed` on `GateAnswered` and `RequestAmended` records this. Older logs have `routed = false` (the field has `#[serde(default)]`), so the fold still replays them as before. The page about gates lists which answers need a route.

### The output of route-answer

- `route` is `requirement_change`, `implementation_detail`, or `stage_choice`. The fold acts differently only on `requirement_change`. At a work-loop gate with a spec, it stops the phase and sends the text into the spec, so the spec is generated again and approved again (Rule D10). At the spec and plan gates, every delivered answer goes into the spec. If the session has no spec, the answer goes to the phase. The prompt says that doubt resolves to `requirement_change`, because a stale spec corrupts every later stage.
- `items` has one item for each open question ID, or one item with the ID `answer` for a single text. Each item has a `disposition`, a `note`, and `stages`.
- `research` has at most `MAX_ANSWER_RESEARCH` = 3 explore tasks. The fold uses the primary project when a task names a project that the session does not have.
- `forget` lists IDs of earlier notes (`N1`, `N2`, and so on) that the user takes back or replaces.
- `reason` is one or two sentences for the user.

### The three dispositions

| Disposition | Meaning | What the engine does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `deliver` | The answer settles the current stage or changes what the agent must do. This is the default. | The agent that asked gets the answer as written. |
| `remember` | The whole answer concerns a later stage. | Nothing reaches the current stage. The note reaches the stages in `stages`. |
| `discard` | The user told Ostra to ignore the text. | Nothing reaches any agent. The answer stays in the log. |

`stages` uses `implement`, `tests`, and `docs`. The spawn block of the implementer shows the notes for `implement`. The spawn blocks of the write-test agent and the execution-path analyzer show the notes for `tests`. The spawn blocks of the documentation agents and the system-architecture agent show the notes for `docs`. Each block lists them under the label `User notes`.

The prompt tells the judge to use `discard` only when the user says so in the user's own words. A wrong `discard` loses a decision of the user.

```rust
pub fn item_for(items: &[AnswerItem], id: &str) -> AnswerItem {
    let parts = parts_for(items, id);
    let has = |d: Disposition| parts.iter().any(|p| p.disposition == d);
    let disposition = if parts.is_empty() || has(Disposition::Deliver) {
        Disposition::Deliver
    } else if has(Disposition::Remember) { Disposition::Remember } else { Disposition::Discard };
    ...
}
```

A model sometimes splits one answer into parts. `item_for` merges the parts of one ID. `deliver` wins over `remember`, and `remember` wins over `discard`, because the user gave the answer. An answer that the judge did not name is delivered. On a gate with one text, every item counts for that text, whatever ID it carries.

The fold keeps a remembered note as a `UserNote` with the ID `N<count + 1>`. A forgotten note stays in the log and reaches no agent. A note that the judge kept without text takes the answer text.

## Override a decision

The user can replace a decision of four judges: `classify`, `stakes`, `track`, and `sufficiency`. The route is `POST /api/decisions/{id}/override` with the body fields `output` and `reason`. `Engine::override_decision` checks two things:

1. `SessionState::can_override` must be true. Otherwise the error is `Work that depends on this decision has already started, so it can no longer be overridden.`
2. The new `output` must deserialize into the output type of the judge. Otherwise the error is `The override does not match the decision's output shape.`

| Judge | The override works while |
| --- | --- |
| `classify` | No research task started and no phase has work. |
| `stakes` | No plan run exists and no phase started. |
| `track` | No spec run exists and no phase started. |
| `sufficiency` | No spec run exists. |

A terminal session never accepts an override. The runner appends `DecisionOverridden`, and the fold runs the decision logic again with `overriding = true`. A new `stakes` decision clears the phases. A new `sufficiency` decision first removes the queued tasks of origin `Sufficiency` that did not start. The other six judges have no override, because their decisions apply to work that starts at once.

## Add a judge

Follow these steps. Each step is a place where the code must know the new kind.

1. Add a variant to `JudgeKind` and to `as_str` in `crates/ostra-core/src/event.rs`.
2. Add the `*Out` type and a branch in `output_schema` in `crates/ostra-engine/src/judge.rs`.
3. Add the prompt file `assets/judges/<name>.md`. The file stem must equal the `as_str` value.
4. Add a branch in `judge_input` and a branch in the validator of `perform_judge`.
5. Add a branch in `SessionState::on_decision` in `crates/ostra-engine/src/state.rs`.
6. Make `next_steps` emit `Step::Judge` for the new kind.
7. Add a conformance fixture in `tests/conformance/main.rs` and a case in `tests/evals/judges.toml`.

The Rust compiler flags steps 1 to 5 because the `match` expressions are exhaustive.

## Limits

| Value | Number | Holder |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Attempts of one judge call | 3 | `for attempt in 0..3` in `call_judge` |
| Wait after a failed attempt | 500, 1,000, 1,500 ms | `500 * (attempt + 1)` in `call_judge` |
| Model turns in one attempt | 2 | `for attempt in 0..2` in `ostra_providers::structured` |
| Effort and tier of a judge call | `Low`, `Advanced` | `call_judge` |
| Output tokens | 16,000 | `structured_cancellable` |
| Sufficiency rounds | 3 | `SUFFICIENCY_ROUNDS` in `state.rs` |
| Research tasks of one answer | 3 | `MAX_ANSWER_RESEARCH` in `judge.rs` |
| File excerpt in a judge input | 24,000 characters | `FILE_EXCERPT` in `judge_input.rs` |
| Research excerpt for the track judge | 12,000 characters | `TRACK_EXCERPT` in `judge_input.rs` |
| Session title | 60 characters | `TITLE_CHARS` in `judge.rs` |

The user sees each decision, its `reason`, and the override button in the session detail (`view::detail` returns the decisions with `can_override`). The user cannot change the retry numbers. They are constants in the code.

sections.title: Gates: the 14 kinds, their answers, and YOLO
sections.summary: Lists each gate kind with its stage, trigger, answer shape, validation message, and YOLO answer. Explains which gates YOLO never answers and how the budget gate works.
sections.body:
## Why the engine has gates

A session reaches points where only the user can decide: approve a spec, give a missing fact, spend more money, or accept a result. Without a defined stop, the engine would guess or would run past the point. A gate is such a stop. The planner opens a gate, the session waits for that decision, and the answer enters the event log.

This page lists the 14 gate kinds. For each kind it gives the stage, the trigger, the answer shape, the validation, and the YOLO answer. It also explains the budget gate and the cases that change the result. The console forms for gates are in the page "Gate forms, book reader, and HTML export". The loops that open the work-loop gates are in "The implement, review, autofix, and rescue loop". The page "Judges: what each one decides and how a call runs" explains the judges that route a typed answer.

## How a gate opens and closes

The type `GatePayload` in [`crates/ostra-core/src/event.rs`](crates/ostra-core/src/event.rs) has one variant for each gate kind. The planner returns `Step::OpenGate` with a title, an explanation, and a payload. The runner appends `GateOpened` with a new `GateId`. The planner never opens a gate twice: the step key is `gate:{kind}:{owner}`, and the fold stores the open gate on the track that owns it.

### Sequence of one gate

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Planner as next_steps
    participant Runner as Engine runner
    participant Log as event log and fold
    participant User as console or API
    participant Judge as route-answer judge
    Planner->>Runner: Step OpenGate with payload
    Runner->>Log: append GateOpened
    User->>Runner: POST gates answer
    Runner->>Runner: validate_answer
    Runner->>Log: append GateAnswered with routed flag
    Log-->>Planner: state shows the answer
    Planner->>Judge: Step Judge when routed is true
    Judge-->>Log: DecisionMade applies the answer
```

The route is `POST /api/gates/{id}/answer` with a `GateAnswer` in the body. `Engine::answer_gate` in [`crates/ostra-engine/src/runner.rs`](crates/ostra-engine/src/runner.rs) does these steps:

1. Load the gate. A gate that does not exist gives the error `gate <id>`. A gate that has an answer gives `This gate was already answered.`
2. Run `validate_answer` (see the table of messages below).
3. For a spec or plan approval, check the fact-check verdict.
4. For the answer `always-in-workspace` on a permission gate, add the suggested allow rule to the workspace settings.
5. Append `GateAnswered` with `source: User` and the `routed` flag from `answer_needs_route`.
6. For a permission gate, wake the waiting tool call with the answer.

The fold method `on_gate_answered` in [`crates/ostra-engine/src/state.rs`](crates/ostra-engine/src/state.rs) ignores an answer for an unknown or answered gate. This idempotence protects the state when two answers arrive at the same time.

## The answer shapes

`GateAnswer` has six variants. The `kind` field names the variant in JSON.

| Variant | Fields | Used by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `questions` | `answers`: list of `{id, question, answer}` | `open_questions` |
| `approval` | `approved`, `feedback` | `spec_approval`, `plan_approval` |
| `choice` | `option`, `text` | `fact_check_recurring`, `review_cap`, `stuck`, `phase_blocked`, `harness_failure`, `execution_failed`, `budget_reached`, `implementation_review` |
| `closing` | `items`: list of `{project, tests, docs}` | `closing_gate` |
| `permission` | `answer`: `allow-once`, `always-in-workspace`, or `deny` | `permission` |
| `skills` | `decisions`: list of `{name, disposition}` | `skill_approval` |

The `choice` variant carries a `text` field for a stated fact, for instructions, or for an amount of dollars.

### Validation of an answer

`validate_answer` checks only the shape and a few content rules. It does not check the `option` string of most `choice` gates.

| Case | Error message |
| --- | --- |
| The variant does not fit the gate kind | `That answer does not fit this gate.` |
| An open-questions answer has no entry, or a blank entry, for a question | `Answer <id> before continuing.` |
| An approval has `approved: false` and no feedback text | `Say what to change.` |
| An approval of a spec or plan has `approved: true` and the fact-check has no PASS on this version | `Approval requires a fact-check PASS on this version.` |
| An implementation review answer is `feedback` with no text | `Say what to change.` |
| An implementation review answer is neither `done` nor `feedback` | `Answer done, or feedback with what to change.` |
| The gate has an answer | `This gate was already answered.` |

An unknown `option` on the other choice gates is not an error. The fold treats it as the safe branch. For `review_cap`, `stuck`, and `phase_blocked`, the safe branch blocks the phase. For `budget_reached`, it stops the session. For `execution_failed` and `harness_failure`, it abandons the step. For `fact_check_recurring`, every option except `stop` starts another round, so send `stop` to stop.

## The 14 gate kinds

The stage is the board stage that shows the gate (`GatePayload::stage`). The YOLO column shows the answer under YOLO. The next section explains YOLO.

| Kind | Stage | Answer | YOLO answer |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open_questions` | `OpenQuestions` | `questions` | YOLO judge. |
| `spec_approval` | `SpecApproval` | `approval` | YOLO judge. |
| `plan_approval` | `PlanApproval` | `approval` | YOLO judge. |
| `fact_check_recurring` | `FactCheckSpec` or `FactCheckPlan` | `choice`: `another-round`, `stop` | `another-round` while `passes` is below 6, else `stop`. |
| `review_cap` | `Review` or `TestReview` | `choice`: `another-pass`, `stop` | `another-pass`. |
| `stuck` | `Rescue` | `choice`: `fact` with text, `block` | YOLO judge. |
| `phase_blocked` | `Implement` | `choice`: `retry` with optional text, `leave` | `leave`. |
| `closing_gate` | `ClosingGate` | `closing` | Fixed choice from the request. |
| `permission` | `Implement` | `permission` | Allow once, at once. |
| `harness_failure` | `Implement` | `choice`: `retry`, `native` | `native`. |
| `skill_approval` | `SkillApproval` | `skills` | The default dispositions of the proposal. |
| `execution_failed` | `Implement` | `choice`: `retry`, `abandon` | `retry` for the first 2 gates of one agent, then `abandon`. Never for a stopped run. |
| `implementation_review` | `ImplementationReview` | `choice`: `done`, `feedback` with text | `done`. |
| `budget_reached` | `Intake` | `choice`: `raise` with optional amount, `stop` | None. YOLO never answers it. |

### When each gate opens

- **`open_questions`.** The spec or the plan has open questions and the questions of this version were not asked yet. The spec stage asks before any fact-check (Rule D3). The title is `Questions about the requirements` for a spec and `Questions from the plan` for a plan. Answers go into the spec first, because only the spec can hold a requirement (Rule D10).
- **`spec_approval`.** The spec passed the fact-check and the category needs an approval (`PLAN` and `IMPLEMENT` on the full track). The title is `Approve the spec`. The gate carries the LOW findings of the passing check.
- **`plan_approval`.** The plan passed the fact-check. The title is `Approve the plan`. The payload holds the phase list. Approval adopts the phases.
- **`fact_check_recurring`.** The fact-check failed `FACTCHECK_RECURRING_LIMIT` = 3 times in a row on the same artifact. The title is `The spec fact-check keeps failing` for a spec. Each `another-round` allows 3 more failures before the next gate.
- **`review_cap`.** A review loop used its passes (`REVIEW_CAP` = 3 plus `extra_cap`) and HIGH or MEDIUM findings remain. The title is `Review of phase N reached its cap`. Under YOLO the loop goes to the `resolve-review` judge and the gate never opens, unless YOLO is switched on while a loop waits at the cap.
- **`stuck`.** The `rescue` judge chose `gate`. The title is `Phase N is stuck`. The payload holds the diagnostic and the need text of the agent.
- **`phase_blocked`.** A phase is blocked and the engine announced it. The gate opens only when YOLO is off and the loop has no answered gate (Rule D9). Phases that depend on it leave the queue. Independent phases continue.
- **`closing_gate`.** The code of a project is done, its format command ran, and the request did not ask for both tests and docs (Rules T3, T6). The title is `Tests and documentation`. Projects that reach this point together share one gate.
- **`permission`.** A tool call of an agent needs approval from the policy. The title is `<agent> asks to run <tool>`. The payload has a suggested allow rule.
- **`harness_failure`.** An execution failed with an error that starts with `harness-`, after the automatic retry. The title is `<Harness> could not run`. The planner also uses it for a harness that is not signed in.
- **`skill_approval`.** The init flow of a project proposed skills. The title is `Approve the skills`. Each skill has a disposition: `generate`, `regenerate`, `reuse`, or `drop`.
- **`execution_failed`.** An execution ended without a usable result after its retry, or the user stopped it. The title is `<agent> failed` or `You stopped <agent>`. The init flow opens the same gate for the initializer.
- **`implementation_review`.** Every phase is terminal, nothing runs, and no feedback round waits for a route (Rule F1). The title is `Review the implementation`. The runner writes the session context file before it appends this gate.
- **`budget_reached`.** A spawn is blocked because the spend reached the limit (see the budget section).

### What each answer does in the fold

- `open_questions`: a spec answer sets `needs_run` so that `generate-spec` runs again with the answers. A plan answer becomes a requirement change in the spec.
- `spec_approval` and `plan_approval`: `approved: true` with a PASS on the current version approves the artifact. Text in `feedback` becomes a spec change. A revoked gate (a change landed after it opened) gets no approval, because its answer is stale.
- `fact_check_recurring`: `stop` marks the artifact as stopped, and the planner then fails the session with `The spec stage was stopped.` or `The plan stage was stopped.` Any other option allows 3 more failures. Text becomes a spec change.
- `review_cap`: `another-pass` adds 1 to `extra_cap` and runs a fix pass. Any other answer blocks the phase.
- `stuck`: `fact` with text runs the agent again with the fact. Any other answer blocks the phase.
- `phase_blocked`: `retry` gives the loop `iterations` more passes and runs a fix. Text becomes an instruction. `leave` keeps the phase blocked.
- `closing_gate`: for each project, the fold sets the closing choice `(tests, docs)`. A stage that the request already asked for is true, and the user answer sets the other stages. A project that the answer omits gets false for each stage that the gate asked about.
- `harness_failure` and `execution_failed`: `retry` or `native` runs the step again, and `native` also forces the native executor for that agent. Other answers abandon the step. The page about the work loop explains abandon.
- `skill_approval`: the decisions go to the init track, which then generates skills.
- `implementation_review`: `feedback` with text creates a feedback round, and `done` sets `feedback.accepted`.
- `permission`: the answer returns to the waiting tool call. The fold does not change the state.

## Answers that a judge routes

A routed answer waits for the `route-answer` judge (or the `feedback` judge) before the fold applies it. `answer_needs_route` decides this when the answer is recorded. The rule is that only an answer with content needs a route. A bare choice has one meaning.

| Gate | The answer is routed when |
| --- | --- |
| `open_questions` | `answers` is not empty. |
| `spec_approval`, `plan_approval` | `feedback` has text. |
| `fact_check_recurring` | The option is not `stop` and `text` has content. |
| `review_cap` | The option is `another-pass` and `text` has content. |
| `stuck` | The option is `fact` and `text` has content. |
| `phase_blocked` | The option is `retry` and `text` has content. |
| `implementation_review` | The option is `feedback` and `text` has content. |
| All other cases | Never. The fold applies the answer as it is. |

While an answer waits for its judge, the planner starts nothing for that track. The answer of a spec gate sits in `held_answers`. The answer of a work-loop gate puts the loop in `LoopNext::AwaitRoute`.

## YOLO

YOLO is a session mode in which the engine answers gates for the user. The engine switches it on in three ways: the New task form sets `options.yolo`, the workspace setting `yolo.default` forces it on for every new session, and `POST /api/sessions/{id}/yolo` with `enabled` toggles it later. The event `YoloSet` records each toggle. When the user switches YOLO on, `Engine::set_yolo` also answers each waiting permission gate with `allow-once`.

Under YOLO, the planner emits `Step::YoloAnswer` for every open gate, with two exceptions. It skips `permission` gates, because the run that asks answers them itself. It skips gates for which `yolo_leaves_open` is true. The runner then runs `perform_yolo`, which asks `yolo_plan` in [`crates/ostra-engine/src/judge_input.rs`](crates/ostra-engine/src/judge_input.rs) for a plan. A plan is either a fixed answer or a judge call. The runner appends `GateAnswered` with `source: Yolo` and the reason of the plan.

### Fixed answers

- `implementation_review`: `done`. The reason is that only the user can say what to change.
- `closing_gate`: for each item, `tests` is true only if the item did not ask (`ask_tests` is false) and the request wants tests. `docs` follows the same rule. Without an explicit request, the answer is no tests and no docs (Rules T2, T3).
- `fact_check_recurring`: `another-round` while `passes` is below 6, else `stop`. The first gate has `passes` = 3, so YOLO allows exactly one more round of 3 failures.
- `review_cap`: `another-pass`.
- `phase_blocked`: `leave`.
- `execution_failed`: `retry` while fewer than 2 earlier answered `execution_failed` gates exist for the same agent in the session, else `abandon`.
- `harness_failure`: `native`.
- `skill_approval`: the default disposition of each proposed skill.
- `permission`: `allow-once`. The code path is `ask_permission`, which opens the gate and answers it in the same call.

### Judge answers

The gates `open_questions`, `spec_approval`, `plan_approval`, and `stuck` use the `yolo-answer` judge. The engine then checks the answer in `yolo_answer_from_judge`:

- Open questions: the engine fills each question that the judge skipped with the label of the recommended option.
- Approvals: the answer `approved: true` needs a fact-check PASS on the current version. A rejection needs feedback text. A failed check gives the `Note` `The YOLO answer was refused: <reason>. The gate waits for you.`
- Stuck: the option `fact` without text becomes `block`, because the judge must never guess a fact that only the user has.

The YOLO prompt also describes rules for review caps, closing gates, and permissions. The engine does not send those gates to the judge. It uses the fixed answers above.

### Gates that YOLO never answers

`yolo_leaves_open` returns true for two cases:

- `budget_reached`. Spending more money is the decision of the user.
- `execution_failed` for an execution that the user stopped (Rule P4). The explanation says `Ostra leaves a stopped execution to you, YOLO included.`

A paused session starts nothing, and that includes YOLO answers (Rule P1). A YOLO answer also never breaks a guard: approval still needs a PASS, and BLOCKER findings still loop without a cap.

When YOLO is on, the runner sends no push notification for a gate, except for a `harness_failure` gate, because the user must sign in. The completion judge lists every YOLO decision in the section `Decided for you`.

## The budget gate

The budget limits the spend of one session. The setting is `limits.session_budget_usd` in the workspace settings. The default is 25.0 dollars. The value 0 means no limit. A negative or non-finite value is a validation error. The runner reads the setting on every planner pass, so a change applies to the next pass without a restart.

```rust
let limit = budget + self.s.budget_raised;
let spent = self.s.spent_usd();
if spent >= limit {
    if self.s.budget_gate.is_none() { /* open GatePayload::BudgetReached */ }
    return;
}
```

The guard sits in `Planner::push` in [`crates/ostra-engine/src/plan.rs`](crates/ostra-engine/src/plan.rs) and checks only `Step::Spawn`. Judge calls, commands, and gates still run. Executions that already run continue to the end. `SessionState::spent_usd` adds the cost of finished executions. A running execution counts when it ends. Judge cost does not count.

The gate payload holds `spent_usd` and `budget_usd`. The field `budget_usd` holds the current limit (`budget + budget_raised`). The answers are:

- `raise`: the extra amount is the number in `text` (a leading `$` is allowed). If the text is empty, not a number, not finite, or not above 0, the extra amount is `budget_usd` again, at least 1.0. The fold adds the extra amount plus any overshoot (`spent - limit`) to `budget_raised`. The new limit then equals the spend plus the extra amount.
- `stop` or any other option: the session fails with `Stopped at the session budget after spending $<amount>.`

Example: the budget is 25.00 and the spend is 26.10 when the gate opens. The answer `raise` with no text adds 25.00 plus 1.10. The new limit is 51.10, so the session can spend 25.00 more.

## What happens when

- **The user answers a gate twice.** The second call fails with `This gate was already answered.` If both calls pass the check at the same moment, the fold ignores the second `GateAnswered`.
- **A change revokes an approval gate.** An answer to a revoked spec or plan gate does not approve it. The planner opens a new gate for the new version.
- **The server restarts.** `Engine::recover` answers every open `permission` gate with `deny` (source `Engine`), because the run that asked is gone. Other gates stay open, and the answer applies after the restart.
- **The user stops the session.** `Engine::stop_session` appends `SessionFailed` and sends `deny` to waiting permission calls. Open gates stay in the log, and nobody can answer them in a useful way.
- **A run ends or the session pauses while a permission gate waits.** The engine answers the gate with `deny` (source `Engine`) because the run that asked ends.
- **YOLO is on and the judge fails.** The gate stays open with a `Note`. The user can answer it as usual.
- **YOLO is switched on while a gate is open.** The next planner pass emits `Step::YoloAnswer` for the gate. Permission gates get `allow-once` at once.

## The user's view

- Each open gate shows as a card on the session board, with the title and the explanation of the planner.
- The session status is `Waiting` when gates are open and no execution runs.
- Send an answer with `POST /api/gates/{id}/answer`.
- Switch YOLO with `POST /api/sessions/{id}/yolo` or set `yolo.default` in the workspace settings.
- Set the spend limit with `limits.session_budget_usd`.

## Limits

| Value | Number | Holder |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Consecutive fact-check failures before the gate | 3, plus 3 for each `another-round` | `FACTCHECK_RECURRING_LIMIT` in `state.rs` |
| YOLO stops the fact-check at | 6 failures | `passes < 6` in `yolo_plan` |
| Review passes before the gate | 3, plus 1 for each `another-pass` | `REVIEW_CAP` in `state.rs` |
| Review passes under YOLO | 10 | `YOLO_REVIEW_BUDGET` in `state.rs` |
| YOLO retries of a failed agent | 2 | `prior < 2` in `yolo_plan` |
| Session budget | 25.0 dollars, 0 for no limit | `limits.session_budget_usd` |

sections.title: Uploads, attached files, and context added during a session
sections.summary: Explains how uploads are staged and claimed, the limits and the file name rule, attached files, amendments with queue or now delivery, kept notes, and the session context file.
sections.body:
## Why context needs its own rules

A user often has files that the request alone cannot carry: a PDF specification, a log, or a design note. A new task uploads them before the session exists, so the engine has no session folder yet. A user also adds facts while the session runs, and agents already work on the old request. Without rules, files could overwrite each other, a hostile file name could escape the folder, and new text could reach only some agents.

This page covers five ways that user context reaches agents: attached files, uploads, amendments, kept notes, and the session context file. It stops at the console forms. The page "Gate forms, book reader, and HTML export" covers the forms. The page "Judges: what each one decides and how a call runs" explains the `route-answer` judge that decides what happens to added context.

| Kind | The user gives | Where the agent finds it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Attached file | A path inside a project or a visible workspace artifact | An absolute path in the request text |
| Upload | A file from the user computer | An absolute path in the session `uploads/` folder, listed in the request text |
| Amendment | Text, files, or uploads added while the session runs | The request text, after the judge delivers it |
| Kept note | Part of an answer that the judge keeps for a later stage | The `User notes` line of the spawn block |
| Session context file | Nothing. The engine writes it. | The `Context files` line of a revision spawn |

## Attached files and folders

An attached file is a `ContextFile` with a `project` key and a project-relative `path`. A folder path ends with `/`. The tag `@project/path` names the file in request text (`ContextFile::tag`). The user can attach files when the user creates a task and when the user adds context.

`validate_files` in [`crates/ostra-engine/src/runner.rs`](crates/ostra-engine/src/runner.rs) checks the list (Rule C1). The rules are:

- At most `MAX_CONTEXT_FILES` = 50 entries. The error is `Attach at most 50 files, because each one is read by every agent.`
- The `project` key must name a project of the session. The error is `Tag files from this session's projects only. <key> is not one of them.`
- The path must stay inside the project. The engine rejects empty, absolute, and non-normal components such as `..`. It also resolves the real path and checks that it starts with the project root. The error is `Tag a file or folder inside <project>. <path> is not one.`
- A path that ends with `/` must be a folder.
- The project key `_artifacts` (`artifacts::TAG_ROOT`) names a workspace artifact. The artifact must exist and be visible. A hidden artifact cannot be tagged (Rule W2). The error is `Tag a workspace artifact that exists and is not hidden. <path> is not one.`
- The engine normalizes the paths (forward slashes, no leading `./`, folders end with `/`) and drops duplicates.

The limit of 50 exists because every agent reads each file. A long list costs tokens in every execution.

The fold keeps the list in `SessionState.files`. The method `full_request()` in [`crates/ostra-engine/src/state.rs`](crates/ostra-engine/src/state.rs) appends the text `Files and folders the user attached to the request. Read each file and look through each folder before you start, because the user chose them as context:`. After that text, each entry has one line with the absolute path (forward slashes on every operating system), the word `folder` for a folder, and the tag.

## Uploads

An upload is a file that the user sends from the user computer. The engine keeps it in two steps, because a new task uploads before its session exists.

### Sequence of an upload

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Console as console
    participant Api as upload route
    participant Engine as Engine
    participant Uploads as uploads module
    participant State as SessionState
    Console->>Api: POST uploads with name and bytes
    Api->>Engine: stage_upload
    Engine->>Uploads: stage
    Uploads-->>Console: UploadRef with id name size
    Console->>Engine: create_session or amend with upload ids
    Engine->>Uploads: check and claim
    Uploads-->>Engine: UploadedFile list
    Engine->>State: SessionCreated or RequestAmended with uploads
```

### Stage

The route is `POST /api/workspaces/{ws}/uploads?name=<file name>` with the raw bytes as the body. The route allows a body of `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES + 1024` bytes. `uploads::stage` in [`crates/ostra-engine/src/uploads.rs`](crates/ostra-engine/src/uploads.rs) then does these steps:

1. Reject an empty body with `The file is empty.`
2. Reject a body above `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` = 25 MiB with `Upload files of at most 25 MB, because every agent reads them.`
3. Make a random ID: the 32 hex characters of a UUID.
4. Make the file name safe with `safe_name`.
5. Write the file to `<staging>/<id>/<name>`. The staging folder is `uploads` inside the workspace runtime folder (`paths::upload_staging`). The first write also creates a `.gitignore` with the content `*` in the staging folder.
6. Return an `UploadRef` with `id`, `name`, and `size`.

### The file name rule

`safe_name` makes a name that is safe to write in one folder. The reason is that the name comes from the user and a path such as `../../etc/passwd` must never leave the folder. The rule has these steps:

1. Keep only the last segment. The function splits on `/` and `\\`.
2. Remove control characters.
3. Replace each of `: * ? " < > |` with `_`.
4. Trim spaces and remove leading dots, so that the file is never hidden.
5. Cut the result to 120 characters.
6. If nothing remains, use `upload`.

The unit tests show the results: `../../etc/passwd` becomes `passwd`, `C:\\Users\\me\\notes.txt` becomes `notes.txt`, `.env` becomes `env`, and `a:b?.pdf` becomes `a_b_.pdf`.

### Check and claim

`Engine::create_session` and `Engine::amend` call `uploads::check` before they change anything, and `uploads::claim` after that. The check has two rules:

- At most `MAX_UPLOADS` = 20 IDs for one request or one addition. The error is `Upload at most 20 files at a time.`
- Each ID must be 32 hex characters and must name a staged file. The error is `An upload is missing. Upload the file again, then send.` An ID such as `../x` fails here, so an ID cannot select another folder.

`claim` moves each file into `<session root>/uploads/` (`paths::session_uploads`). It renames the file and copies it when the rename fails. Then it deletes the staging folder of the ID. If the name exists in the target, the file gets a number: `spec.pdf`, then `spec (2).pdf`, then `spec (3).pdf`. No upload overwrites another upload. A claimed ID cannot be claimed again, because its staging folder is gone.

The result is a list of `UploadedFile` with `name`, `path`, and `size`. The runner stores it in `SessionCreated.uploads` or `RequestAmended.uploads`. The fold method `full_request()` appends `Files the user uploaded with the request. Read each one before you start, because the user chose them as context:` and one line with the absolute path of the session copy for each file.

### What happens when

- **The user uploads a file and never sends the task.** The file stays in the staging folder. `uploads.rs` has no step that deletes an unclaimed upload.
- **Two uploads have the same name.** Each gets its own staging ID. At the claim, the second file gets the name `<stem> (2).<ext>`.
- **A name has no extension.** The number goes after the whole name, for example `notes (2)`.
- **The session ends.** The uploads stay in the session folder with the other session files.

## Amendments: context added while the session runs

An amendment is text, files, or uploads that the user adds to a running session. `Engine::amend` (route `POST /api/sessions/{id}/amend` with `text`, `files`, `uploads`, and `delivery`) rejects an empty addition with `Say what to add or change, tag a file with @, or upload one.` It rejects an ended session with `This session has ended. Start a new task instead.` Then it validates the files, claims the uploads, and appends `RequestAmended`.

### Queue and now delivery

`ContextDelivery` has two values. The default is `queue`.

| Delivery | What happens to running executions | When the context reaches agents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `queue` | They finish on the old request. | The next step that starts sees the new context. |
| `now` | The engine interrupts all of them with `Interrupt::Context`. They end with the status `Interrupted` and the message `Interrupted to deliver the context the user added.` | They run again from their spawn block with the new context. |

The fold clears `resume_from` on every amendment. The reason is that a resumed conversation would not see the new context, so the engine runs a new execution instead. An interrupted work loop becomes `Work` with kind `Rerun`.

### Flow of one amendment

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[RequestAmended appended] --> B{Classified and category is RESEARCH SPEC PLAN or IMPLEMENT}
    B -- no --> C[Delivered at once]
    B -- yes --> D[Pending until the judge decides]
    D --> E[Planner emits route-answer judge and starts nothing else]
    E --> F{Disposition}
    F -- deliver --> G[Joins the request]
    F -- remember --> H[Becomes a note for later stages]
    F -- discard --> I[Reaches no agent]
    G --> J[Research task for the added part]
    J --> K{Spec exists}
    K -- yes --> L[Requirement change and spec update]
    K -- no --> M[Next steps use the new request]
```

`SessionState::routes_amendments` is true when the session has a classify decision and the category is `RESEARCH`, `SPEC`, `PLAN`, or `IMPLEMENT`. Then `RequestAmended.routed` is true and the amendment is `pending`. The planner emits a `route-answer` judge with the subject `amendment:{i}` and returns before it starts any other step (Rule C2). The reason is that a spawn that starts before the decision could use the wrong request.

Before classification, the `classify` judge reads the amendment with the request, because `full_request()` already includes it. For `VERIFY`, `TEST`, `DOCS`, `PROMPT`, `QUICK_CHANGE`, and `QUICK_ANSWER`, nothing is routed. The amendment joins the request at once.

The judge gives one item with the ID `answer`:

- `deliver`: the amendment joins the request that `full_request()` builds. The fold adds a research task for the added part (origin `Amendment`), plus up to 3 tasks that the judge asked for. If a spec exists, the fold also records a requirement change, so the spec is generated, checked, and approved again (Rule D2). The judge route `implementation_detail` skips the spec change.
- `remember`: the text becomes a note for the named stages. It does not join the request.
- `discard`: the text reaches no agent. Interrupted work runs again without it.

When the amendment is not routed, the fold applies the same research and spec rules at once.

## What each agent reads

| Agent input | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `full_request()` | The request, the attached files, the uploads, and every delivered amendment, each as `Added later by the user: <text>`. |
| `added_context()` | A short list of delivered amendments. The planner appends it to the text of each research task, because the classify judge wrote that text without the new context. |
| Phase file | A planned phase with a phase file gets no `task` input. The agent reads the phase file, which the plan agent wrote from the spec. |
| `User notes` | Kept notes for the stage of the agent. |
| `Context files` | The session context file, for a revision phase. |

The classify judge must write the absolute paths of attached files and uploads into the research tasks that need them. The reason is that a research agent reads only its task and never sees the lists of the request. The prompt tells the judge to name a file in every task when it cannot tell which task needs the file.

## Kept notes

A kept note is the part of an answer or an amendment that the judge keeps for later stages. The fold stores it as a `UserNote` with an ID such as `N1`, the stages, the text, and the gate. `SessionState::notes_for(stage)` returns the notes that are not forgotten. The planner puts them in the `user_notes` input of the spawn. The spawn block shows them under `User notes`.

| Stage | Agents that get the notes |
| --- | --- |
| `implement` | `implementer` |
| `tests` | `write-test` and `execution-path-analyzer` |
| `docs` | `documentation` and `system-architecture` |

A note never changes a requirement. If an answer changes what the system must do, the judge must deliver it so that the spec records it.

## The session context file

The session context file is a Markdown index of the session. The path is `ostra-session-context.md` in the session root (`paths::report::session_context`). `context::render` in [`crates/ostra-engine/src/context.rs`](crates/ostra-engine/src/context.rs) builds it from the folded state.

The problem is that a revision after a feedback round needs the whole history, but a conversation grows with each round. A file that the engine rewrites from the log stays small. Thus a session can take any number of feedback rounds (Rule F2). The file holds paths and short summaries only. The first paragraph tells the agent to read the listed files when it needs detail.

The file has these sections, in this order:

1. `Request`: the output of `full_request()`.
2. `Route`: category, track, and projects in scope.
3. `Research documents`: one path for each finished research task, including superseded ones.
4. `Spec`: path, summary, and whether it is approved.
5. `Plan`: path of the master plan and its summary.
6. `Phases`: for each phase, the status (`passed review`, `blocked: <reason>`, `not started`, or `in progress`), the implementer report path, and the review ledger path when a review ran.
7. `Feedback rounds`: the text of each round, a line for a requirement change that waits for the spec, and the phases that built the round.

The runner rewrites the file in two cases. It writes it before it appends an `implementation_review` gate (`Step::OpenGate`). It also writes it in `perform_spawn` before any spawn whose `context_files` input contains the path. The planner sets that input for each revision phase, together with the paths of earlier reports of the same project. The gate payload also carries `context_path`, so the user can open the file.

If the write fails, the step fails with `Could not write <path>: <error>`. The drive loop then appends a `Note` and plans again.

## What happens when

- **The user adds context to an ended session.** `amend` fails. Start a new task.
- **The user adds context to a paused session.** The amendment is stored. The planner starts the judge call only after the resume, because a paused session starts nothing (Rule P1).
- **The server restarts with a pending amendment.** The log holds `pending` state. After `recover`, the planner emits the judge call again.
- **A `now` amendment arrives while a harness run waits for a message.** The engine interrupts the run like any running execution. It runs again from its spawn block.
- **The judge call for an amendment fails.** The session fails, because the `route-answer` judge has no fallback. See the page about judges.
- **The user attaches a file that another agent changes.** The agents read the current file. The engine does not snapshot attached files.

## The user's view

- Attach files with the `@` tag in the task form or in the add-context form.
- Upload with the file control. The console sends each file to `POST /api/workspaces/{ws}/uploads` and keeps the returned ID.
- Choose `queue` or `now` when you add context.
- The session detail lists the uploads and the additions (`view::detail`).

## Limits

| Value | Number | Holder |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Size of one upload | 25 MiB | `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` in `uploads.rs` |
| Uploads in one request or addition | 20 | `MAX_UPLOADS` in `uploads.rs` |
| Attached files in one request or addition | 50 | `MAX_CONTEXT_FILES` in `runner.rs` |
| Length of a stored file name | 120 characters | `safe_name` in `uploads.rs` |
| Upload ID | 32 hex characters | `valid_id` in `uploads.rs` |
| Research tasks from one judged answer | 3 | `MAX_ANSWER_RESEARCH` in `judge.rs` |
