sections.title: The implement, review, autofix, and rescue loop
sections.summary: How one phase moves through work, review, autofix, fix passes, rescue, and staging, and how the review cap, BLOCKER findings, blocked phases, and YOLO change that path.
sections.body:
## Why each phase has a work loop

An agent that changes code can leave defects, fail on a fact that it does not know, or write dangerous code. One pass has no check. An unlimited repeat has no end. The work loop gives each phase a fixed cycle of work, review, and repair. Each loop ends in `Done` or `Blocked`.

This page covers the loop states, phase scheduling, the kinds of work, the review pass, autofix, the review cap, BLOCKER findings, STUCK and HANDOFF, blocked phases, YOLO answers, and staging. The test loop uses the same code, so each rule here also holds for tests. The page "Closing gate, tests, documentation, and the completion report" covers the stages after the loops. The page "Agent coordination: ask, reply, and pair loops" covers conversations between agents.

## How the fold and the planner share the loop

Each phase is a `PhaseRun` in `SessionState.phases`. A `PhaseRun` holds two `WorkLoop` values: `impl_loop` for the code and `test_loop` for the tests. The field `WorkLoop.next` holds a `LoopNext` value, which is the state of the loop. Two functions use it:

- `SessionState::loop_finished` reads a finished execution and sets `next`.
- `Planner::loop_steps` reads `next` and returns the step that moves the loop on.

The planner returns no step for a loop when `WorkLoop.running` or `WorkLoop.gate` is set. One execution or one open gate owns a loop at a time. Two steps for one loop would start two agents on the same files.

The field `WorkLoop.in_flight` stores the `next` value that was active when an execution started. If the engine interrupts the execution, `loop_finished` restores that value. Then the same step runs again. A `Work` step restarts with the kind `Rerun`. The page "Failure, restart, stop, pause, and concurrency" explains interrupts. The page "The planner, steps, and the drive loop" explains how the runner performs steps.

### The LoopNext states

| State | Meaning | Step that `loop_steps` returns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Idle` | The phase has not started. | None. `Planner::phases` starts it with `Work` of kind `Initial`. |
| `Work` | An agent must change files. The state holds a `WorkKind` and optional instructions. | `Step::Spawn` of the work agent. |
| `Review` | A review pass is due. | `Step::Spawn` of `code-reviewer`. |
| `Autofix` | Findings have an exact Fix text. | `Step::Autofix`. |
| `Rescue` | An execution reported STUCK. | `Step::Judge` with `JudgeKind::Rescue`. |
| `RescueExplore` | A research task looks for the missing fact. | None. The result of the task moves the loop. |
| `RescueGate` | The Rescue judge chose to ask the user. | `Stuck` gate. |
| `AwaitRoute` | A gate answer with text waits for the Route answer judge. | `Step::Judge` with `JudgeKind::RouteAnswer`. |
| `AnswerResearch` | Research that an answer queued is running. | None. The last finished task moves the loop. |
| `Handoff` | An agent asked for a specialist. | `Step::Spawn` of `prompt-generation`. |
| `CapReached` | The review cap is reached and YOLO is off. | `ReviewCap` gate. If YOLO is on, `Step::Judge` with `JudgeKind::ResolveReview`. |
| `Resolve` | The review cap is reached and YOLO is on. | `Step::Judge` with `JudgeKind::ResolveReview`. |
| `Stage` | Reviewed files wait for `git add`. | `Step::Command` with `CommandPurpose::Stage`. |
| `Failed` | An execution failed after its automatic retry. | `ExecutionFailed` gate, or `HarnessFailure` gate. |
| `Done` | The loop passed. | None. |
| `Blocked` | The loop stopped. | `Step::AnnounceBlocked`, then maybe a `PhaseBlocked` gate. |

### State changes of one work loop

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Idle
    Idle --> Work : phase starts
    Work --> Review : submit Ok and review on
    Work --> Stage : submit Ok and review off
    Work --> Done : submit Ok and nothing to stage
    Work --> Rescue : submit STUCK
    Work --> Handoff : submit HANDOFF
    Work --> Failed : no usable result
    Handoff --> Work : specialist finished
    Rescue --> Work : rerun or explore result
    Rescue --> RescueGate : judge asks the user
    RescueGate --> Work : user gives a fact
    RescueGate --> Blocked : user answers block
    Review --> Work : BLOCKER or fix pass
    Review --> Autofix : findings with exact Fix text
    Review --> Stage : no HIGH or MEDIUM left
    Review --> CapReached : cap reached
    Review --> Resolve : cap reached under YOLO
    Autofix --> Work : findings remain
    Autofix --> Stage : nothing remains
    CapReached --> Work : another-pass
    CapReached --> Blocked : stop
    Resolve --> Work : fix
    Resolve --> Blocked : block
    Failed --> Work : retry
    Failed --> Blocked : abandon
    Blocked --> Work : retry
    Stage --> Done : git add ran
    Done --> [*]
```

## Schedule phases

`Planner::phases` runs on each planner pass. It does these steps in order:

1. Call `removed_phases` to find idle phases that depend, directly or through other phases, on a blocked phase (Rule D9).
2. Build the set `busy`: each project that has a loop that is not idle and not terminal.
3. For each idle phase that is not removed, start the loop only if its project is not in `busy` and `deps_passed` is true. The loop starts with `Work` of kind `Initial`.
4. For each other phase, call `loop_steps`.

Rule M2 allows one implement loop in a project at a time. Phases of different projects run at the same time. `deps_passed` is true when the `impl_loop` of every phase in `depends_on` is `Done`. If `depends_on` is unreadable, the phase depends on every phase with a lower id (Rule M5). A blocked dependency is not `Done`, so its dependents wait, and `removed_phases` takes them out of the queue.

A phase without a plan file is an inline phase. `inline_phase` makes it, and its `depends_on` is the previous inline phase. Thus the inline phases of a request with many projects run one after the other.

The source of a loop sets its agents and its review mode:

| Source | Work agent | Fix agent | `ReviewMode` | Stage |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Phases of an approved plan, and inline phases of an IMPLEMENT session | `implementer` | `implementer` | `Always` | Yes |
| QUICK_CHANGE request | `implementer` | `implementer` | `Never` | Yes, only if files changed |
| VERIFY request | `implementer` with purpose `Verify` | `implementer` | `Never` | No |
| PROMPT request | `prompt-generation` | `implementer` | `IfCodeChanged` | Yes, only after a review |
| `test_loop` of every phase | `write-test` | `write-test` | `Always` | Yes |
| TEST or DOCS request | The inline phase starts as `Done`. | None | None | None |

`IfCodeChanged` runs a review only when a changed file is not an instruction file. An instruction file ends in `.md`, `.mdx`, or `.txt`, or ends in `.toml` and has `agent` in its path.

## Kinds of work

A `Work` state carries a `WorkKind`. The kind sets the instructions, the agent, and whether the new execution continues an earlier conversation.

| `WorkKind` | When it starts | What the instructions hold |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Initial` | The first pass of a loop. | None. The spawn block holds the phase file, or the request for an inline phase. |
| `Fix` | A review left HIGH or MEDIUM findings. | `fix_instructions`: each finding line verbatim, and an order to record FIXED or WONTFIX in the review ledger. |
| `BlockerFix` | A review found a BLOCKER. | `blocker_instructions`: only the BLOCKER findings, and an order to remove the dangerous code. |
| `Resume` | A HANDOFF specialist finished. | The request of the specialist and the resume instructions of the agent. |
| `Rescue` | A STUCK execution has a fact now. | `rescue_context`: the diagnostic verbatim, the need, and the fact. |
| `Rerun` | The engine interrupted the execution, or the user chose `retry`. | The earlier instructions. |

`loop_work` picks the agent. `Initial` uses `work_agent`. `Rerun` and `Resume` use `work_agent` when `work_count` is 1 or less. Each other case uses `fix_agent`. `work_count` counts the work executions that are not resumed. The spawn input `ledger_file` is set only for `Fix` and `BlockerFix`. A `Fix`, `BlockerFix`, `Rescue`, or `Resume` pass continues the conversation of the previous work execution when the rules of the page "Agent coordination: ask, reply, and pair loops" allow it.

## The review pass

The planner spawns `code-reviewer` with the purpose `ExecPurpose::Review`. The field `iteration` is `iterations + 1`. The spawn input `phase_value` is `N` for code and `N-tests` for tests. The input `changed_files` lists each file that the work passes reported. The input `rationale` is the instructions of the last work pass that was not `Initial`. If none exist, it is the phase title, or the request for an inline phase. The input `ledger_file` names the review ledger `ostra-review-ledger-phase-N.md`. The reviewer reads the ledger on each pass to see what the fix agent recorded.

At spawn time, the runner reads the review rules of `project.toml`, takes the ids marked `auto_fixable`, and stores them in the execution params under `AUTO_FIXABLE_PARAM`. This keeps the fold a pure function of the event log, because the fold must not read `project.toml` from disk.

When the reviewer ends, `loop_finished` runs these steps:

1. If the status is not `Ok`, `Stuck`, or `Handoff`, use the failure path. See "Failed executions in a loop" below.
2. If the submit is not readable, set `Failed`.
3. Reset `error_retries`, add 1 to `iterations`, and store the review as `last_review`.
4. If `security_block` is true or a finding has severity BLOCKER, set `blocker_open` and `Work` of kind `BlockerFix`. Stop here.
5. Clear `blocker_open`. Split the findings by class, as the next table shows.
6. If any finding is auto-fixable, set `Autofix`. Otherwise call `after_findings`.

| Class | Members | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BLOCKER | Severity BLOCKER, or `security_block` is true. | `BlockerFix` with no cap. |
| Auto-fixable | Severity is not BLOCKER, the rule does not start with `SEC-BLOCK` or `PHASE-REQ`, and the rule id is in `auto_fixable_ids`. | `Autofix` step, with no model call. |
| Open | Severity HIGH or MEDIUM, and not auto-fixable. | Becomes `remaining` for `after_findings`. |
| Leftover | Severity LOW, and not auto-fixable. | Stored in `leftover_low`. No agent fixes them. |

`after_findings` takes `remaining` and applies these rules in order:

1. If `remaining` is empty, set `Stage` when `stage` is true. Otherwise set `Done`.
2. If `iterations` is at or above `effective_cap`, use the cap rules below.
3. Otherwise set `Work` of kind `Fix` with `fix_instructions`.

Thus a review with only LOW findings ends the loop. The conformance test `only_low_findings_exit_the_loop` checks this. The submit tool also checks the reviewer. `validate_submit` refuses a `CodeReviewerSubmit` when `security_block` is not true exactly when a BLOCKER finding exists. The model must correct the payload before the run can end.

## Autofix without a model call

Autofix applies a review finding from its exact Fix text. It costs no model call, and it gives the same result on each run. The planner returns `Step::Autofix` with the findings of `LoopNext::Autofix`. The runner then does these steps:

1. Call `autofix::apply_findings` on a blocking thread.
2. Parse each `fix` text with `parse_fix`. Only two forms are valid: ``Change `old` to `new` on line N.`` and ``Add `text` above line N: `anchor`.`` An optional `Fix:` prefix is removed. Double backticks delimit a span that contains a backtick.
3. Group the fixes by file. Sort the fixes of one file by line number, highest first. A fix near the end of the file then cannot move the lines of an earlier fix.
4. Call `apply_fix` for each fix, and write the file.
5. Append `AutofixApplied` with the lists `applied` and `failed`.

`apply_fix` looks for the needle on line N. If it is not there, it checks the lines N-1, N+1, N-2, and N+2 in this order. Earlier fixes in the same file can move lines, and this search covers a shift of two lines. A `Change` fix needs a non-empty `old` text that occurs exactly once on the chosen line. An `Add` fix inserts the text above the anchor line with the indentation of the anchor, unless the text starts with white space. The function keeps the final newline of the file.

The fold handles `AutofixApplied` in this way. Each failed finding of severity HIGH or MEDIUM returns to `remaining`. A failed LOW finding is dropped. Then `after_findings` runs. If nothing remains, the loop goes to `Stage` and no new review runs. Autofix does not change `iterations`.

| Cause | Text in `failed` |
| --- | --- |
| The Fix text has neither form | `the Fix text is not in an auto-fixable form` |
| The path leaves the project folder | `the file is outside the project` |
| The file cannot be read | `{file} could not be read` |
| The old text is empty | `the old text is empty` |
| The old text is absent near line N | `` `old` is not on or near line N `` |
| The old text occurs twice on the line | `` `old` appears more than once on line N `` |
| The anchor is absent near line N | `the anchor is not on or near line N` |

A write failure is recorded under the file name and not under a finding line. The fold matches `failed` entries to findings by line text, so it does not return those findings to the fix agent. Keep this in mind when you change the write step.

## The review cap

The cap stops a loop that does not converge. `effective_cap(yolo)` is `REVIEW_CAP` (3) or, when YOLO is on, `YOLO_REVIEW_BUDGET` (10), plus `extra_cap`. The check runs in `after_findings`, with the value of `yolo` at the time the review result folds.

When YOLO is off, the loop goes to `CapReached`. The planner opens the `ReviewCap` gate titled "Review of phase N reached its cap". The gate shows the open findings and the ledger path. These answers are valid:

- `another-pass` adds 1 to `extra_cap` and sets `Work` of kind `Fix`. If the answer has text, the text first goes to the Route answer judge.
- Any other answer sets `Blocked` with the reason `The review loop reached its cap with N findings open.` and the ledger path. The fold marks the gate as answered, so no second `PhaseBlocked` gate opens.

For example, passes 1 and 2 find HIGH and MEDIUM findings, and each is fixed. Pass 3 finds a HIGH finding. `iterations` is 3, so the gate opens. After `another-pass`, the cap is 4. One fix runs, then review pass 4. If findings remain, the gate opens again.

When YOLO is on, no user answers. The loop goes to `Resolve`, and the planner calls the `ResolveReview` judge with the subject `phase:N` or `phase:N:tests`. The judge returns `fix` or `block`:

- `fix` adds 1 to `resolve_rounds`, stores the open count in `open_before_resolve`, and adds 1 to `extra_cap`. The loop sets `Work` of kind `Fix` with one instruction for each finding. If the judge gives no instruction, the loop uses `fix_instructions`. The added cap gives one verification review for each round.
- `block` sets `Blocked` with the reason of the judge.

Resolution repeats only when it converges. At the next cap, the loop calls the judge again only if `resolve_rounds` is 0 or `remaining` is smaller than `open_before_resolve`. If not, the loop sets `Blocked` with the reason `The review loop stopped converging after N resolution rounds`. The page "Judges: what each one decides and how a call runs" describes the judge call.

## BLOCKER findings

A BLOCKER finding marks code that is unsafe to keep. Rule Hard 21 sets four consequences:

- The BLOCKER findings go alone to the fix agent as `BlockerFix`. The instruction tells the agent to remove the dangerous code and not to rewrite it. The reason in the instruction text is that a secure rewrite is a separate request that the user makes after the user understands the risk.
- No cap applies. The BlockerFix path returns before `after_findings`. A review that finds a BLOCKER again starts another `BlockerFix`, with no limit.
- The runner appends `SecurityBlock` with the BLOCKER findings after the review ends. The fold ignores this event. The console and push notices use it.
- While `blocker_open` is true in the `impl_loop` or `test_loop` of a passed phase, the documentation stage skips that project. The next review without a BLOCKER clears the flag.

A phase that ends `Blocked` is not a passed phase. If it is the only phase of a project, the project gets no format step, no tests, and no documentation. The conformance test `hard21_open_blocker_blocks_docs` checks that no documentation starts after a BLOCKER and an abandoned fix.

## STUCK, HANDOFF, and rescue

A work agent ends with status `stuck` when it hits a failure that it cannot solve. It must give `StuckInfo` with the exact `diagnostic` and the `need`. If it gives none, the fold uses the final text and the need `The agent reported STUCK without a diagnostic.` The loop sets `Rescue`. The loop never makes a plain retry, because the same approach would fail again. The test `stuck_goes_to_rescue_never_a_plain_retry` checks this.

The planner calls the `Rescue` judge with the id of the stuck execution as subject. The judge returns an `action`:

- `explore` queues a research task with the origin `Rescue`, and the loop waits in `RescueExplore`. This task does not hold the rest of the session. When it ends with `Ok`, the loop sets `Work` of kind `Rescue` with the findings summary and the research path.
- `rerun` sets `Work` of kind `Rescue` with the fact of the judge, or its reason if it gives no fact.
- `gate` sets `RescueGate`. The planner opens the `Stuck` gate titled "Phase N is stuck". The answer `fact` with text sends the text to the Route answer judge, and a delivered fact starts `Work` of kind `Rescue`. The answer `block`, or a `fact` answer with no text, sets `Blocked` with the reason `Stuck: {need}`.

The text of `rescue_context` names the failed attempt, the need, and the new fact. It ends with the order `Do not repeat the approach that failed.`

A work agent ends with status `handoff` when it needs a specialist. It must give `HandoffInfo`. Without it, the loop fails with `The agent reported HANDOFF without saying what it needs.` With it, the loop sets `Handoff`. The planner spawns `prompt-generation` with the purpose `PromptGen` and the field `handoff_for`. The `request` is the task, and `target_files` lists the files. If the list is empty, the input says `Determine them from the task.` When the specialist ends with `Ok`, the loop sets `Work` of kind `Resume`. Any other status sets `Failed`.

## Blocked phases

A loop becomes `Blocked` in these cases:

- The user answers a `ReviewCap` gate with `stop`, or answers a `Stuck` gate with `block`.
- The user abandons a failed execution. The reason is `{agent} failed and the user abandoned it.`
- The `ResolveReview` judge answers `block`, or YOLO resolution stops converging.
- The user changes a requirement in an answer, and a spec exists. The loop stops, and the spec restarts (Rule D10).

The planner handles `Blocked` in two steps. First, if `announced_block` is false, it returns `Step::AnnounceBlocked`. The runner appends `PhaseBlocked`, and the fold sets `announced_block`. Second, if YOLO is off, `block_gate_answered` is false, and no gate is open, the planner opens the `PhaseBlocked` gate titled "Phase N is blocked". The answer `leave` keeps the loop blocked. The answer `retry` does these steps:

1. Set `extra_cap` to `iterations`. The effective cap becomes `REVIEW_CAP` plus `iterations`, so the loop gets 3 more review passes.
2. Reset `announced_block`, `block_gate_answered`, `resolve_rounds`, and `open_before_resolve`.
3. Set `Work` of kind `Fix` with the open findings of the last review. If the answer has text, the Route answer judge sees it first.

A blocked loop is terminal, so the session goes on. `removed_phases` removes the idle phases that depend on it, and independent phases continue. The `ImplementationReview` gate lists each blocked reason. The reason for Rule D9 is that one failed phase must not stop work that does not need it.

## Failed executions in a loop

The fold treats `Ok`, `Stuck`, and `Handoff` as usable results. A status `Interrupted` restores `in_flight`. Each other status is a hard failure. If the status is `Error`, `error_retries` is below `ERROR_RETRIES` (1), and the error text does not start with `harness-`, the loop retries the same step one time. In all other cases the loop sets `Failed`. Then the planner opens a gate:

- An error that starts with `harness-` opens `HarnessFailure`. The answer `native` adds the agent to `native_fallback` and retries. The answer `retry` retries.
- Any other error opens `ExecutionFailed`. The answer `retry` resets `error_retries` and starts a review again for a review execution, or `Work` of kind `Rerun` for a work execution. The answer `abandon` sets `Blocked`.
- If the user stopped the execution, the title is "You stopped {agent}". The engine leaves this gate to the user, also under YOLO (Rule P4).

The page "Failure, restart, stop, pause, and concurrency" has the full failure matrix.

## Stage reviewed files

The `Stage` step runs `git add -A -- <files>` for the files that the loop changed. The runner first removes planted git directories with `repair_git_dirs`, adds the automatic git overrides, and runs the command with a 60-second timeout. The fold sets `staged` to true only if the exit code is 0. In both cases the loop becomes `Done`. A failed `git add` does not block the phase.

Staging keeps each review focused on the unstaged diff. Without it, the review of phase 2 would see the changes of phase 1 again. A QUICK_CHANGE loop with no changed files skips staging.

## YOLO answers for loop gates

Under YOLO, `Planner::flows` returns `Step::YoloAnswer` for each open gate, except `Permission` gates and the gates that `yolo_leaves_open` names. The page "Gates: the 14 kinds, their answers, and YOLO" lists all answers. These are the answers for loop gates:

| Gate | YOLO answer |
| --- | --- |
| `ReviewCap` | `another-pass`. This applies when the user turns YOLO on while the gate is open. |
| `PhaseBlocked` | `leave`. The planner does not open this gate under YOLO. |
| `Stuck` | The YOLO judge picks `fact` or `block`. It must not guess a fact that only the user has. |
| `ExecutionFailed` | `retry`, until two earlier answered gates exist for the same agent. Then `abandon`. The engine leaves a stopped execution open. |
| `HarnessFailure` | `native` |

## Limits

| Value | Number | Holder |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Review passes before the cap gate | 3 | `REVIEW_CAP` in `state.rs` |
| Review passes under YOLO | 10 | `YOLO_REVIEW_BUDGET` in `state.rs` |
| Passes that one `another-pass` adds | 1 | `WorkLoop.extra_cap` |
| Automatic retries of an `Error` execution | 1 | `ERROR_RETRIES` in `state.rs` |
| Timeout of `implementer` and `write-test` | 2400 seconds | `timeout_seconds` in `agent.toml` |
| Timeout of `code-reviewer` | 1200 seconds | `timeout_seconds` in `agent.toml` |
| Timeout of `prompt-generation` | 1800 seconds | `timeout_seconds` in `agent.toml` |
| Timeout of `git add` for staging | 60 seconds | literal in `perform_command` |
| Output tail that the engine keeps | 4000 bytes | literal in `run_command` |

All values are constants. A settings change does not change them. The user cannot change the cap, except through the `another-pass` answer.

## What happens when

- **The server restarts during a pass.** The fold marks the execution `Interrupted`. `loop_finished` restores `in_flight`, and the loop runs the same step again, as `Rerun` for work.
- **The user pauses the session.** The planner returns no step. After the user resumes, a paused execution continues under its own id.
- **The user adds text to an `another-pass`, `fact`, or `retry` answer.** `answer_needs_route` is true, so the loop waits in `AwaitRoute`. If the judge delivers the text, the next work pass gets it. If the judge discards it, the loop uses its fallback state.
- **The user turns YOLO on in the middle of a loop.** The next review result uses the cap 10. Open gates get YOLO answers.
- **A reviewer finds a BLOCKER and a HIGH finding together.** Only the BLOCKER goes to the fix agent. The next review finds the HIGH finding again if it remains.
- **An implementer creates a project with `ProjectCreate`.** The fold interrupts that execution. The loop restarts with `Initial` after the new project finishes its init.
- **Two phases belong to different projects.** They run at the same time, within the execution slot limit of the workspace.

sections.title: Closing gate, tests, documentation, and the completion report
sections.summary: How a session moves from accepted code to its final report: the format command, the batched closing gate, the test stage, the documentation stage, the architecture stage, the book write, and the completion judge.
sections.body:
## What must happen after the last phase passes

After the code is built and reviewed, a session still has work to do. It formats the code, offers tests and documentation, writes the documentation book, and reports what happened. Without a fixed order, these stages could start before the user accepts the code, run twice, or leave a session that never ends. The planner holds this order in `Planner::closing_stages`, `Planner::book_stage`, and `Planner::completion`.

This page covers the implementation review gate, the format command, the closing gate, the test stage, the documentation stage, the architecture stage, the book write, the init of created projects, and the completion report. The loops that come before these stages are on the page "The implement, review, autofix, and rescue loop". The book file format is on the page "Book model, submit rules, merge, and files on disk".

### Stage order for one project

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["All phases of the project are terminal"] --> B["ImplementationReview gate: done"]
    B --> C["Format command, once"]
    C --> D{"Tests and docs both requested?"}
    D -- yes --> F["closing = tests and docs"]
    D -- no --> E["ClosingGate asks the missing choices"]
    E --> F
    F --> G{"Tests chosen?"}
    G -- yes --> H["EPA per covered phase, then write-test per phase"]
    G -- no --> I{"Docs chosen and no BLOCKER open?"}
    H --> I
    I -- yes --> J["documentation agent for the project"]
    J --> K["system-architecture for 2 or more parts, then WriteBook"]
    I -- no --> M["Completion judge"]
    K --> M
```

The stage order in the diagram holds for the IMPLEMENT category. Two categories skip the first steps. A TEST request and a DOCS request start with an inline phase that is already `Done`, and `closing` is preset to `(true, false)` for TEST and `(false, true)` for DOCS. The format result is preset to "no command". Thus they have no implementation review gate, no format command, and no closing gate. The categories VERIFY, PROMPT, and QUICK_CHANGE have no closing stages. They go to completion when each loop is terminal and nothing runs.

## Implementation review gate

The `ImplementationReview` gate is the entry condition for the closing stages (Rule F1). The planner opens it in `Planner::implementation_review` when each phase is `Done` or removed and nothing runs. Before it opens the gate, it calls the Feedback judge for each feedback round that has no route. The runner writes the session context file `ostra-session-context.md` before it appends the gate, so a revision phase reads a file and not a long conversation.

The answer `done` sets `feedback.accepted`, and the closing stages start. The answer `feedback` with text adds a feedback round. The Feedback judge routes it, and the fold adds revision phases (`add_revision_phases`) that run through the work loop again. Under YOLO the engine answers `done`, because only the user can say what to change. The gate text says that accepting moves on to formatting, tests, documentation, and the completion report.

## Format command

`closing_stages` returns `Step::Command` with `CommandPurpose::Format` once for each project that has a passed phase and no format result (Rule D8). This step has no gate. The command comes from `[commands].format` in `project.toml`. The runner reads it on each planner pass in `plan_ctx`.

The runner records the result with `CommandRan`. The fold stores it in `ProjectTrack.format`. These cases exist:

| Case | Recorded result |
| --- | --- |
| No format command | Exit code `None`, and the text `No format command in project.toml, so format was skipped.` |
| The user did not approve the command | Exit code `None`, and the text `FORMAT_NOT_APPROVED`. The command does not run. |
| The command runs | The exit code of the command. The runner uses `bash -c` under the sandbox, with a 600-second timeout. |

Each case sets `format` to `Some(...)`, so the planner asks for the format step one time only. A non-zero exit code does not stop the session. The reason for the approval check (Rule A1) is that `project.toml` can arrive with a repository, and a program that it names must not start before the user approves exactly that content. The page "Trust approvals and registry-only settings" explains the approval.

## The closing gate

The closing gate asks the user whether to write tests and documentation. Both are optional, and neither changes the requirements (Rule T5). The gate has the title "Tests and documentation" and the payload `GatePayload::ClosingGate`.

The planner decides in `closing_stages` for each project after its format step:

1. If `ProjectTrack.closing` is set, use it.
2. Compute `ask_tests` as `!tests_requested()` and `ask_docs` as `!docs_requested()`. `tests_requested` is true when the task form set `options.tests` or the Classify judge set `opts_in.tests`. `docs_requested` works in the same way.
3. If both are false, no gate is needed, and `closing` is `(true, true)`. An explicit request replaces the gate (Rule T3).
4. Otherwise, add a `ClosingItem` with `project`, the number of passed phases, `ask_tests`, and `ask_docs` to the batch. A project with an open closing gate is not added again.
5. After the loop, if the batch is not empty, open one gate for all items. Projects that reach this point in the same pass share one gate (Rule T6).

The answer is `GateAnswer::Closing` with one `ClosingChoice` of `project`, `tests`, and `docs` for each item. The fold applies each item: for a flag that the gate asked, it takes the choice of the user, and false if the project is missing from the answer. For a flag that the gate did not ask, it takes the value that was requested before. Then it stores `closing` and clears `closing_gate`.

Under YOLO, the engine answers the gate with no tests and no documentation, except for the flags that the request already asked. The engine does this because the extra stages cost money and the user did not ask for them. The user can still answer the gate. The conformance tests `t6_closing_gate_is_batched` and `t2_yolo_answers_the_closing_gate` check these rules.

## Test stage

The test stage starts after the format step and when `closing.0` is true. It runs only after the project code is done. No test agent runs between phases (Rule T1). `test_stage` does these steps:

1. Select the covered phases: a phase with no plan file, or a plan phase with `TestPolicy::Required` (Rule T4). A phase with `TestPolicy::Skip` has no tests.
2. For each covered phase with `EpaState::NotStarted`, spawn `execution-path-analyzer` with the purpose `Epa`. All of them run at the same time. Each writes `ostra-epa-phase-N.md`.
3. Wait until each analyzer is `Done` or `Abandoned`. Write-test never starts earlier.
4. Take the first covered phase whose `test_loop` is not terminal. If it is idle, start it with `Work` of kind `Initial` for `write-test`. If not, call `loop_steps` for it. Then return, so write-test runs one phase at a time, in phase order.

The `test_loop` is a normal work loop. Its review is `code-reviewer` with the phase value `N-tests` and the stage `TestReview`. The review gets the analyzer report as `epa_report`. The same cap, autofix, BLOCKER, STUCK, and staging rules hold. A blocked test loop is terminal, so tests for later phases still run.

The analyzer has its own states in `EpaState`. An `Error` ends in `NotStarted` for one automatic retry. After that, or after any other failure, the state is `Failed` and the planner opens an `ExecutionFailed` gate. The answer `retry` sets `NotStarted`. The answer `abandon` sets `Abandoned`, and the phase gets no tests. An interrupted analyzer returns to `NotStarted`.

## Documentation stage

The documentation stage runs for a project when `closing.1` is true and the test stage is finished or off. `docs_stage` does these steps:

1. Return at once if a passed phase of the project has `blocker_open`. This is Rule Hard 21.
2. If the state is `NotStarted`, count the documentation executions that run or are queued in this pass. If the count is below `MAX_DOCS_WRITERS` (4), spawn `documentation` with the purpose `Docs { project }`. The inputs are the implementer reports of the passed phases and the user notes for documentation.
3. If the state is `Failed` with no gate, open an `ExecutionFailed` gate.

The cap of 4 limits cost and the number of parallel executions for a session with many projects (Rule B7). Projects that wait for a place start in a later pass.

The agent submits `DocumentationSubmit` with its part of the book. The fold turns the result into `DocsState` with `stage_run`. The state is `Done` only if the status is `Ok` and the submit is readable, because the engine builds the book from the submit. A run with status `Ok` and no readable submit becomes `Failed` with the text `The run ended without a readable submit call, so there is nothing to put in the book.` A documentation failure has no automatic retry, so the gate opens at once. The answer `retry` sets `NotStarted`. The answer `abandon` sets `Abandoned`, and the project has no part in the book.

For a DOCS request, no implementer ran. The runner writes a stub report `ostra-docs-request.md` for each missing report path, so the agent reads the request from a file.

## Architecture stage and book write

`book_progress` tells the planner when the book is ready. It returns nothing while any project may still get documentation. It returns the list of parts when each project with documentation on is `Done` or `Abandoned`. A project is skipped if it has no passed phase, has documentation off, or has an open BLOCKER.

`book_stage` then does these steps:

1. If the list of parts is empty, or the book was written, do nothing.
2. If the list has 2 or more parts, run `system-architecture` one time (Rule B4). The runner first writes `ostra-docs-parts.json` with the parts of this session. The agent runs in the session root. If it fails, the same `ExecutionFailed` gate rules hold. If the user abandons it, the book has no architecture.
3. Choose the book id. If the user picked a book and the id is valid, use it. If not, use `book_id` of the sorted project keys (Rule B6).
4. Return `Step::WriteBook`.

The runner builds the update with `book_update`, calls `ostra_core::book::apply`, and appends `BookWritten` with the book id, the projects, and an error text if any. A write error does not fail the session. The error text is `The book could not be written to {folder}: {error}`. The planner treats the book as written in all cases. No agent writes a book file (Rule B5), so the engine can check each part before it writes.

## Initialize a created project

An implementer can create a project with `ProjectCreate`. The fold adds the project to the session scope, makes an `InitTrack` for it, and interrupts the execution that made it. The planner holds each spawn for that project, except the initializer and the advisor, until the init ends (Rule O4). `init::plan_created` plans the init in these steps:

1. Run `initializer` in the mode `detect`.
2. Run one `scout` execution for each slice. The cap is `MAX_SCOUTS` (6).
3. Run `propose`, and open the `SkillApproval` gate.
4. Run `generate-skill` for each chosen skill. Only the first `MAX_DEFAULT_GENERATE` (8) skills default to `generate`.
5. Run `generate-inventory`, then return `Step::FinishInit`. The runner checks the inventory and the profile, and appends `ProjectInitFinished`.

If a step fails in a created project, the planner starts `advisor` first, for at most `MAX_ADVICE` (2) rounds for that step. The advisor sees at most `MAX_STEP_RESULT_CHARS` (8000) characters of the failed result. If the advisor escalates, or the rounds end, the user gets an `ExecutionFailed` gate. If the user stopped the step, the advisor is skipped (Rule P4). An init session for a project uses the same plan and ends with a `Project initialized` report.

## Completion and the report

`all_implement_done` is true only when nothing runs and each project is finished with its format, tests, documentation, and book. A project with no passed phase is skipped. Then the planner calls `completion`. It returns nothing in these cases:

- An execution still runs.
- A created project has not finished its init.
- `coordination_open` is true, because a subagent waits for an answer (Rule H9).

If no `completion_decision` exists, the planner calls the `Completion` judge. The judge returns `report_markdown`. When the decision exists, the planner returns `Step::Complete`. The text is the judge report plus a section `## Projects created` if agents created projects. Each row names the key, the path, the stack, and `initialized`, or `not initialized` with a note.

The runner writes the text to `ostra-completion.md` in the session root. The summary is the first non-empty line of the text with the leading `#` characters removed. Then it appends `SessionCompleted`. The fold sets `completed`, the session becomes terminal, and the driver stops. For a session of the kind Init, the runner first checks the inventory and the profile. If they are not valid, it appends `SessionFailed` with `Init did not finish`.

A QUICK_ANSWER session has no judge. Its answer becomes the report. The categories RESEARCH, SPEC, PLAN, VERIFY, PROMPT, and QUICK_CHANGE use the judge too.

If the judge fails 3 times, `perform_judge` appends a fallback decision for `Completion` only. Its report starts with `# Session complete` and says that the judge failed, and then it lists the state facts. Thus a finished session always has a report. Each other judge failure fails the session. Judge cost counts in the session cost, but the budget guard does not count it.

## Limits

| Value | Number | Holder |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Documentation executions at one time | 4 | `MAX_DOCS_WRITERS` in `plan.rs` |
| Format command timeout | 600 seconds | literal in `perform_command` |
| Output tail of a command | 4000 bytes | literal in `run_command` |
| Timeout of `documentation` | 2400 seconds | `timeout_seconds` in `agent.toml` |
| Timeout of `system-architecture` | 1800 seconds | `timeout_seconds` in `agent.toml` |
| Timeout of `execution-path-analyzer` | 1200 seconds | `timeout_seconds` in `agent.toml` |
| Automatic retries of an analyzer | 1 | `ERROR_RETRIES` in `state.rs` |
| Completion judge attempts | 3 | `call_judge` in `runner.rs` |
| Init scouts, default skills, advice rounds | 6, 8, 2 | `MAX_SCOUTS`, `MAX_DEFAULT_GENERATE`, `MAX_ADVICE` in `init.rs` |

## What happens when

- **A project has no passed phase.** It gets no format step, no tests, and no documentation. The session can still complete.
- **The user answers the gate for only one project of a batch.** The answer must hold one choice for each item. A missing project gets false for each flag that the gate asked.
- **Tests are on and docs are on.** Documentation waits for the test stage of the same project. Another project can start documentation earlier.
- **A BLOCKER stays open.** Documentation for that project does not start, and the book has no part for it.
- **The book has one part.** No architecture runs, and the book has no architecture section.
- **The session budget is reached.** The budget guard in `Planner::push` holds each new spawn, also the closing stages. The planner opens one `BudgetReached` gate.
- **The user pauses the session.** The planner returns no step until the user resumes it.
- **The completion judge fails.** The fallback report is used.

sections.title: Agent coordination: ask, reply, and pair loops
sections.summary: How agents ask each other questions with SubagentAsk and SubagentReply, how the engine routes a question and wakes the asker, how pair loops continue a conversation, and why open coordination holds completion.
sections.body:
## Why agents need to ask each other

An agent that works from a report reads the work of another agent cold. It cannot ask what the author meant, and the author cannot defend a choice. The result is guessing, or a restart with a long report. Coordination lets one agent ask another a question, wait, and continue with the answer. A pair loop, such as an implementer and its reviewer, also continues its own conversation and does not start over.

This page covers subagent ids, the three coordination tools, the checks on an ask, the wait rules, the route of a question, the delivery of a message, pair loops, and the rule that open coordination holds completion. All routing code is a pure function of the event log, so a restart gives the same result.

## Terms

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Execution | One run of an agent. It has an id that starts with `x_`. |
| Conversation | A chain of executions where each one continues the one before it. |
| Subagent | A conversation. Its id is the id of its first execution (Rule H1). |
| Asker | The execution that calls `SubagentAsk`. |
| Answerer | The execution that gets the question and calls `SubagentReply`. |
| Helper | A new `explore` execution that a question starts. |
| Consult | A new execution that continues the conversation of a subagent that ended, to answer a question. |
| Head | The latest execution of a subagent. |

`SessionState::subagent_of` maps an execution id to its subagent id. The map `subagents` gets an entry when `ExecutionStarted` has a `resumes` value. The new execution takes the subagent of the execution that it continues. An execution with no entry is its own subagent.

## The three tools

`COORD_TOOLS` in `crates/ostra-core/src/coord.rs` lists the tools. Each has a name on the Ostra MCP server and a native name.

| Tool | MCP name | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SubagentList` | `subagent_list` | Shows the subagents of the session, their status, and the partner roles of the caller. It makes no event. |
| `SubagentAsk` | `subagent_ask` | Sends a question to a helper or to a subagent. The caller waits. |
| `SubagentReply` | `subagent_reply` | Answers the question that the caller owes. |

Only agents with the capability `coordinate` get these tools. In `assets/agents`, these agents have it: `explore`, `generate-spec`, `fact-check`, `plan`, `implementer`, `code-reviewer`, and `write-test`. The reply tool has a different name on a harness. For Claude Code it is `mcp__ostra__subagent_reply`. For other harnesses it is `subagent_reply`. `reply_tool` returns the name.

The entry point is `Engine::coordinate` in `runner.rs`. It returns a `CoordReply` with a text for the model and a `RunEnd`:

| `RunEnd` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Continue` | The execution goes on. `SubagentList` returns it. |
| `Wait` | The execution waits for a message (Rule H2). A successful ask returns it. A reply from a non-consult execution returns it too, because that execution goes back to wait for its own answer. |
| `Finish` | A consult execution answered, and it ends. |

If a check fails, `Engine::coordinate` returns an error text to the model and appends no event.

## Checks on an ask

`SessionState::ask_event` checks an ask in this order. The first failing check gives the error.

| Order | Check | Error says |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `AskInput::parse`: `message` has 1 to 8000 characters after trimming, and exactly one of `agent` and `subagent_id` is set. | Give `message` as plain text of at most 8000 characters, or give exactly one of `agent` or `subagent_id`. |
| 2 | The asker is a running execution of this session. | This run is not running in its session any more. |
| 3 | The asker is not a consult execution. | Answer with `SubagentReply` instead. |
| 4 | The asker does not owe an answer. | Answer the question you were given first, because its asker waits for you. |
| 5 | The session has fewer than 24 asks. | The session reached its limit of 24 questions between subagents. |
| 6 | For a helper: the agent is `explore`. | Ask a helper of an agent that Ostra can start. |
| 7 | For a helper: the asker is not itself a helper. | A helper may not start helpers of its own. |
| 8 | For a helper: the asker started fewer than 3 helpers. | This run already started 3 helpers, the limit. |
| 9 | For a helper: the project is in the scope of the session. The default is the project of the asker. | Give `project` as a key in the scope of this session. |
| 10 | For a subagent: the id belongs to an execution of this session. | The id is not a subagent of this session. |
| 11 | For a subagent: the id is not the asker itself. | This ID is your own. |

The limits stop a loop of questions and the cost of many helpers. The session cap of 24 counts all asks, helpers included. A consult execution cannot ask, so a chain of consults cannot grow. `SessionState::reply_event` checks a reply in a shorter way. The message must be valid, the execution must run, and it must owe an answer. If it owes none, the error says that no question waits for its answer. The result is `Finish` for a consult execution and `Wait` for any other.

## Wait rules

A waiting execution must not hold a resource that another execution needs. The two kinds of executor wait in different ways.

- **Native executor.** `RunEnd::Wait` ends the execution with status `Waiting`. The fold stores the execution in `waiting_keys` under the purpose key of its stage. The fold then treats the result as `Interrupted` for the stage logic. The planner holds the spawn for that purpose key until a message is ready. Then the spawn gets `resumes` with the id of the waiting execution. `perform_spawn` appends `MessageDelivered` and `ExecutionResumed`. The same execution id continues with the message as its note and with its earlier usage.
- **Harness executor.** The process stays alive. `EngineHost::wait_for_wake` registers a oneshot channel in the `mail` map. It then gives back the execution slot of the run and waits. When a message arrives, it takes a slot again and returns the message. A harness reply tool tells the model to end its turn and answer only `Waiting`.

The execution gives its slot back because of the slot limit. Without this rule, a limit of 1 would stop the session. The waiting execution would hold the only slot, and the execution that it waits for could not start.

`recover` handles a restart. For each running execution with an open ask, it appends `ExecutionFinished` with status `Waiting`. Each other running execution gets `Interrupted`. Thus a restart does not lose a question.

## Route of a question

`SessionState::route` decides where a question to a subagent goes. It is a pure function, and the planner calls it again in each pass. A question that cannot go anywhere yet stays pending, and no state is stored.

### How a question finds its answerer

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["AgentAsked"] --> B{"Target"}
    B -- "agent: explore" --> C["Queue an explore task with origin Ask"]
    B -- "subagent_id" --> D{"Head execution of the subagent"}
    D -- "waits on the asker" --> E["WakeInPlace"]
    D -- "running, or waits on another" --> F["Pending"]
    D -- "ended Ok, Stuck, or Handoff, none live" --> G["Consult"]
    D -- "ended Error, Denied, or Cancelled" --> H["Failed with a text"]
    D -- "no such subagent" --> H
```

| `Route` | When | What follows |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `WakeInPlace(id)` | The head execution waits, and it waits on the asker. | The planner delivers the question to that execution. |
| `Pending` | The head runs, waits on another subagent, or has a newer live run. | The question waits. The next pass checks again. |
| `Consult(id)` | The head ended `Ok`, `Stuck`, or `Handoff`, and no execution of the subagent is live. | The planner spawns a consult execution that continues the head. |
| `Failed(text)` | The head ended `Error`, `Denied`, or `Cancelled`, or the subagent does not exist. | The text becomes the answer of the asker: the subagent cannot answer, so continue without it, or ask another. |

A consult execution has the purpose `ExecPurpose::Consult` and the same agent as the head. It has `answer_only` set in its context, so it must not change files. Its note tells it to answer from its conversation and then call the reply tool. The planner skips a consult spawn if another spawn already continues the same subagent in this pass.

A question to `agent: explore` starts a helper. The fold queues an explore task with the origin `Ask`. `coord_started` sets the answerer when the helper starts. When the helper ends with `Ok`, `coord_finished` makes the answer from the findings summary, the research path, and the items that are not covered. This task does not hold the rest of the session, because `loop_bound` is true for the origin `Ask`. If the helper fails after its automatic retry, the failure text is the answer. No gate opens for a helper (Rule H3).

If an answerer ends without a reply, `coord_finished` writes the answer `{subagent} ended its run with status {status} without answering. Continue without the answer, or ask again.` An answerer that is `Interrupted` or `Waiting` keeps the question, unless it is a consult execution.

## Deliveries

`SessionState::next_delivery` gives the message that a waiting execution gets next. It returns nothing if the execution does not wait. The order is fixed:

1. The answer to the own question of the execution, if an answer exists. The note says `The answer from {who} to your question arrived. Continue your task from here.` It also lists the question and the answer. If the user added context after the question, the note ends with that text.
2. A question from the subagent that this execution waits on, if its route is `WakeInPlace` to this execution. The note tells the execution to answer with the reply tool and then end its turn. The execution then goes back to wait for its own answer.

The order puts the answer first because the execution that waits for its own answer can then continue its task at once. A question that arrives while an answer is ready can wait one pass.

Harness executions get deliveries from the planner. `Planner::coordination` returns `Step::Deliver` for each running harness execution that has a delivery. The runner appends `MessageDelivered`, and `deliver_mail` hands a `Wake` with the note to the execution. If the execution does not wait yet, `deliver_mail` stores the `Wake` as `pending`, and `wait_for_wake` returns it at once. The flag `owes_reply` is true when the message is a question. If such an execution tries to end without a reply, the executor tells it to call the reply tool now, because the asker reads only that call.

Native executions get deliveries through their stage spawn, as the wait rules show.

### One question from ask to answer

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Asker as Asker execution
    participant Eng as Engine.coordinate
    participant Fold as SessionState
    participant Plan as Planner
    participant Run as Runner
    participant Cons as Consult execution
    Asker->>Eng: SubagentAsk with message and subagent_id
    Eng->>Fold: ask_event checks the ask
    Eng->>Fold: append AgentAsked
    Eng-->>Asker: waiting text and RunEnd Wait
    Asker->>Run: ends with status Waiting
    Plan->>Fold: route returns Consult
    Plan->>Run: Step Spawn with purpose Consult
    Run->>Cons: ExecutionStarted, continues the head
    Cons->>Eng: SubagentReply with message
    Eng->>Fold: append AgentReplied
    Eng-->>Cons: RunEnd Finish
    Plan->>Run: Step Spawn of the stage with resumes
    Run->>Asker: MessageDelivered and ExecutionResumed
```

## Pair loops

A pair loop is a repeat of two agents on the same work, such as an author and a fact checker, or an implementer and a reviewer. `SessionState::continuation` lets the new execution continue the conversation of the previous one. The agent then keeps what it read and wrote, and it keeps the prompt cache (Rule H5). `Planner::push` sets `continues` when the spawn has no `resumes`.

These pairs continue:

| New execution | Continues |
| --- | --- |
| `generate-spec` after a spec exists | The last spec execution |
| `plan` after a plan exists | The last plan execution |
| `fact-check` of the same target | The last check of that target |
| `code-reviewer` of the same phase and test flag | The last review of that loop |
| `implementer` or `write-test` with kind `Fix`, `BlockerFix`, `Rescue`, or `Resume` | The last work execution of the same phase |

The new execution starts fresh in these cases (Rule H6):

- The previous execution did not end `Ok`, `Stuck`, or `Handoff` with a submit.
- The head of the conversation is a different agent, or did not end with a submit.
- A forced executor differs from the executor of the head.
- The head ran on a harness and left no native session id.
- The user added context after the previous execution started.
- The conversation already has 6 executions (`MAX_CONVERSATION_RUNS`).

The cap of 6 stops a conversation from growing without limit, because a long conversation costs more and can lose focus. A continued execution keeps the executor and the model that the conversation started on.

Rule H7 allows one live execution for each conversation. If the subagent of the head has a live execution, `Planner::push` skips the spawn. The planner tries again after the live execution ends.

The terms "resume" and "continue" differ. A resume keeps the same execution id. The engine uses it for a paused execution and for a waiting execution. A continue makes a new execution id in the same conversation. The engine uses it for pair loops and for consults.

## Open coordination holds completion

`coordination_open` is true when an ask has no delivered answer and its asker waits. `Planner::completion` returns nothing while this is true (Rule H9). Without the rule, a session could complete while an execution waits for an answer. That execution would never wake, and its work would be lost. The conformance test `h9_a_waiting_subagent_holds_completion` checks this rule.

The planner also starts no consult, no delivery, and no helper when the session is paused or has ended. A budget stop holds consult spawns too, because they are spawns.

## Limits

| Value | Number | Holder |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Helpers that one execution can start | 3 | `MAX_HELPERS_PER_RUN` in `ostra-core/src/coord.rs` |
| Asks in one session | 24 | `MAX_SESSION_ASKS` |
| Executions in one conversation | 6 | `MAX_CONVERSATION_RUNS` |
| Characters in one message | 8000 | `MAX_MESSAGE_CHARS` |
| Agents that a question can start | `explore` only | `HELPER_AGENTS` |

These are constants. No setting changes them.

## What happens when

- **The subagent is busy.** The route is `Pending`. When the subagent ends `Ok`, the next pass routes the question to a consult.
- **The subagent failed.** The asker gets the failure text as its answer and continues without it.
- **Two agents ask each other.** If B asks A while A waits on B, the route is `WakeInPlace` to A. A answers, and then A waits again for its own answer.
- **The server restarts while an execution waits.** The execution gets status `Waiting`. The question stays, and the planner routes it again.
- **The user adds context while an execution waits.** The answer note ends with the added text. The next pair-loop spawn starts fresh, because rule H6 applies.
- **The user pauses the session.** No consult and no delivery starts until the user resumes.
- **The user stops the session.** The session is terminal, so waiting executions never wake.
- **A harness execution waits.** It gives its slot back, and it takes a slot again when the message arrives. The wait can take longer than the limit of slots allows, so a new slot can be late by up to 2 seconds.
