`HubMsg` and `Pushed`, the two kinds of broadcast message.
The `tree_patch` and `activity` tickers.

sections.title: Files, git, artifacts, skills, and commands routes
sections.summary: Explains path containment, the file read and save rules, live file updates, workspace artifacts with hidden units, the skill routes, and the command save rules. The git routes are on the next page.
sections.body:
## The problem this part solves

The Files dock lets the user read and edit project files in the browser while agents write the same files. Without rules, a path can leave the project, a save can overwrite an edit that an agent made, and an agent can read a file that the user wants to keep private. The routes on this page enforce path containment, a hash check on save, a read-only list, and the hidden state of artifacts. The page also covers the skill routes and the command routes.

The page covers:

- Path containment (`tree::contain`).
- The file routes: tree, read, save, folder create, name index, diff, and changes.
- Live updates of the dock (`Touch`, `run_touches`, the code watcher).
- Workspace artifacts, hidden units, and Rules W2 and W4.
- The skill routes and the command save rules.

The page "Git dock, clone, pull, and saved git credentials" covers the git routes. The page "REST routes, errors, and the WebSocket protocol" gives the status mapping and the body limits.

## Path containment

Every file route takes a path that is relative to the project root. `tree::contain` in [crates/ostra-server/src/files/tree.rs](crates/ostra-server/src/files/tree.rs) checks it:

1. An absolute path fails with "Use a path relative to the project root."
2. A `..` that goes above the root, a drive, or a root component fails with "That path is outside the project. Use a path inside the project root."
3. The server resolves the path with symlinks followed on the longest part that exists. The result must be inside the canonical project root. A link therefore cannot lead out of the project.

The wrapper `files::contain` turns each failure into 403. A project that is not in the workspace gives 404 "No project `{key}` in this workspace." A project whose folder is gone gives 404 "The folder of project `{key}` is missing". The write-scope guard of the policy engine follows the same symlink rule.

The project key `_artifacts` (`TAG_ROOT`) is special. The same routes then serve the workspace artifacts. The view merges the visible folder and the hidden folder, and creates them if they are missing.

## File routes

### Tree

`GET .../projects/{key}/tree?path=&depth=&hidden=` lists a folder. The depth defaults to 1 and the server clamps it to 1 to `MAX_DEPTH` (4). The list has at most `TREE_CAP` (5,000) entries, and `truncated` shows a cut. Folders come before files. The server never lists `.git`. Dotfiles appear only with `hidden=true`. The server lists symlinked folders and ignored folders but does not enter them. It uses the same ignore sources as the Grep and Glob tools of the agents, so the dock and the agents agree. Each entry carries a git mark from a cached `git status --porcelain=v2 -z`, `staged`, `has_changes` for folders, `ignored`, and `changed_by` (session, execution, agent, phase, running).

### Read

`GET .../file?path=` reads at most `TEXT_CAP` (1 MiB). A longer file has `truncated`. A NUL byte in the first 8,000 bytes marks the file as binary and the response has no content. `hash` is the SHA-256 in hex. It is present only when the text is the whole file and is valid UTF-8. `read_only` holds the reason that a save would fail.

### Save

`PUT .../file` takes `{path, content, base_hash}`. The hash is the optimistic lock: the editor sends the hash of the version it opened, and the server writes only if the disk still has that version.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[PUT file] --> B["Contain the path"]
  B --> C{"Path is empty or a folder"}
  C -- yes --> R1[400]
  C -- no --> D{"Content over 1 MiB"}
  D -- yes --> R1
  D -- no --> E{"Read-only reason"}
  E -- running execution --> R2[409]
  E -- other reason --> R3[403]
  E -- none --> F{"Hash matches disk"}
  F -- no --> R2
  F -- yes --> G["Write temp file and rename"]
  G --> H["Announce project_fs_changed"]
```

The steps are:

1. Contain the path. For a new path inside a hidden artifact unit, use the hidden folder.
2. Refuse an empty path or a folder with 400. For a new artifact, apply the name rules and the limit of 2,000 artifacts.
3. Refuse content larger than `TEXT_CAP` with 400 "The text is larger than 1 MB ..."
4. Apply the read-only rules (see the list below).
5. Take the save mutex. One async mutex serializes all saves.
6. Compare. `save_file` hashes the current bytes and compares them with `base_hash`.
7. Write atomically. The server writes a temp file `.ostra-save-*` in the same folder, calls `sync_all`, keeps the old permissions (or 0644 for a new file on Unix), and renames it over the target. Missing parent folders are created.
8. Record the time of the user edit. This time supersedes older attribution. Then the server invalidates the caches, announces `project_fs_changed`, touches the code index, and returns the file that it reads again.

The read-only rules (`read_only_reason`) are:

- Any path segment equal to `.git`: 403 "Files under .git are read-only here. Use git to change them."
- The runtime folder `.ostra` of the workspace, except the artifacts folder, and the memory folder of the project: 403 "Ostra's own state is read-only here ..." The reason: a direct edit skips the validation of the Settings screen.
- A file that a running execution is writing: 409, because a save now would let one change overwrite the other.

The hash cases (`save_file`) are:

| Disk | `base_hash` | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| File missing | absent | Create the file. |
| File missing | present | 409 on `base_hash`: the file was deleted after you opened it. |
| File exists | absent | 409 on `base_hash`: the file already exists. Open it and edit that version. |
| File exists | differs | 409 on `base_hash`: the file changed on disk. Reload it, or save over it. |
| File exists | equal | Write. |

To save over a changed file, the client reads the file again and sends the new hash.

### Create a folder, list names, diff, and changes

- **`POST .../mkdir {path}`** creates folders like `mkdir -p`. An empty path gives 400. An existing path gives 409 on `path`. The read-only rules apply. The response is the listing of the parent at depth 1 with hidden files shown.
- **`GET .../files`** returns the name index of every file that no ignore rule excludes. It includes dotfiles and excludes `.git`. The list is sorted and holds at most `INDEX_CAP` (50,000) names. It is cached for `INDEX_TTL` (30 seconds) or until a write.
- **`GET .../diff?path=&base=`** returns the diff of one file. `base` defaults to `HEAD` and must pass `valid_base`: 1 to 200 bytes of letters, digits, and `._/~^@{}-`, and no leading `-`. Otherwise the status is 400. For `HEAD` in a repository without commits, the diff uses the empty tree, so new files show as added. An untracked file diffs against nothing. The output is cut at `DIFF_CAP` (4 MiB) with `truncated`. A folder that is not a git repository gives an empty diff. An artifact also gives an empty diff, because artifacts have no history.
- **`GET .../changes`** lists files from sessions that still differ from `HEAD`, at most `CHANGES_CAP` (500). It adds counts from `git diff --numstat` (an untracked file counts its lines). Attribution reads the `ATTRIBUTION_SESSIONS` (20) most recently updated sessions that touched the project, and caches the result for `ATTRIBUTION_TTL` (3 seconds).

Git runs read-only in these routes. The calls use `--no-optional-locks` and `--literal-pathspecs`, set `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` and `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, close stdin, and time out after `GIT_TIMEOUT` (15 seconds). A timeout or a start failure gives no status and no diff, and the dock shows nothing for it.

## Live updates of the dock

The dock must show a file that an agent wrote within a second. Two sources feed `Touch` values to `files::run_touches`:

- **Native executions.** `ToolWatch` pairs a write tool call (`Write`, `Edit`, `MultiEdit`, `NotebookEdit`, `ApplyPatch`) with its successful result. It holds at most `MAX_PENDING` (4,096) pending calls and clears them when the execution ends.
- **Harness executions.** The post-tool observer of the hook bridge reports the writes.

`run_touches` collects the touches of one project for `DEBOUNCE` (150 ms). Then it invalidates the file, git, and attribution caches, touches the code index, and pushes `project_fs_changed`. The server keeps at most `MAX_LIVE` (5,000) live write marks for each project and clears them above that number. A live mark overrides older attribution, unless a newer user save exists.

Changes from outside Ostra, such as an editor or a shell, reach the dock through two paths. The code watcher (`code_watch.rs`) uses the `notify` crate on the project root and on each folder that holds a listed file. It ignores `.git` and paths that `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude` match. It waits for `QUIET` (250 ms) without events and never longer than `MAX_WAIT` (2 seconds) after the first event. A create, remove, or rename marks the batch as structural, and then the server invalidates the listing caches. If the OS refuses folders (a watch limit), the server logs it. If the OS refuses the root, no watch exists and outside edits show within `INDEX_TTL` (30 seconds). The topic "Native tools and code navigation" explains the index that the watcher feeds.

## Workspace artifacts

An artifact is a file that the user keeps for every session of a workspace. Visible artifacts live in `<workspace root>/.ostra/artifacts/`. Every agent reads them. The user can hide a file or a folder. Hidden artifacts live in `<data dir>/hidden-artifacts/<workspace id>/`, where no agent, harness, or sandboxed command reads them (Rule W2).

### Hidden units

The hidden state is a list of units. A unit is a folder or a file that the user hid. The list is in `<data dir>/hidden-artifacts/<workspace id>.units.json`. A path is hidden when it or a folder above it is a unit. This includes files that the user adds to a hidden folder later. `tidy_units` sorts the list, removes duplicates, and drops units inside other units. If the units file is missing (a workspace that hid files before units existed), each hidden file is its own unit.

The invariant is: a path is in the hidden folder exactly when it is within a hidden unit. Every operation keeps it. For example, a new file that the user adds inside a hidden folder goes to the hidden folder, and a file that moves into a hidden folder becomes hidden.

### Rules for names and size

`artifacts::normalize` in `crates/ostra-core/src/artifacts.rs` accepts a relative path with `/`. Backslashes become `/`. A leading `./` and a trailing `/` are removed. The path must have no absolute prefix, no `.` or `..` segment, no empty segment, no segment that starts with `.`, and no control character. The error is 400 "Name the artifact with a relative path such as `guides/style.md` ..." Containment on disk uses `tree::contain` and gives 403.

| Limit | Value | Result when exceeded |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MAX_ARTIFACT_BYTES` | 25 MiB for each upload or save | 400 "Upload artifacts of at most 25 MB, because agents read them whole." |
| `MAX_ARTIFACTS` | 2,000 for each workspace, visible and hidden together | 409 on `path`: delete an artifact first, because the brief of each agent lists them |
| `MAX_BRIEF_ARTIFACTS` | 40 names in the brief of an agent | Agents find the rest with Glob |

### Artifact routes

- `GET .../artifacts` returns `{dir, artifacts[{path, size, modified, hidden}], delete_blocked}` sorted by path.
- `POST .../artifacts?path=` takes the raw body. It answers 409 on `path` if the path exists in either root. The server writes with the atomic `save_file`.
- `GET .../artifacts/download?path=` answers 404 "The workspace has no artifact ..." if the file is absent.
- `POST .../artifacts/hidden {path, hidden}` hides or shows a unit. Hiding a hidden path does nothing. Showing a path inside a hidden folder gives 409: "Show the folder `X` instead: it is hidden, and a hidden folder hides everything in it." `relocate` then moves the files between the two roots.
- `POST .../artifacts/move {from, to}` moves a file or a folder.
- `DELETE .../artifacts?path=` deletes a file and removes empty parent folders up to the root.

After each change, the server announces `project_fs_changed` on the key `_artifacts`.

### Rule W4: no delete or move while agents can read

`blocked` refuses a delete or a move with 409 in these cases:

- A session is Running, Waiting, Stalled, or Paused: "Stop session {id} or wait for it to end, then delete, because its agents may be reading the artifact."
- An execution is running: "Wait for execution {id} to finish, then delete, because it may be reading the artifact."

The API handler also takes `w.work.try_write()`. No session can then start between the check and the change. If it fails, the status is 409 "Try again in a moment, because work is starting in this workspace." The reason for the rule: the old path stops naming a file that an agent can be reading.

`move_to` has these cases: `from` equal to `to` does nothing. A target inside the source gives 400. A missing source gives 404. An existing target gives 409 on `to`. `relocate` checks every target before it moves anything. It creates folders, renames files (it copies and deletes if the data dir is on another file system), removes folders that it emptied, and saves the units last.

## Skills routes

A skill is a `SKILL.md` file with instructions for agents. Ostra skills live in `<project>/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (`SKILLS_DIR`). Ostra still reads the older `<project>/.ostra/skills/` (`LEGACY_SKILLS_DIR`) but never writes it. The `skills` list in `.ostra/project.toml` registers a skill. Only registered skills reach the repo brief. Harness skills live in `.claude/skills`, `.codex/skills`, `.grok/skills`, `.gemini/skills`, and `.ultracode/skills` (`HARNESS_DIRS`). An execution does not load them until the user adopts them.

- **`GET .../workspaces/{ws}/skills`** returns, for each project, a `blocked` reason and the skills. `scan` lists first the entries of `project.toml`, then folders with a `SKILL.md` in the Ostra directories that no entry names, then the harness directories (origin `harness`). The description comes from the frontmatter and supports folded (`>`) and literal (`|`) blocks. A project with a missing folder has no skills and a blocked message. A project with an init session running is blocked: "Wait for the init session to finish before you change skills, because the initializer writes them."
- **`GET .../skills/{name}`** returns the content. The status is 404 if the skill is unknown and 409 if its path leaves the project. `in_project` resolves each path and ignores one that leaves the project, because `project.toml` can come from the repository itself.
- **`GET .../harness-skill?path=`** returns an adopted-not skill from a harness folder, or 404.
- **`PUT .../skills/{name}`** takes `{kind, content, component_type}`. The name has 1 to 64 characters from letters, digits, `-`, and `_`, and starts with a letter or digit, because it becomes a folder name. `kind` is one of `convention`, `creation`, `test`, and `other`. The content cannot be empty and has at most `MAX_SKILL_BYTES` (512 KiB). The target file is the registered path, else the folder that already holds the skill, else `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`. After symlinks, it must be under `.agents/skills/` or the `.ostra/` folder of the project. Otherwise the status is 409 "Edit `{rel}` in the Files tab ..." A symlinked `.agents` cannot carry a write out of the project. Then the server writes the file and updates the `project.toml` entry with source `user`. A broken `project.toml` gives 409 "Fix `.ostra/project.toml` first".
- **`DELETE .../skills/{name}`** removes the entry and deletes the folder `<name>` in each skills directory. It answers 404 if neither existed and 204 otherwise.
- **`POST .../skills/{name}/adopt {from, kind, component_type}`** copies the whole folder of a harness skill into `.agents/skills/<name>`. It copies regular files and folders and skips symlinks. It registers the entry with source `adopted`. A taken name gives 409. A `from` that is not a harness skill gives 404.

## Command save rules

`PUT .../projects/{key}/commands` takes `Commands {build, test, test_one, format, lint, typecheck, run}`. The file `.ostra/project.toml` must exist. If not, the status is 409 "Initialize {key} first". If it does not parse, the status is 409 "Fix `.ostra/project.toml` first".

`clean` checks each field:

- It trims the text. A blank value or a lone dash `—` becomes unset.
- A newline or carriage return is an issue: "Write the command on one line; chain steps with `&&`."
- A control character is an issue.
- A text longer than `MAX_COMMAND_LEN` (2,000 bytes) is an issue.

The server collects all issues and answers 422 "Fix the commands and save again." Each issue has the path `commands.<field>`. A save writes the file with `save_toml`. `trust::saved_format` records the approval of the format command when the user saved it. Then the handler pushes `workspace_updated`, because `ProjectView` carries the profile. The engine and the policy read the profile for each execution, so a saved command applies to the next run.

## What happens when

- **An agent writes a file that the user is editing.** The editor shows `read_only` for that file while the execution runs. A save gives 409.
- **The user saves a file that changed on disk.** The save gives 409 on `base_hash`. Nothing is written.
- **A path uses a symlink that points outside the project.** Containment fails and the status is 403.
- **The user deletes an artifact while a session runs.** Rule W4 answers 409.
- **Two saves arrive at once.** The save mutex runs them one after the other. The second sees the file that the first wrote, so its hash check can fail.
- **A project has no `.ostra/project.toml`.** Skill and command saves answer 409 until the init session writes it.

code_refs.note: Save rules, read-only reasons, caches, and the `run_touches` loop.
Path containment and the ignore-aware walk.
Read-only git calls for status and diff.
Pairs write tool calls with results to make `Touch` values.
The OS watcher and the batching of outside edits.
Hidden units, Rule W2, Rule W4, move, and delete.
Artifact constants and the path rule.
Skill list, save, delete, and adopt.
Command cleaning and the 422 issues.

sections.title: Git dock, clone, pull, and saved git credentials
sections.summary: Explains the git routes of the Files dock, the project claim that serializes git, clone and pull rules, and how saved git credentials reach git without a leak.
sections.body:
## The problem this part solves

The user runs git from the browser while agents also change the project. Two git processes in one folder can corrupt the index. A git command that runs while an agent edits can commit half of a change. A saved token can leak into `.git/config` or to the wrong host. The git routes prevent these cases with a busy check, a project claim, a fixed environment for each git process, and sealed credentials.

The page covers:

- The read routes (status and branches).
- The write operations (`Op::run`).
- Clone and pull.
- Saved git credentials and how git gets them.

The page "Files, git, artifacts, skills, and commands routes" covers the read-only git calls for the file tree and the diff. The master key page "Startup sequence, request guard, and sign-in" explains how the registry seals `git_credential:` rows.

## Read routes

`GET .../projects/{key}/git` returns `GitRepoStatus`: branch, short head, upstream, ahead and behind counts, staged, unstaged, and conflicted lists, `staged_elsewhere`, `busy`, and `truncated`. It runs `git status --porcelain=v2 --branch -z --untracked-files=normal --ignore-submodules=all -- .` with an output cap of 32 MiB. Each change list holds at most `LIST_CAP` (2,000) paths, and `truncated` shows a cut. `staged_elsewhere` counts staged paths outside the folder of the project, because a project can be a subfolder of a larger repository. `busy` holds a text when a session works in the project. A folder that is in no work tree answers `is_git: false`.

`GET .../git/branches` runs `for-each-ref refs/heads refs/remotes --count=500` (`BRANCH_CAP`). The current branch comes first, then local branches before remote ones, then by name. The server omits `<remote>/HEAD`.

## Write operations

The operations are `stage`, `unstage`, `commit`, `fetch`, `push`, and `checkout`. Each is a `POST .../projects/{key}/git/<name>`. Each runs through `Op::run` in [crates/ostra-server/src/repo.rs](crates/ostra-server/src/repo.rs), inside its own spawned task. If the tab closes, git does not stop halfway.

`Op::run` does these steps:

1. Refuse with 409 (`GitError::Busy`) if a session in the status Running, Waiting, or Paused works in the project, or an init session works there. The text is "Stop session {s} or wait for it to finish, then try again, because it is working in `{key}`."
2. Refuse with 502 (`GitError::Git`) if the folder is not in a git repository: "Run git init in it first."
3. Take the claim for the project with `claim`.
4. Run git.
5. Always announce `project_fs_changed` with an empty path list, so the Files dock reloads, even after a failure.
6. Return `{output, status}`, where `status` is the new `GitRepoStatus`.

The claim is a guard object. `claim` refuses with 409 if the workspace is being deleted or a session is starting (the read lock of `w.work` is not available). It also refuses if another clone, pull, or operation holds the same key or a folder that overlaps the folder of this project: "Git is already running in `{k}`. Wait for it to finish, then try again." Dropping the claim frees the key.

| Operation | Git command | Timeout | Rules |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | `git add -A -- <pathspecs>` | `LOCAL_TIMEOUT` (60 seconds) | Each path goes through `contain`. An empty list means `.`. |
| `unstage` | `git restore --staged -- <specs>`. Before the first commit: `git rm --cached -r -q --ignore-unmatch --` | 60 seconds | Same path rules. |
| `commit {message}` | `git commit --no-edit -m` | `COMMIT_TIMEOUT` (5 minutes) | The message is trimmed. Empty: 400 "Write a commit message first." Nothing staged: 400. Conflicts: 400 "Resolve the conflicted files and stage them, then commit." The long timeout is for hooks that run formatters and tests. |
| `fetch` | `git fetch --prune -- <remote>` | `REMOTE_TIMEOUT` (10 minutes) | The remote is `branch.<b>.remote`, else `origin`, else the only remote. No remote: 400. Many remotes and no upstream: 400. |
| `push` | `git push --porcelain` with `HEAD:<branch.<b>.merge>` or `HEAD:refs/heads/<b>` and `--set-upstream` when none | 10 minutes | A detached HEAD gives 400. |
| `checkout {branch, create, start}` | `git switch -c`, `git switch`, or `git switch --track` | 60 seconds | See below. |

The local operations use `--literal-pathspecs`, so a path with a glob character names that file and not a pattern. `fetch` and `push` use the saved credential that matches the URL of the remote.

`checkout` validates the name with `branch_ok`: it must not be empty, must not start with `-`, must not contain `..`, white space, control characters, or any of `~^:?*[\`, and must not end with `/` or `.lock`. `start` must pass `valid_base`. With `create` set, the server runs `git switch -c <name> [start]`, and an existing local branch gives 400. For an existing local branch, it runs `git switch`. For a branch that exists only on a remote, it runs `git switch --track <remote/branch>`. An unknown name gives 400. After a checkout, the server pushes `workspace_updated`.

### Status mapping

The handler `git_err` maps `GitError::Busy` to 409, `GitError::Git` to 502 (Bad Gateway), and `GitError::Invalid` to 400. An import error after a clone gives 422 with issues or 500.

## Clone

`POST .../workspaces/{ws}/clone {url, key, stack, path, branch, credential}` clones a repository and imports it as a project. `clone_plan` checks every field first and answers 422 with one issue for each field (`url`, `key`, `stack`, `path`, `branch`, `credential`).

`parse_remote` accepts `https://`, `http://`, `ssh://`, and `user@host:path`. It refuses these inputs, because they read or run things on the machine of the server:

- Local paths, `file://` URLs, and `ext::` URLs.
- A URL that starts with `-`.
- A URL with white space or control characters.
- An `https` URL that embeds a password, because the password would land in `.git/config`.

The credential comes from the `credential` field, or the server picks one. The automatic choice takes the saved credential whose host and path prefix match the URL. The longest match wins. A `http://` URL to a host that is not loopback never matches, so a token never crosses the network unencrypted. A credential that the user chooses must match the URL kind (ssh or https). The destination is `path`, which must be absolute, or `<workspace root>/<key>`. `new_folder_issues` checks the folder.

The clone runs in a spawned task with `git clone --progress [--branch b] -- url dest` and the timeout `CLONE_TIMEOUT` (30 minutes). The task sends `git_progress` messages, at most one in `PROGRESS_EVERY` (250 ms), and removes a secret of 4 or more characters from each line. If the clone fails, the server removes the destination. If the destination existed and was empty, the server empties it again. If the clone succeeds, the server imports the checkout as a project and pushes `workspace_updated`.

## Pull

`POST .../projects/{key}/pull` runs `git pull --ff-only` with the timeout `PULL_TIMEOUT` (10 minutes). The server refuses in these cases: the folder is not a git repository (400), a session works in the project (409), or no branch is checked out. The remote is `branch.<b>.remote`, else `origin`. The result is `{branch, updated, before, after, output}`, where `updated` is true if `HEAD` changed. `--ff-only` makes the pull fail instead of creating a merge commit, so a pull never changes history without the user.

## Saved git credentials

The routes `GET` and `POST /api/git/credentials`, and `PATCH` and `DELETE /api/git/credentials/{id}`, manage credentials. Each is a registry row `git_credential:gc_<uuid v7>`, sealed with the master key. The responses show only a view with `has_secret`, never the secret.

- `kind` is `https` or `ssh`.
- The host is normalized: `https://GitHub.com/acme/` becomes `github.com/acme`. It must hold letters, digits, `.`, `-`, an optional `:port`, and optional path segments of `[A-Za-z0-9._~-]`.
- An https secret is a token without white space or control characters. The default user name is `x-access-token` (`DEFAULT_TOKEN_USER`).
- An ssh secret must contain `PRIVATE KEY-----`. A newly entered key must not be `ENCRYPTED`, because git has no terminal to ask for a passphrase.

### How git gets the secret

`GitAuth` builds the environment of each git process. Every git process gets `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, and on Windows `GCM_INTERACTIVE=never`, so git fails and does not wait for input. The server removes the secret from the output.

- **https token.** The server clears the helpers of the user (`credential.helper=`). It adds a one-off `credential.helper` that answers only for the host of the credential, so a `url.*.insteadOf` rewrite in a repository cannot send the token to another host. It pins `http.proxy=` and `http.sslVerify=true`. It passes the token in the variables `OSTRA_GIT_HOST`, `OSTRA_GIT_USERNAME`, and `OSTRA_GIT_PASSWORD`, so the token is never in a command line or a file.
- **ssh key.** The server writes the key with mode 0600 in a temp folder under `<data dir>/tmp`. It sets `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` to `ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new -o IdentitiesOnly=yes -i <key>`. `BatchMode` stops password prompts, and `IdentitiesOnly` stops ssh from offering other keys.

## What happens when

- **A session starts in the project while the user commits.** `claim` fails if the read lock of `w.work` is not available, and `Op::run` refuses if a session already works there.
- **The user clicks Fetch twice.** The second call finds the claim and answers 409.
- **Two clones target overlapping folders.** The second answers 409, because `claim` compares the folders.
- **The tab closes during a push.** The task goes on and finishes, and the Files dock reloads for other tabs.
- **A remote needs a login and no credential matches.** Git fails at once, because prompts are off. The status is 502 with the output of git.
- **The user deletes a workspace during a clone.** The claim holds the read lock of `w.work`. `retire` refuses a busy workspace.

## Limits

| Name | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `LIST_CAP` | 2,000 paths in each list |
| `BRANCH_CAP` | 500 branches |
| `LOCAL_TIMEOUT` | 60 seconds |
| `COMMIT_TIMEOUT` | 5 minutes |
| `REMOTE_TIMEOUT` | 10 minutes |
| `CLONE_TIMEOUT` | 30 minutes |
| `PULL_TIMEOUT` | 10 minutes |
| `QUICK_TIMEOUT` | 30 seconds |
| `PROGRESS_EVERY` | 250 ms |
| Status output | 32 MiB |
