sections.title: REST client, socket manager, and live state
sections.summary: Explains the request wrapper, the reconnecting socket, the shared stores, the activity fold, and the rule that a REST snapshot is the truth.
sections.body:
## Two data sources and one rule

The server sends data in two ways: REST responses and socket messages. A socket message can be lost when the connection drops. A message can also arrive before the data that it changes. Without one rule, a screen would show stale or doubled data. The console uses this rule: **the REST snapshot is the truth, and the socket only keeps the snapshot fresh.** After each reconnect, the console fetches the snapshot again.

This page covers the REST client, the generated types, the socket manager, the shared stores, the per-screen hooks, the activity fold, and the failure cases. A **snapshot** is the data that one REST request returns. A **live message** is one JSON message from the socket. A **channel** is a named stream of live messages that a client subscribes to. The page *Console structure, routing, tabs, and the shell* explains the mock that replaces both sources in mock mode.

## The REST client

### One request wrapper

All typed endpoint functions call `request<T>` in `web/src/api/client.ts`. The wrapper does these steps:

1. Call `fetch` with the method, an optional `AbortSignal`, `credentials: same-origin`, and a JSON body. A JSON body adds the header `Content-Type: application/json`.
2. If the status is 401, call every function that `onUnauthorized` registered. `App` registers one function, and it shows the sign-in screen.
3. If the status is not in the 2xx range, build the message `<status> <statusText>`. If the body is JSON, replace the message with its `error` string and keep its `issues` array. Throw `HttpError(status, message, issues)`.
4. If the status is 204, or the body is empty, return `undefined`. Otherwise parse the body as JSON.

```ts
if (res.status === 401) {
  unauthorizedListeners.forEach((fn) => fn());
}
if (!res.ok) {
  let message = `${res.status} ${res.statusText}`;
  ...
  throw new HttpError(res.status, message, issues);
}
```

### Status codes the screens see

| Status | Cause | What the console does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | No session cookie, or an unknown cookie. | Shows `SignIn` through the listeners. |
| 409 | The engine returns `EngineError::Invalid` or `EngineError::Ended`. | Throws `HttpError`. The gate card shows the message under the form. |
| 422 | A validation failure. The body has `issues`. | Throws `HttpError` with `issues`. Screens place each issue next to its field. |
| Other | Any other non-2xx status. | Throws `HttpError` with the status line, or the `error` text of the body. |

The server maps the errors in `ApiErr` in `crates/ostra-server/src/api.rs`. The page *REST routes, errors, and the WebSocket protocol* explains that side.

### Paths, queries, and uploads

- Every path segment goes through `encodeURIComponent`.
- The helper `q()` builds a query string. It drops parameters that are `undefined`, `null`, or an empty string.
- `rawPost` uploads an artifact as `application/octet-stream`. It throws `HttpError` on failure, but it does not call the 401 listeners.
- `uploadFile` stages a session file with `?name=<file name>`. It throws a plain `Error` with the message only. It carries no `issues` and makes no 401 broadcast.
- `fsBrowse` accepts an `AbortSignal`. The other functions do not.
- `search` has the default limit 30. `codeSymbols` has the default limit 50.

Because `rawPost` and `uploadFile` skip the listeners, a revoked browser does not see the sign-in screen from these two calls alone. The next call through `request` shows it.

### Endpoint groups

`httpApi` holds one function for each server route. `Api` is `typeof httpApi`. These groups exist:

- **Auth and info:** `info`, `exchange`, `signIns`, `revokeSignIn`, `revokeOtherSignIns`, `signOut`.
- **Workspaces:** `workspaces`, `createWorkspace`, `workspace`, `saveSettings`, `deleteWorkspace`, `fixSettings`, `validateSettings`, `approveCommands`, the four MCP calls, `uiState`, `patchUiState`, `onboarding`, `tree`, `search`, `workspaceActivity`, `cost`, `ask`.
- **Projects and git:** import, clone, pull, remove, init, the git status and write calls, the git credential calls, and the project file, diff, and change calls.
- **Code intelligence:** `codeFile`, `codeUsages`, `codeExternal`, `codeDeps`, `codeSymbols`, `codeGraph`, `codeReindex`.
- **Sessions and executions:** `sessions`, `createSession`, `session`, `events`, `setYolo`, `amend`, `stopSession`, `pauseSession`, `resumeSession`, `uploadFile`, `answerGate`, `overrideDecision`, `execution`, `activity`, `cancelExecution`, `resumeExecution`, `inspectExecution`.
- **Artifacts, memory, skills, and books:** the artifact calls, the lesson calls, the skill calls, `books`, `book`, `deleteBook`.
- **Environment and push:** `environment`, `saveProvider`, `listDir`, `fsBrowse`, `fsMkdir`, `harnessSetup`, `pushSubscribe`.

### Generated types

The Rust types in `crates/ostra-core/src/api.rs` and its sibling modules carry `#[ts(export)]`. The command `cargo test -p ostra-core export_bindings` runs ts-rs and writes one file for each type to `web/src/api/gen/`. The file `.cargo/config.toml` sets `TS_RS_EXPORT_DIR` to `web/src/api/gen` and `TS_RS_LARGE_INT` to `number`, so 64-bit integers become `number`. Each file starts with 'This file was generated by ts-rs. Do not edit this file manually.' Biome skips this folder.

`web/src/api/types.ts` re-exports 232 of the 332 files with `export type *`. A few types are imported straight from `./gen`, for example `Book`, `BookSummary`, `CodeRef`, and `Severity`. `api/nav.ts` re-exports the tree, search, and activity shapes. `api/extra.ts` holds the only hand-written wire types: `PtyFrame` and `SocketState`.

The console and the server share one definition. A renamed field is therefore a compile error in `npm run typecheck` and not a surprise at run time. A newer server can send a gate kind that the console does not know. The page *Gate forms, book reader, and HTML export* explains what the console shows in that case.

## The socket manager

`socket()` creates one `SocketManager` at its first call and starts it. The URL is `ws://<host>/ws`, or `wss://` on an HTTPS page. Every screen shares this one connection. The state is `connecting`, `open`, or `closed` (`SocketState`).

### Messages and channels

The client sends seven message types: `subscribe`, `unsubscribe`, `term_input`, `term_resize`, `code_complete`, `code_signature`, and `code_navigate`. The server sends fifteen: `session_event`, `execution_delta`, `execution_status`, `session_updated`, `workspace_updated`, `harness_status`, `subscribed`, `error`, `project_fs_changed`, `git_progress`, `tree_patch`, `activity`, `code_completion`, `code_signature_help`, and `code_navigation`.

The five channel kinds are `session:<id>`, `execution:<id>`, `term:<execution>`, `workspace:<id>`, and `home`. The function `channelsFor` decides which channels get a message:

| Live message | Channels |
| --- | --- |
| `session_event` | `session:<session>` |
| `execution_delta`, `execution_status` | `execution:<execution>` |
| `session_updated` | `session:<id>`, `workspace:<workspace>`, `home` |
| `workspace_updated` | `workspace:<workspace>`, `home` |
| `harness_status` | `home` |
| `project_fs_changed`, `git_progress`, `tree_patch`, `activity` | `workspace:<workspace>` |
| `subscribed`, `error` | none |

`onAny` listeners receive every message. The three hint replies (`code_completion`, `code_signature_help`, `code_navigation`) go only to the pending hint promise. The manager drops a malformed JSON message without a trace.

### Subscribe and unsubscribe

`subscribe(channel, handler)` adds the handler to a set for the channel. Only the first handler of a channel sends `{ type: subscribe, channel }`. Only the removal of the last handler sends `unsubscribe`. This reference count lets many components read one channel with one server subscription. `send` writes only when `readyState` is 1. Otherwise it drops the message, because the manager replays all subscriptions on the next open.

### Connection states and reconnect

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> connecting: start
    connecting --> open: onopen
    connecting --> closed: onclose
    open --> closed: onclose
    closed --> connecting: backoff timer fires
    closed --> [*]: stop
```

The `onclose` handler does the recovery work. `onerror` does nothing, because a close event always follows it. On close, the manager sets the state to `closed` and settles every pending hint with `null`. Unless `stop()` ran, it schedules `connect()` after `min(10000, 500 * 2^attempts)` ms. The delays are 500, 1000, 2000, 4000, 8000, and then 10000 ms. A successful open sets `attempts` back to 0.

On each open, the manager sends `subscribe` again for every channel in its map. From the second successful open on, it also calls every `onReconnect` listener. Stores and screens use these listeners to fetch their snapshot again. The first open calls no listener, because no data is stale yet.

### Binary terminal frames

The server sends terminal output as binary frames: byte 0 is the length `n` of the execution id, then `n` bytes of the id in UTF-8, then raw terminal bytes. `decodePtyFrame` returns `null` for an empty buffer or a buffer shorter than `1 + n`. `terminal(execution, handler)` registers a byte handler and subscribes to `term:<execution>`. The first frame after the subscribe is the backlog: the live screen, or the stored transcript of an ended execution. Keystrokes return as `term_input`, and the size returns as `term_resize`.

### Hints

`hint(type, request)` sends `code_complete`, `code_signature`, or `code_navigate` with an increasing id. The promise resolves with `null` in these cases:

- The socket is not open when the call starts.
- `HINT_TIMEOUT_MS` (30000 ms) passes without a reply.
- The socket closes.
- A newer request of the same type replaces it. The server also stops the older request.

A reply carries the id and settles the matching promise. It is not routed to a channel.

### Server limits the console meets

These limits come from `crates/ostra-server/src/ws.rs`:

| Limit | Value | Result when exceeded |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MAX_MESSAGE` | 1 MiB for each client message | The server sends an `error` message. |
| `MAX_TERM_INPUT` | 64 KiB for each `term_input` | The error is 'Terminal input is limited to 64 KiB per message. Paste in smaller parts.' |
| `MAX_CHANNELS` | 256 channels for each connection | The server sends an `error` message. |
| `TERM_QUEUE` | 64 queued binary frames for each socket | A slow socket lags and resynchronizes. |

The server re-checks the sign-in every `RECHECK` (5 seconds) and closes a revoked socket with code 4401 and the reason 'Signed out'. A lagging broadcast sends the `error` message 'lagged'. The console has no handler for `error` messages, and it does not treat code 4401 in a special way. It only reconnects. A revoked browser reaches the sign-in screen through the next REST 401.

## Shared stores

`SharedStore<T>` in `web/src/lib/store.ts` gives every component that reads one key the same data: one fetch, one socket subscription, and one reload after each reconnect. A store has a `load(key, feed)` function and an optional `live(key, feed)` function. For each key, it keeps one snapshot with `data`, `error`, and `loading`.

These steps run for one key:

1. The first subscriber starts the entry. The store runs `live` (the socket subscription), registers `socket().onReconnect(load)`, and then runs `load`.
2. Each `load` increments a generation counter. A response from an older generation is ignored (`gen === e.gen`). This stops a slow old response from replacing newer data.
3. If a load fails, the snapshot keeps its old data and sets `error`.
4. When the last subscriber leaves, the store waits one `setTimeout(0)` tick before it stops the entry. A remount in the same tick (React `StrictMode` or a tab switch) therefore keeps the subscription.
5. The last value stays cached. A screen that returns renders it at once and refreshes it in the background. A stop also increments the generation, so a response that arrives after the stop is dropped.

`useShared(store, key)` binds a store to React with `useSyncExternalStore`. A `null` key reads nothing. `feed.update(fn)` replaces the data only when `fn` returns a different value. Returning the previous value leaves the data unchanged. The function `throttle(fn, ms)` runs `fn` at once, then at most one time for each `ms`, with one trailing call. Its `cancel()` clears the timer.

| Store (hook) | Key | Loads | Live update |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `treeStore` (`useWorkspaceTree`) | workspace | `api.tree`, sorted by `updated_at` descending | `tree_patch` upserts a row. `session_updated` upserts through `summaryToTree`, which keeps the groups and artifacts of the old row. |
| `summariesStore` (`useSessionSummaries`) | workspace | `api.sessions` | `session_updated` replaces or prepends a summary. |
| `activityStore` (`useActivity(ws)`) | workspace | `api.workspaceActivity` | `activity` replaces the value. |
| `fileIndexStore` (`useFileIndex`) | workspace and project | `api.projectFiles` | `project_fs_changed` for the project reloads it, at most once each 1000 ms. |
| `changesStore` (`useProjectChanges`) | workspace and project | `api.projectChanges` | The same reload rule as `fileIndexStore`. |
| `workspacesStore` (`useWorkspaces`) | `all` | `api.workspaces` | `workspace_updated` or `session_updated` on `home` reloads it, throttled to 1000 ms. |

Note that `useActivity(ws)` in `lib/live.ts` and `useActivity(id, onStatus)` in `screens/execution/useExecution.ts` are two different hooks. The first reads workspace activity for the status bar. The second reads the activity stream of one execution.

Two more hooks live in `lib/live.ts`. `useSocketState` returns the manager state and follows `onState`. `useSearch(ws, query, delayMs = 100)` waits the delay, then calls `api.search`. An empty query returns no items and makes no request. If the request fails, the hook sets `unavailable`, and callers search the rows that they already hold.

## Per-screen hooks

Smaller needs use the older helpers in `web/src/lib/hooks.ts`:

- `useAsync(load, deps)` loads data, exposes `reload` and `set`, and reloads when `deps` change and after every socket reconnect.
- `useChannel(channel, handler)` subscribes for the life of the component. It keeps the latest handler in a ref, so a new handler does not resubscribe.
- `useThrottled(fn, ms)` is the hook form of `throttle`.
- `useStoredFlag(key, initial)` keeps a boolean in `localStorage` as `1` or `0`.

## The REST snapshot is the truth

Three mechanisms follow the rule.

### Stores

A store reloads after a reconnect, and it ignores older loads. A live message only patches the data between loads.

### The session board

`SessionScreen` keeps the REST `detail`, the REST `events`, and a `live` list from `session:<id>`. `mergeEvents` removes duplicates by `seq` and sorts the result. When a `session_event` arrives, the screen appends it to `live` and calls a throttled refresh (400 ms, with a trailing call) that reloads `api.session(id)`. A `session_updated` message replaces `detail.summary` at once. When the events snapshot reloads, the effect `setLive([])` clears the live list, because the new snapshot already contains those events.

### The execution stream

`useActivity(id, onStatus)` in `useExecution.ts` loads the activity snapshot and subscribes to `execution:<id>`. A delta that arrives before the snapshot is held in a list. After the snapshot lands, the hook folds it and applies the held deltas. After a reconnect, it requests only the items after the last `seq`.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Screen as useActivity
    participant REST as api.activity
    participant Socket as channel execution id
    Screen->>REST: request activity snapshot
    Socket-->>Screen: delta seq 7, held
    REST-->>Screen: items seq 1 to 6
    Screen->>Screen: foldActivity then apply held deltas
    Socket-->>Screen: delta seq 8, applied at once
    Socket-->>Screen: reconnect
    Screen->>REST: request items after last seq
```

`useExecution(id)` adds two reloads. A `gate_opened` or `gate_answered` event on the session channel reloads the execution (throttled to 400 ms), because `pending_gate` comes from the fold of the session. An `execution_started`, `execution_resumed`, or `execution_finished` event reloads the session (throttled to 800 ms). The hook `useNow(on)` ticks once each second while an execution runs, for the elapsed time.

## The activity fold

`applyDelta(state, seq, delta)` in `web/src/lib/events.ts` is a pure reducer that turns execution deltas into display entries. The first rule is `if (seq <= state.lastSeq) return state`. A delta at or below the last seen `seq` changes nothing, so a snapshot and the live stream can overlap safely. `foldActivity(items, start)` reduces the REST items with `applyDelta`.

| Delta kind | Effect on the state |
| --- | --- |
| `text`, `thinking` | Merge into the last entry if it has the same kind and lies in the current turn. Otherwise add a new entry. |
| `status` | Add a status entry. |
| `tool_call` | Add a tool entry. If the call id is in `pending.ids`, the entry gets the cost share `pending.share`. |
| `policy` | Set the policy decision on the tool with that call id. |
| `tool_output` | Append the chunk to the `live` text of that tool. |
| `tool_result` | Set `output`, `isError`, and `durationMs`, and mark the tool `done`. |
| `usage` | Replace the usage. |
| `turn` | Attach `{ cost, calls }` to the latest thinking entry of the turn. If no thinking entry exists and there are 0 calls, add a `turn` entry. Set `pending` to the call ids and an even cost share. Move `turnStart` to the end. |
| `native_session_id` | Store the id. |
| `egress`, `decoy` | No case exists. These deltas change nothing. |

A tool result for an unknown call id is ignored, because `findTool` returns -1. The reason for the cost share: a native executor streams the text of a response, then its tool calls, and the provider reports one cost for each response. The console divides the cost evenly among the calls of the response and shows the share on each call.

The same file holds more pure helpers:

| Helper | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `toolSummary` | One line for a tool call: the path for `Read`, `Write`, and `Edit`, the command for `Bash` (cut at 160 characters), the pattern for `Grep` and `Glob`, and so on. A tool whose name starts with `submit_` shows 'result submitted to Ostra'. |
| `denialAdvice` | What to do after a refusal, keyed by the guard id. A deny rule and an ask with no rule have their own text. |
| `currentGate` | The first open permission gate, else the oldest open gate by `opened_at`. |
| `phaseLayers` | Layers of the phase graph. A `null` `depends_on` means that the phase depends on every lower id. A phase in a cycle counts as depth 0. |
| `describeEvent` | One line for each `SessionEvent` type. |
| `activeSecurityBlocks` | The latest `security_block` for each project, phase, and tests flag. An event with no findings clears the block. |

## What happens when

- **A load fails.** The snapshot keeps its old data and sets `error`. A screen with no data shows a banner with 'Try again'. `SessionScreen` shows 'Ostra could not load this session'.
- **The socket is down.** The status bar shows 'Offline, reconnecting'. Data stays stale until the first reconnect fetch.
- **The socket reconnects.** The manager subscribes again to every channel, then calls the `onReconnect` listeners. A gate that opened or closed during the outage appears without a manual refresh.
- **A REST request returns 401.** The app shows the sign-in screen.
- **A search request fails.** `useSearch` sets `unavailable`, and the palette filters local rows.
- **A live message names an unknown type.** `channelsFor` returns no channel, and no handler runs.
- **A hint gets no reply.** The promise resolves with `null` after 30000 ms.
- **A component remounts in the same tick.** The store keeps its subscription.

## Limits and defaults

| Name | Value | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reconnect delay | 500 ms doubling to 10000 ms | `web/src/api/socket.ts` |
| `HINT_TIMEOUT_MS` | 30000 ms | `web/src/api/socket.ts` |
| Store reload throttle | 1000 ms | `web/src/lib/live.ts` |
| Session refresh throttle | 400 ms | `web/src/screens/SessionScreen.tsx` |
| `useSearch` debounce | 100 ms | `web/src/lib/live.ts` |
| `search` limit | 30 | `web/src/api/client.ts` |
| `codeSymbols` limit | 50 | `web/src/api/client.ts` |

sections.title: Gate forms, book reader, and HTML export
sections.summary: Explains how each gate kind renders and validates an answer, how book pages are built and escaped, how the reader works, and the steps and sanitizing rules of the HTML export.
sections.body: ## Why gate forms and books need rules A gate stops a session until a person answers. The answer must fit the shape that the engine expects. If a form sends the wrong shape, the server refuses it, and the user loses time. A documentation book has a second risk: agents write its text, and that text must never change the structure of a page or run code in the browser. This page covers the gate forms, the checks that the console makes before it sends an answer, the book reader, and the HTML export. The page *Gates: the 14 kinds, their answers, and YOLO* explains the engine side of gates. The page *Documentation books* explains how the docs stage writes a book. ## From a gate to a form `GateCard` in `web/src/features/gates/GateCard.tsx` renders one gate. It wraps the content in a `div` with the id `gate-`. A URL hash `#gate-` scrolls to this card. The status bar uses the same anchor. If `gate.answer` is not `null`, the card shows the design `GateCard` in answered mode. These rules apply: - `answeredBy` is `yolo` when `gate.source` is `yolo`, else `user`. - The answer text is `answerSummary(gate)`. When `source` is `engine`, the text starts with 'Closed by Ostra: '. - If `gate.reason` exists, the card shows 'Reason: ...'. If the gate is open, `OpenForm` picks the form from the payload kind: | Payload kind | Form | | --- | --- | | `fact_check_recurring`, `review_cap`, `stuck`, `phase_blocked`, `harness_failure`, `execution_failed`, `budget_reached`, `implementation_review` | `ChoiceGate` | | `open_questions` | `QuestionsGate` | | `spec_approval`, `plan_approval` | `ApprovalGate` | | `closing_gate` | `ClosingGate` | | `permission` | `PermissionGate` | | `skill_approval` | `SkillsGate` | | Any other kind | The design `GateCard` with a title and an explanation, and no form. | Every form receives `GateFormProps` from `kit.tsx`: the `gate`, the typed `payload`, `submit`, `fail`, `busy`, and `error`. `OpenGate` in the same file builds the open card: the design `GateCard` with the form body, an error line with `role=alert`, and the button row. A newer server can send a gate kind that the console does not know. Then `ANSWER_KIND[kind]` is `undefined`, `isChoiceKind` is false, and the card has no form and no buttons. The user cannot answer in the console. The design `GateKind` union also lacks `implementation_review`, so that kind shows the fallback icon `circle-pause`. ### Send an answer ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant User participant Form as Gate form participant Answers as gateAnswers.ts participant Card as GateCard participant Server participant Board as SessionScreen User->>Form: press an answer button Form->>Answers: build and check the answer Answers-->>Form: answer or error text Form->>Card: submit answer or fail message Card->>Server: POST /api/gates/id/answer Server-->>Card: 200 GateView or 409 with error Card->>Board: onAnswered with the new gate Board->>Server: reload detail and events ``` The `submit` function in `GateCard` does these steps: 1. Set `busy` to true and clear the error. The card dims to opacity 0.7, and the buttons are disabled. 2. Call `api.answerGate(gate.id, { answer })`. 3. On success, call `onAnswered(updatedGate)`. `SessionScreen` patches the gate into its `detail` and reloads the detail and the events. The answered card replaces the open card, and it appears under 'Show answered gates (N)'. 4. On failure, show `error.message` under the form. 5. In every case, set `busy` to false. When a form calls `fail(message)`, the card shows the message and sends no request. ## Why the console and the server both check `web/src/lib/gateAnswers.ts` mirrors `validate_answer` in `crates/ostra-engine/src/runner.rs`. The server is the authority. The console checks first, because a local message appears at once and costs no request. The server still checks, because a client can be old or wrong. These are the server messages. Each one is `EngineError::Invalid`, which the API returns as status 409: | Condition | Server message | | --- | --- | | The answer kind does not fit the gate kind. | That answer does not fit this gate. | | An open question has no non-empty answer. | Answer before continuing. | | A spec or plan change request has no feedback. | Say what to change. | | An `implementation_review` answer is `feedback` without text. | Say what to change. | | An `implementation_review` option is not `done` or `feedback`. | Answer done, or feedback with what to change. | A gate that ended with its session returns `EngineError::Ended`, which is also status 409. The console is stricter than the server in three places. It requires text for the option `fact` of a `stuck` gate. It checks the amount of a `budget_reached` answer. It requires the Other text of a question. The server does not check these three cases. ## The answer kinds `ANSWER_KIND` maps each of the 14 gate kinds to one answer kind: | Answer kind | Gate kinds | | --- | --- | | `questions` | `open_questions` | | `approval` | `spec_approval`, `plan_approval` | | `choice` | `fact_check_recurring`, `review_cap`, `stuck`, `phase_blocked`, `harness_failure`, `execution_failed`, `budget_reached`, `implementation_review` | | `closing` | `closing_gate` | | `permission` | `permission` | | `skills` | `skill_approval` | ## Approval gates `ApprovalGate` serves `spec_approval` and `plan_approval`. The gate opens only after a fact-check PASS, so the card shows the chip 'Fact-check PASS', a link to the artifact, and the summary. A plan card also shows a phase table with the columns Phase, Project, Complexity, Tests, and Depends on. A `null` `depends_on` shows 'Unclear, runs after earlier phases'. LOW findings appear in a table with the note 'These LOW findings do not block approval.' The card has one text box and two buttons: - **Approve the spec** or **Approve the plan** is the primary button. It sends `{ kind: approval, approved: true, feedback: null }`. It is disabled while the text box holds text, with the tooltip 'Clear the change request to approve'. This stops a user from approving and asking for a change in one action. - **Request changes to the spec** or **Request changes to the plan** needs text. If the text is empty, `changeRequest` returns the error 'Say what should change so the spec agent can rewrite it.' Otherwise it sends `approved: false` with the trimmed text. ## Open questions `QuestionsGate` renders one fieldset for each question, with the id chip, the tag chip, and 'Choose one or more' for multi-select questions. The recommended option moves to the front (`orderedOptions`) and gets the chip 'Recommended'. Options are numbered from 1. The last option is always **Other** (the value `__other__`), with a text field. A single-select question uses radio buttons. A multi-select question uses checkboxes. No option is selected at the start (`defaultSelections` is empty). When the user presses **Send the answers**, `questionsAnswer` checks each question in order: - If the user chose Other and the text is empty, the error is ': write your answer in the Other field.' - If nothing is chosen, the error is ' has no answer yet.' - Otherwise the answer joins the chosen labels and the trimmed Other text with a semicolon and a space. The result is `{ kind: questions, answers: [{ id, question, answer }] }`. ## Choice gates `ChoiceGate` serves eight kinds. The buttons come from `CHOICES[kind]` in order, and exactly one button is primary. `choiceAnswer` checks, in this order: the option exists for the kind ('This gate has no option .'), a required text is not empty, and the budget amount has the right format. It sends `{ kind: choice, option, text }`. `text` is `null` for an option with `text: none`, and for an empty field otherwise. | Gate kind | Options (option string, button label, variant, text) | Text field | | --- | --- | --- | | `fact_check_recurring` | `another-round` Run another fact-check round, primary, optional. `stop` Stop the session, danger, none. | Optional. What the target agent should know about the findings. | | `review_cap` | `another-pass` Run another fix and review pass, primary, optional. `stop` Stop and block the phase, default, none. | Optional. An instruction for the fix pass, added after the findings. | | `stuck` | `fact` Re-run with this fact, primary, required. `block` Block this work, default, none. | Required for `fact`: 'The missing fact', 3 rows, quoted to the agent verbatim. The error is 'Write the missing fact first. The agent re-runs with it quoted verbatim.' | | `phase_blocked` | `retry` Retry the phase, primary, optional. `leave` Leave the phase blocked, default, none. | Optional. An empty field retries with the last review findings. | | `harness_failure` | `retry` Retry after login, primary, none. `native` Run on the native executor, default, none. | None. | | `execution_failed` | `retry` Retry the execution, primary, none. `abandon` Abandon this work, default, none. | None. | | `budget_reached` | `raise` Raise the budget, primary, optional. `stop` Stop the session, danger, none. | Optional amount in US dollars. The placeholder is the budget with 2 decimals. An empty field adds the budget again. | | `implementation_review` | `done` Accept the implementation, primary, none. `feedback` Send feedback, default, required. | Required for `feedback`: 'What to change', 4 rows. The error is 'Describe what to change first. Ostra builds it as a reviewed revision.' | The `budget_reached` amount must pass `parseDollars`: a positive number with an optional leading dollar sign. Otherwise the error is 'Enter the amount as a number of US dollars, such as 10. Leave it empty to add the budget again.' The card also says that YOLO never answers this gate, because spending more is the decision of the user. The body of each kind shows the context: for example the findings tables, the diagnostic of a `stuck` gate, the harness name and the link 'Open the terminal' for `harness_failure`, and the links to the session context and the reports for `implementation_review`. ## Permission gates `PermissionGate` shows the agent, the tool, a link 'Open the execution', and the call. A `Bash` call appears as `$ `. Other tools appear as JSON. The card also shows the policy reason when it differs from the gate explanation, and `Rule: `. It has three buttons: - **Allow once** (primary) sends `allow-once`. - **Always in this workspace: ** sends `always-in-workspace`. It is disabled when `payload.suggestion` is `null`, with the tooltip 'This call has no rule to add'. The engine function `suggest_rule` computes the suggestion. - **Deny** (danger) sends `deny`. The agent then continues without the call. The execution waits until the user answers. `currentGate` puts permission gates first in the list of open gates. ## Skill and closing gates `SkillsGate` shows a table with the name, the kind, the description and examples, and a `Select` for each skill. The options are `generate`, `regenerate`, `reuse`, and `drop`, and the default is the disposition of the proposal. The footer shows ' of kept for ', and `drop` is not counted as kept. **Approve the skills** sends `{ kind: skills, decisions }`. The engine writes nothing before this approval. `ClosingGate` shows one block for each project with the number of phases. The checkbox 'Write tests for these phases' appears only when `item.ask_tests` is true. The checkbox 'Write the documentation book' appears only when `item.ask_docs` is true. If both are false, the block says that the request already decided. Both boxes start unchecked, and the card says that leaving both unchecked finishes now. `closingAnswer` forces `tests` and `docs` to `false` for a question that nobody asked. The button is **Confirm the closing choices**. ## Findings and security blocks `ReviewFindings` and `FactFindings` render finding tables. The severity chip uses the tone `bad` for `BLOCKER` and `HIGH`, `warn` for `MEDIUM`, and `neutral` for other values. `BlockerNotice` is not a gate. It is a `bad` banner with no dismiss action, because only a passing review clears a security block. `activeSecurityBlocks` finds the active blocks in the events. ## Summary text of answered gates `answerSummary` builds the one-line text for an answered card: - `questions`: `: ` for each question, joined with a semicolon. - `approval`: 'Approved', or 'Changes requested: '. - `choice`: the button label of the option. If text exists, `: ` follows. For `budget_reached` with a valid amount, the form is `

sections.title: Shortcuts, command palette, keyboard lock, and push install
sections.summary: Explains the shortcut model and its storage, the palette rows and their ranking, keyboard lock, app install, and the push client with the service worker.
sections.body:
## Why the console has its own shortcut system

A browser keeps many key combinations for itself, for example Ctrl+W and Ctrl+Tab. Users also want their own keys, two-stroke sequences, and different keys in different workspaces. A shortcut must never fire while the user types text in a field or an editor. The console solves these needs with a shortcut model in `web/src/lib/shortcuts.ts`, a global key handler in `WorkspaceShell`, and a settings editor. This page also covers the command palette, keyboard lock, app install, and the push client. The phone shell has no shortcut handler and no palette.

A **stroke** is one key press with its modifiers. A **sequence** is two strokes pressed one after the other. A **binding** is the stroke or sequence that is assigned to an **action**.

## Actions and default bindings

The console has 11 actions. `mod` is Meta on Mac and iOS, and Ctrl elsewhere (`isMac` tests `navigator.platform`).

| Action id | Label | Default | What the shell does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `palette` | Open the command palette | `mod+k` | Toggles the palette. |
| `dock` | Toggle the quick-question dock | `mod+/` | Toggles the dock. |
| `sidebar` | Toggle the sidebar | `mod+b` | Toggles the sidebar. |
| `files` | Show the Files tab | `shift+meta+e` on Mac, `ctrl+shift+e` elsewhere | Opens the sidebar on Files. If Files already shows, it switches to Sessions. |
| `next-tab` | Next tab | `ctrl+Tab` | Activates the next tab in strip order, with wrap. Needs 2 or more tabs. |
| `prev-tab` | Previous tab | `ctrl+shift+Tab` | Activates the previous tab, with wrap. |
| `close-tab` | Close the focused tab | `mod+w`, marked `reserved` | Closes the active tab. |
| `new-task` | New task | none | Opens `ws:overview`. |
| `settings` | Open settings | none | Opens `ws:settings`. |
| `theme` | Toggle light and dark theme | none | Toggles the theme. |
| `keyboard-lock` | Lock or release keyboard shortcuts in fullscreen | none | Toggles keyboard lock. |

The flag `reserved` marks a default that the console claims only when the browser lets the combination through. The reason for `close-tab`: the browser keeps Meta+W for its own tabs unless the keyboard is locked or Ostra runs as an installed app.

## Strokes

A stroke is the text `ctrl+alt+shift+meta+<key>`. The modifiers appear in this fixed order, and `<key>` follows. `strokeOf(event)` builds it:

- It returns `null` for a lone modifier key.
- A space is `Space`.
- A one-character ASCII key without Alt or Shift uses the lower-case character.
- With Alt or Shift, or for a character outside ASCII, the physical key (`event.code`) names the stroke. The code maps `KeyA` to `KeyZ`, `Digit0` to `Digit9`, and the keys Slash, Backslash, Period, Comma, Semicolon, Quote, BracketLeft, BracketRight, Minus, Equal, and Backquote. The reason: Alt+K types another character on a Mac, so the typed character cannot name the key.
- The keys `Dead`, `Unidentified`, `Process`, `CapsLock`, `NumLock`, `ScrollLock`, and the empty key use the code. Other named keys use `event.key`.

`parseStroke` rejects an empty key, a modifier name, a key longer than 24 characters, and a key that contains `+` unless the key is `+` itself.

## How the console matches a key press

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Key event"] --> B{"Lone modifier?"}
    B -->|yes| X["Ignore"]
    B -->|no| C{"Typing in a field, no pending stroke, text stroke?"}
    C -->|yes| X
    C -->|no| D{"Pending stroke younger than 1500 ms and a sequence matches?"}
    D -->|yes| E["Run the action"]
    D -->|no| F{"Stroke starts a sequence?"}
    F -->|yes| G["Store pending stroke and consume the event"]
    F -->|no| H{"One-stroke binding matches?"}
    H -->|yes| E
    H -->|no| I["Do nothing"]
```

`matchStroke(bindings, pending, stroke, now, claimReserved)` considers a binding only if it is not `reserved`, or if `claimReserved` is true. `claimReserved` is true when keyboard lock is on or `runningAsApp()` is true. The `consume` field of the result decides whether the handler calls `preventDefault`. A pending stroke older than `SEQUENCE_MS` (1500 ms) is ignored.

### The typing guard

The global `keydown` listener skips a stroke when three conditions are true: the stroke would type text (`typesText`: no Ctrl, Alt, or Meta, and not an F key), the target is editable, and no sequence is pending. The editable targets are `input`, `textarea`, `select`, `contenteditable` elements, `.monaco-editor`, and `.ex-xterm`. Because of this guard, a shortcut without a modifier key works only outside fields. One more rule: Ctrl+W inside the terminal (`.ex-xterm`) stays with the shell, because it deletes a word there.

## Customize shortcuts

The Settings tab `shortcuts` (`ShortcutsSection`) edits the bindings. Each row has the buttons Set or Change, Remove, and Reset. The panel has Reset all when overrides exist.

1. Press **Set** or **Change**. The row waits for keys. Console shortcuts do not fire during this time.
2. Press one combination, or press a first stroke and a second stroke. If no second stroke follows within `SECOND_STROKE_MS` (1200 ms), the first stroke becomes a one-stroke shortcut. Pressing Esc with no stroke cancels. A blur ends the recording.
3. `conflicts(bindings, action, keys)` looks for other actions with the same keys, or with a first stroke that equals the whole binding of the other action. If a conflict exists, a warning banner offers **Use it here** and **Cancel**. **Use it here** unbinds the other actions. An action with a default becomes `null`. An action without a default loses its override.
4. After a save, the section shows notes. `reservedBy` returns `browser` or `system` for combinations that the browser or the operating system usually handle first. A first stroke that types text gets the note that it works only outside text fields and editors.

**Remove** stores `null` for an action with a default (the action is unbound). It drops the override of an action without a default. **Reset** drops one override. **Reset all** removes the stored entry.

The reserved lists are:

| Owner | Mac | Other systems |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `browser` | `meta+w`, `meta+t`, `meta+n`, `meta+q`, `shift+meta+t`, `shift+meta+n`, `shift+meta+w` | `ctrl+w`, `ctrl+t`, `ctrl+n`, `ctrl+shift+t`, `ctrl+shift+n`, `ctrl+shift+w` |
| `browser` on all systems | `ctrl+Tab`, `ctrl+shift+Tab`, `ctrl+PageUp`, `ctrl+PageDown` | The same four strokes. |
| `system` | `meta+Tab`, `shift+meta+Tab`, `meta+Space`, `ctrl+Space`, `meta+h`, `meta+m`, `ctrl+ArrowUp` | `alt+Tab`, `alt+shift+Tab`, `alt+F4`, `ctrl+alt+Delete`, `ctrl+alt+ArrowLeft`, `ctrl+alt+ArrowRight`, and any stroke with the Meta key |

### Where shortcuts are stored

The browser keeps shortcuts in `localStorage` under `ostra.shortcuts.<ws>`. The value is `{ v: 1, bindings: { <action>: [stroke] or [stroke, stroke] or null } }`. Only the overrides are stored. If no override exists, the code removes the key. If `localStorage` throws, an in-memory map keeps the value until the page reloads. `parseOverrides` drops anything that is not valid: bad JSON, an unknown action, or keys that are not a list of 1 or 2 valid strokes. The user can edit the value by hand, so the parser trusts nothing.

`useShortcuts(ws)` reads the value with `useSyncExternalStore`. It listens to the custom event `ostra-shortcuts` and the `storage` event. A change therefore applies at once in every component and in other browser tabs. Shortcuts belong to one workspace and one browser. The server does not store them.

## Keyboard lock

Keyboard lock sends browser-reserved combinations to the console. `keyboardLockSupported()` is true when `navigator.keyboard.lock` is a function and `requestFullscreen` exists. This is true in Chromium browsers. The API works only in fullscreen.

`useKeyboardLock` works in these steps:

1. `lock()` enters fullscreen with `{ navigationUI: hide }` when the page is not already fullscreen.
2. It calls `navigator.keyboard.lock()` and then sets `locked`.
3. If an error occurs, it leaves the fullscreen that it entered.
4. When fullscreen ends (the `fullscreenchange` event with no `fullscreenElement`), the hook calls `unlock()` and clears `locked`.

The code comment says that holding Escape or leaving fullscreen releases the lock. While `locked` is true, the shell passes `claimReserved = true` to `matchStroke`, so `close-tab` and the browser combinations reach the console. The status bar shows 'Shortcuts locked'. A click on it releases the lock. The user can also toggle the lock with the `keyboard-lock` action or with the palette command.

## Install the console as an app

An installed app runs in its own window, and the browser passes most of its shortcuts to the page. `runningAsApp()` is true for the display modes `standalone` and `window-controls-overlay`, and for `navigator.standalone`. It also sets `claimReserved`.

`watchInstall()` runs once at boot. It prevents the default prompt, keeps the `beforeinstallprompt` event, and on `appinstalled` clears the event and marks the app as installed. `useInstall()` returns one of three states: `installed`, `ready` (a deferred prompt exists), or `manual`. `install()` calls `prompt()` and waits for `userChoice`. If the outcome is not `accepted`, the code keeps the event for another try. It returns `false` when no event exists.

The Shortcuts page shows an info banner 'Some combos stay with the browser or the system' with the button 'Install Ostra as an app', unless the app is already installed. When `install()` returns `false`, the page shows `manualInstallHint()`:

| Condition | Hint |
| --- | --- |
| The page is not a secure context | Browsers install apps only from an HTTPS address or localhost. |
| Firefox | Firefox does not install web apps. Use Chrome, Edge, or Safari. |
| Safari on iPhone or iPad | Tap Share, then Add to Home Screen. |
| Safari on Mac | Choose File, then Add to Dock. |
| Other browsers | Use the install icon or the browser menu item Install Ostra. |

`web/public/manifest.webmanifest` makes the page installable: `display` is `standalone`, `start_url` and `scope` are `/`, and the colors are `#1f1f1d`. It lists `favicon.svg`, `icon-192.png`, and `icon-512.png`.

## Command palette

The palette is a dialog that finds any resource or command by name. Three files share the work:

- `design/src/components/navigation/CommandPalette.tsx` draws the dialog. It does not know the data.
- `web/src/shell/Palette.tsx` supplies the rows, with debounced server search.
- `web/src/lib/palette.ts` holds the pure functions.

### Open and use the palette

The action `palette`, the title bar button, and the 'Nothing open' hint open the palette. The dialog renders in a portal on `document.body`. It is 560 px wide (at most `calc(100vw - 32px)`) and 12vh from the top. The input row is 44 px high, the result list has a maximum height of 360 px, and each row is 32 px high. A focus trap holds the focus, and the focus returns to the previous element on close.

- ArrowDown and ArrowUp move the highlight and stop at the ends. They do not wrap.
- Enter opens the highlighted row.
- Escape closes the palette and stops the event.
- A click on the scrim closes the palette.
- An empty result shows 'Nothing matches “<query>”.'
- The placeholder is 'Go to a session, execution, artifact or setting…'.

### Which rows appear

`mergePalette(query, hits, local, commands)` builds the list:

1. **Empty query.** The rows are the local rows without the group Files, then the commands. `localItems` builds the local rows from data that the shell already holds: sessions (`session:<id>`, label `title: request`, status hint), executions (`exec:<id>`, label `<Agent> · <run label> in <project>`), artifacts, and projects.
2. **Query with a server answer.** The rows are the server hits, sorted by `score` from high to low. `hitToItem` maps each kind to a group and an icon.
3. **Query without a server answer.** While the request loads, `hits` is `null` and the console filters the local rows with `filterPaletteItems` (a case-insensitive substring match over label, hint, and group).
4. **Failed search.** `useSearch` sets `unavailable`. The palette then loads the file index of the project of the Files tab (`useFileIndex`) and adds those paths to the local rows.
5. **Commands.** The commands that match the query follow the result rows.

The function keeps at most `MAX_ROWS` (200) result rows before the commands. It removes duplicate ids, and the first row wins. It sorts the rows by group in this order: Sessions, Executions, Artifacts, Projects, Files, Lessons, Settings, Workspace, Actions. Groups that are not in the list go last. Rows keep their order inside a group, because the sort is stable. The search request has the limit 30 and the debounce 100 ms.

| Kind of hit | Group |
| --- | --- |
| `session` | Sessions |
| `execution` | Executions |
| `artifact` | Artifacts |
| `project` | Projects |
| `file` | Files |
| `lesson` | Lessons |
| `setting` | Settings |

### Commands

`paletteCommands(hints, lock)` returns these rows. Each row shows the current shortcut of the user as its hint.

| Row | Id | Group |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New task | `ws:overview` | Workspace |
| New workspace… | `cmd:new-workspace` | Workspace |
| Add project… | `cmd:add-project` | Workspace |
| Cost | `ws:cost` | Workspace |
| Settings | `ws:settings` | Workspace |
| Keyboard shortcuts | `setting:shortcuts` | Workspace |
| Ask a quick question | `cmd:dock` | Actions |
| Toggle light and dark theme | `cmd:theme` | Actions |
| Lock keyboard shortcuts in fullscreen, or Release keyboard shortcuts | `cmd:keyboard-lock` | Actions |

The last row appears only when the Keyboard Lock API exists. The hint of 'New task' is its shortcut, or the text `overview` when the action has no binding.

### Select a row

`paletteTarget(id)` decides what a selection does. An id that starts with `cmd:` runs a shell command. An id that starts with `lesson:` opens `ws:memory` with the id as anchor, and the screen selects that lesson. An id that starts with `setting:` opens `ws:settings` with the id as anchor, and the screen opens the tab and marks the field. Any other id opens that resource.

```ts
export function paletteTarget(id: string): PaletteTarget {
  if (id.startsWith("cmd:")) return { kind: "command", command: id.slice(4) };
  if (id.startsWith("lesson:")) return { kind: "open", id: "ws:memory", anchor: id };
  if (id.startsWith("setting:")) return { kind: "open", id: "ws:settings", anchor: id };
  return { kind: "open", id };
}
```

The phone `SearchSheet` uses the same functions. The page *Console structure, routing, tabs, and the shell* describes its differences.

## Push notifications in the browser

A user who leaves the console open in a background tab must learn that a gate waits. Web Push solves this need. The browser side has three parts: `web/src/lib/push.ts`, the settings panel, and the service worker `web/public/sw.js`. The page *External MCP client, OAuth, and Web Push* explains how the server sends a push message.

### Subscribe a browser

At boot, `registerServiceWorker()` registers `/sw.js`. It returns `null` if the browser has no service workers or if the registration fails. The panel Settings, Notifications has a workspace-wide switch (`form.push`) and two buttons for the current browser. The switch text says that push messages go out when a gate waits, a session completes, a phase is blocked, or a harness needs login. The switch applies to every browser that subscribed.

`enablePush()` runs these steps:

1. If `pushSupported()` is false (no `serviceWorker`, `PushManager`, or `Notification`), return 'This browser does not support push notifications.'
2. Call `Notification.requestPermission()`. If the answer is not `granted`, return 'Notifications are blocked for this site. Allow them in the browser's site settings.'
3. Call `api.info()` for `vapid_public_key`. If it is empty, return 'The server has no push key configured.'
4. Reuse the existing subscription, or call `pushManager.subscribe` with `userVisibleOnly: true` and the key converted from URL-safe base64.
5. POST `{ endpoint, keys: { p256dh, auth } }` to `/api/push/subscribe`. The keys use URL-safe base64 without padding.
6. Return `null` on success. A thrown error shows its message in the panel.

The status text of the panel is 'This browser does not support push notifications.', 'Checking…', 'Subscribed. It receives notifications.', or 'Not subscribed.' The button **Enable in this browser** is disabled when the browser is subscribed. The button **Disable in this browser** is disabled when it is not.

`disablePush()` calls `unsubscribe()` on the subscription of the browser only. The client has no call that removes the subscription from the server. The mock `info` returns an empty key, so mock mode cannot subscribe.

### Receive a notification

The service worker installs with `skipWaiting` and takes control with `clients.claim`. It has no fetch handler, so it caches nothing. On a `push` event, it reads JSON `{ title, body, url, tag? }`. The title defaults to 'Ostra' and the URL defaults to `/`. If the data is not JSON, the text becomes the body. The notification uses `/favicon.svg` as icon and badge. A `tag` makes notifications with the same tag replace each other.

On a click, the worker closes the notification. It then takes the first open window of the same origin, focuses it, and navigates it to the URL. If no such window exists, it opens a new one. The server builds the URL as `/s/<session id>`, without a hash. The route `/s/:id` reaches `SessionRedirect`, which finds the workspace. The server limits the plaintext of a payload to 3993 bytes (`MAX_PLAINTEXT` in `crates/ostra-notify/src/lib.rs`), because push services accept at most 4096 bytes of body.

## What happens when

- **A key press has no binding.** The handler does nothing, and the browser handles the key.
- **The user types in a field.** Strokes without Ctrl, Alt, or Meta do not run shortcuts.
- **The second stroke comes after 1500 ms.** The first stroke expires, and the second stroke is matched alone.
- **Two actions share a binding.** The settings editor warns and offers to unbind the other action.
- **The browser keeps a reserved combination.** The console never sees it, unless keyboard lock or the installed app is active.
- **`localStorage` is unavailable.** Shortcuts live in memory until the page reloads.
- **The Keyboard Lock API is missing.** The palette hides its command, and the status bar never shows the lock.
- **The server search fails.** The palette filters local rows and adds project files.
- **The user denies the notification permission.** `enablePush` returns the blocked message.

## Limits and defaults

| Name | Value | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SEQUENCE_MS` | 1500 ms | `web/src/lib/shortcuts.ts` |
| `SECOND_STROKE_MS` | 1200 ms | `web/src/screens/workspace/ShortcutsSection.tsx` |
| Maximum key length | 24 characters | `parseStroke` in `web/src/lib/shortcuts.ts` |
| `MAX_ROWS` | 200 result rows | `web/src/lib/palette.ts` |
| Palette width and list height | 560 px and 360 px | `design/src/components/navigation/CommandPalette.tsx` |
| Search limit and debounce | 30 results and 100 ms | `web/src/lib/live.ts` |
| Push plaintext limit | 3993 bytes | `crates/ostra-notify/src/lib.rs` |

sections.title: Design system: tokens, components, and focus rules
sections.summary: Explains the tokens, the theme switch, the core and feedback components, the keyboard contracts, and the steps to add a component or a screen.
sections.body:
## What the design package does The package `@ostra/design` (`design/`) holds the tokens and React components that the console uses. Its description also names a separate site as a consumer. The folder `site/` does not exist in this checkout, so this book describes only the console as a consumer. Without one shared package, each screen would define its own colors and keyboard behavior, and the two themes would drift apart. This page covers the package surface, the tokens, the theme switch, the components, the keyboard and focus contracts, the docs renderer export, the gallery, the tests, and the steps to add a component or a screen. The package has no README and no contributor guide. The steps on this page come from the code layout and from `web/src/screens/README.md`. ## Package surface `design/package.json` declares the package `@ostra/design` 0.1.0 as private ESM. It has these exports: | Export | File | Content | | --- | --- | --- | | `.` | `src/index.ts` | Imports `index.css` and re-exports every component, its prop types, `cx`, the focus helpers, and `activateOnKey`. | | `./index.css` | `src/index.css` | Fonts, tokens, base rules, component classes, and brand CSS. | | `./gallery` | `src/Gallery.tsx` | The development gallery. | | `./docs` | `src/docs/index.ts` | The docs renderer: `Docs`, `Markdown`, `Diagram`, `MAX_HITS`, and the page types. | | `./docs.css` | `src/docs/docs.css` | Styles of the docs renderer. | | `./docs-standalone.css` | `src/docs/standalone.css` | Color, type, and spacing tokens plus `docs.css`, without fonts. | The dependencies are `lucide-react`, `mermaid`, three `mdast-util` packages, `micromark-extension-gfm`, and the two `@fontsource` packages. React and React DOM are peer dependencies (`^19.3.0`). The console imports `@ostra/design/index.css` in `main.tsx`, and importing `@ostra/design` also loads it. ## Tokens The CSS loads in this order (`src/index.css`): `fonts.css`, `colors.css`, `typography.css`, `spacing.css`, `effects.css`, `base.css`, `components.css`, and `components/brand/brand.css`. The header comment says that the token files come verbatim from the Claude Design project, except `fonts.css`, which loads bundled fonts in place of Google Fonts. The fonts are bundled because Ostra runs offline. ### Colors Raw scales exist for warm grays (`--gray-950` to `--gray-10`), the Ostra blue (`--blue-200` to `--blue-950`), and four status hues: green, amber, red, and violet. Components use only the semantic roles: | Role group | Tokens | | --- | --- | | Surfaces | `--surface-chrome` (title bar, status bar, docks), `--surface-panel` (sidebar), `--surface-editor` (center pane), `--surface-raised` (cards), `--surface-sunken`, `--surface-overlay` (popovers, palette, dialogs), `--surface-terminal`, `--surface-hover`, `--surface-active`, `--surface-selected`, `--surface-scrim` | | Borders | `--border-subtle`, `--border-default`, `--border-strong`, `--border-focus` | | Text | `--text-primary`, `--text-secondary`, `--text-muted`, `--text-disabled`, `--text-on-accent`, `--text-link` | | Accent | `--accent`, `--accent-hover`, `--accent-soft`, `--accent-fg` | | Status | `--ok`, `--warn`, `--bad`, `--info`, each with a `-soft` background | | Code and diff | `--code-bg`, `--diff-add-bg`, `--diff-add-fg`, `--diff-del-bg`, `--diff-del-fg` | | Syntax | `--syntax-keyword`, `--syntax-string`, `--syntax-number`, `--syntax-fn`, `--syntax-comment` | | Terminal | `--term-*`. These values are the same in both themes, because the terminal pane is always dark. | The UI uses one status mapping everywhere: running is accent, waiting is warn, completed is ok, failed and stalled are bad, and handoff and info are violet (`--info`). ### Type, space, shape, and motion - **Fonts.** `--font-sans` is IBM Plex Sans and `--font-mono` is JetBrains Mono, both with system fallbacks. `fonts.css` has 42 `@font-face` rules in woff2 format with `font-display: swap`, one rule for each unicode-range subset. They are generated from the `@fontsource` packages. Regenerate the file when those packages change. - **Type scale.** `--text-2xs` 10.5 px, `--text-xs` 11.5 px, `--text-sm` 12 px, `--text-base` 13 px (the UI base), `--text-md` 14 px (prose), `--text-lg` 16 px, `--text-xl` 20 px, `--text-2xl` 26 px, and `--text-code` 12.5 px. The line heights are 1.25, 1.45, and 1.6. The weights are 400, 500, and 600. The roles `--type-ui`, `--type-prose`, `--type-title`, `--type-heading`, `--type-label`, and `--type-code` combine them. - **Space.** `--space-0` to `--space-12` run from 0 to 48 px with half steps (2, 6, 10, and 14 px). Control heights are 22 px (`--control-h-sm`), 28 px (`--control-h`), and 32 px (`--control-h-lg`). Other chrome sizes: row 26 px, title bar 36 px, tab bar 34 px, status bar 24 px, sidebar 264 px, dock 380 px, `--content-max` 1080 px, and `--prose-max` 760 px. - **Shape.** The radii are 3, 4, 6, and 8 px, and a pill of 999 px. Elevation uses borders first. The shadows `--shadow-popover` and `--shadow-dialog` appear only on floating layers, and they are lighter in the light theme. - **Motion.** The durations are 60 ms (`--dur-instant`), 100 ms, 160 ms, and 240 ms (`--dur-slow`). The easing curves are `--ease-out` and `--ease-in-out`. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, `base.css` sets `animation-duration` and `transition-duration` to 1 ms with `!important`, and `animation-delay` to 0 ms. The console shell overrides `--sidebar-w` and `--dock-w` on its root element with the widths that the user chose. ## The theme switch Dark is the default theme. The attribute `data-theme=light` on the `html` element selects the light theme. The block `[data-theme=light]` in `colors.css` overrides the semantic color tokens, and the same block in `effects.css` overrides the shadows. The console sets the attribute with `applyTheme`. The gallery removes the attribute to show the dark theme. The terminal tokens never change, because harness terminal output must stay on a dark background. The page *Console structure, routing, tabs, and the shell* explains how the console picks and stores the theme. ## Components Components live in `design/src/components/`. Each is a function component with an exported `Props` interface. The doc comments of the props state the usage rules. A component renders `os-*` classes from `tokens/components.css` (1686 lines) and joins class names with `cx`. Plain HTML can also use these classes. | Group | Components | | --- | --- | | `brand` | `LiveMark` (eight arcs and a center pearl, with the states `done`, `run`, `wait`, `fail`, `off`), the constants `REST` and `IDLE`, `MARK_ARCS` (8), and `markSvg` for favicons. `markSvg` uses literal colors, because a favicon cannot read CSS variables. | | `core` | `Button`, `IconButton`, `Icon`, `Kbd`, and the icon registry `icons.ts`. | | `data` | `CodeView`, `Panel`, `SectionLabel`, `Table`. | | `feedback` | `Banner`, `Chip`, `Dialog`, `Spinner`, `StatusChip`, `StatusDot`. | | `forms` | `Checkbox`, `Combobox`, `FolderPicker`, `Input`, `Select`, `Switch`. | | `navigation` | `Breadcrumbs`, `CommandPalette`, `ContextMenu`, `FileTree`, `Menu`, `Stepper`, `Tabs`, `TreeItem`, `TreeSection`. | | `pipeline` | `Decision`, `DiffView`, `ExecutionGroup`, `GateCard`, `LaneStepper`, `PhaseDag`, `PhaseNode`, `StageRow`, `Terminal`, `ToolCall`. | ### Core components - **`Button`.** The `variant` is `default`, `primary` (the one forward action, such as Approve or Start), `ghost` (toolbars and secondary actions), or `danger` (Deny, Cancel execution). The `size` is `sm` (22 px), `md` (28 px), or `lg` (32 px). The props `icon` and `iconRight` take Lucide names. `kbd` shows a key hint. `active` sets `aria-pressed`. `type` defaults to `button`, so a button never submits a form by accident. - **`IconButton`.** The prop `label` is required. It becomes both `aria-label` and `title`. The defaults are `ghost` and `md`. - **`Icon`.** It draws a Lucide icon at stroke 1.75. The default size is 16 px. Use 14 px in dense rows and 12 px inside chips. The icon inherits `currentColor`. It has `aria-hidden` unless `title` is set, and then it has `role=img`. - **`Kbd`.** It renders each key as a `kbd` element with the class `os-kbd`. Pass `keys` or children. - **`ICONS`.** `icons.ts` maps kebab-case names to Lucide components, and `IconName` is `keyof typeof ICONS`. An unknown name is a type error. The file comment says that an explicit map keeps the bundle to the glyphs that the design uses. `ICON_NAMES` lists the names. ### Feedback components - **`Banner`.** The `tone` is `warn` (default), `bad`, `info`, or `neutral`. Each tone has a default icon. `bad` has `role=alert`, and the other tones have `role=status`. `actions` appear on the right. A security block never gets a dismiss action. - **`Chip`.** The tones are `neutral` (default), `accent`, `ok`, `warn`, `bad`, and `info`. `mono` is for ids, executors, models, and rule names. `outline` draws a border only. An icon is 11 px. - **`Dialog`.** The default `width` is 560. `onClose` wires the close button, Escape, and a click on the scrim. A dialog without `onClose` must be answered: it has no close button, and Escape does nothing. The scrim closes the dialog only when the mouse press and the click both land on the scrim. A drag that ends outside a text field therefore does not close the dialog. It renders in a portal on `document.body`, or inline (no scrim and no fixed position) for docs and cards. It sets `aria-modal` and `aria-labelledby`. `initialFocus` takes a ref. Otherwise the first focusable element gets the focus. - **`Spinner`.** The default size is 12 px, with `role=status` and `aria-label=Loading`. - **`StatusDot`.** The default size is 7 px. `pulse` marks a live state, and `hollow` marks a pending state. - **`StatusChip(kind, status)`.** The kinds `session`, `execution`, `stage`, `phase`, and `init` map backend strings to tones. Examples: session `running` is accent, `waiting` is warn, `completed` is ok, `failed` and `stalled` are bad, and `paused` is neutral. Execution `stuck` and `interrupted` are warn, `handoff` and `waiting` are info, `error` and `denied` are bad, and `cancelled` is neutral. An unknown value is neutral. Labels: session `waiting` shows 'Waiting for you', init `not_initialized` shows 'Not initialized', init `missing` shows 'Folder missing'. Other values show the text with a capital letter and spaces for underscores. `statusTone(kind, status)` is exported so that rows and dots match the chip. ### Data and pipeline components used by the console `Panel` is the only card shape. It has an optional 36 px header with an icon, a title, a subtitle, and actions. It has the tones `highlight`, `warn`, and `bad`. `Table` is a dense data table. A row with `onRowClick` is focusable, and Enter opens it only when the row itself has focus. `GateCard` is the shell of every gate. It has an icon for each kind (`KIND_ICON`) and the chips 'Waiting for you' and 'Answered by you' or 'Answered by Ostra (YOLO)'. It shows the form and the actions while open, and the answer and the reason when answered. Unknown kinds use the icon `circle-pause`. The page *Gate forms, book reader, and HTML export* explains the forms inside it. ## Keyboard and focus rules ### The global focus ring `base.css` sets `:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: var(--ring-focus); }`. `--ring-focus` is a 1 px line in `--border-focus` plus a 3 px halo of the same color at 28 percent. Inputs use `:focus-within` on their wrapper. Checks and switches style the box next to the input on `input:focus-visible`. ### The helpers - **`focusables(root)`** returns the elements that match `a[href]`, `button:not([disabled])`, enabled `input` (not hidden), `select`, and `textarea`, and `[tabindex]` other than `-1`. It skips elements inside `[inert]`. - **`useFocusTrap(ref, active, initial?)`** remembers the focused element when `active` becomes true. Unless the focus is already inside, it focuses `initial`, else the first focusable element, else the container (with `preventScroll`). On deactivate, it restores the focus to the remembered element if it is still connected. The returned `keydown` handler wraps Tab: Shift+Tab on the first element goes to the last, and Tab on the last goes to the first. If no focusable element exists, Tab is blocked. `Dialog` (when not inline) and `CommandPalette` use it. - **`arrowIndex(key, index, count, orientation, wrap = true)`** returns the next index for ArrowDown or ArrowRight (next), ArrowUp or ArrowLeft (previous), Home (0), and End (the last). It wraps at the ends unless `wrap` is false. It returns `null` for other keys or when `count` is 0. - **`activateOnKey(fn)`** is a `keydown` handler for clickable elements with `role=button` that are not buttons (`ToolCall` uses it). It runs `fn` on Enter or Space, and only when `event.target` is the element itself. A key typed in a nested control is therefore not taken. ```ts export function arrowIndex(key: string, index: number, count: number, orientation: "vertical" | "horizontal", wrap = true): number | null { if (count === 0) return null; ... if (key === next) return index + 1 < count ? index + 1 : wrap ? 0 : index; if (key === prev) return index > 0 ? index - 1 : wrap ? count - 1 : index; if (key === "Home") return 0; if (key === "End") return count - 1; return null; } ``` ### Keyboard contract of each component | Component | Keys | | --- | --- | | `Tabs` | Roving `tabindex` on the selected tab. Arrow keys, Home, and End move the focus and select. Enter or Space selects. Delete closes a tab in the `bar` variant when `onClose` is set. Ctrl or Meta plus Shift plus Left or Right moves a tab when `onMove` is set. The wheel scrolls a wide strip sideways, except in the `segmented` variant. | | `LaneStepper` | A tab list of nine lanes. Arrow keys, Home, and End select a lane. | | `Menu` | The focus moves to the first item on open. Arrow keys, Home, and End move with wrap. Enter or Space selects and closes. Escape closes and stops the event. Tab closes. The focus returns to the trigger only when it fell to `document.body`. | | `ContextMenu` | A `Menu` at a viewport point, with an 8 px margin. | | `Combobox` | ArrowDown opens the list and moves. ArrowUp moves. Enter picks the highlighted item, or calls `onSubmit`. Escape closes only when the list is open. | | `CommandPalette` | ArrowDown and ArrowUp stop at the ends. Enter opens. Escape closes. | | `TreeItem` | ArrowUp and ArrowDown move among the `treeitem` rows of the tree, without wrap. ArrowRight on a collapsed row and ArrowLeft on an expanded row call `onToggle`. Enter or Space activates. | | `Table` | A row with `onRowClick` is focusable. Enter opens it when the row itself has focus. | | `Dialog` | Escape closes only with `onClose`. Tab stays inside. | The reasons: all screens get the same keyboard behavior without screen code, a trap keeps the focus inside a modal and returns the user to the previous place, and the target checks keep nested inputs working. The Biome accessibility rules (`a11y`) are off in `biome.json`. The components and their tests enforce these contracts, not lint. The tests are `feedback.test.tsx`, `forms.test.tsx`, and `navigation.test.tsx`. Run them with `npm test` in `design/`. ## The docs renderer export `@ostra/design/docs` is a Markdown renderer that the console uses for documentation books. `Markdown` renders the blocks of a page. It never renders raw HTML except `
`. It renders an image only when the image is in the `images` map. It turns an unsafe link scheme into plain text. `Diagram` draws a mermaid block in strict mode and shows the source if the block fails. `Docs` builds pages, anchors, links, and the search index. The page *Gate forms, book reader, and HTML export* explains these rules and the limits in detail. ## The gallery and the tests `design/src/Gallery.tsx` shows each component in all its variants on seven cards: Core, Forms, Feedback, Navigation, Data, Pipeline, and Icons. It has a dark and a light toggle. The console routes it at `/_design` only when `import.meta.env.DEV` is true, so it never ships in the production bundle. The design tests use vitest with jsdom and Testing Library (`design/vitest.config.ts`). `feedback.test.tsx` covers `Dialog`: Escape, the close button, the scrim rule, a dialog without `onClose`, and focus move, trap, and restore. ## Add a design component These steps come from the code layout. Do them in this order: 1. Create `design/src/components//.tsx`. Use one of the seven groups. 2. Export a function component and a `Props` interface. Write a doc comment for each prop. 3. Join class names with `cx` and render `os-` classes. 4. Reuse `Icon`, `useFocusTrap`, `arrowIndex`, and `activateOnKey`. Do not write new keyboard code, because the shared helpers keep the contracts equal. 5. Add the `os-*` rules to `design/src/tokens/components.css`. Use only tokens (colors, `--space-*`, `--radius-*`, `--dur-*`), so that both themes work. 6. Add keyframes to `base.css` only when other components share them. 7. Export the component and its prop types from `design/src/index.ts`. The package root exports only this file. 8. If the component needs a new icon, add the Lucide import and a kebab-case entry to `ICONS` in `core/icons.ts`. 9. Add the component, in each variant, to the matching card in `design/src/Gallery.tsx`. 10. Add a test to `feedback.test.tsx`, `forms.test.tsx`, or `navigation.test.tsx`. 11. Run `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, and `npm run check` in `design/`. ## Add a console screen The file `web/src/screens/README.md` is the only written contract for screens. It has two errors: it lists `pin(id)` on `useNav()` (the interface has `keep`), and it omits `DependencyFileScreen`. The steps below come from the README and from the switches in the code. 1. Create `web/src/screens/Screen.tsx`. Accept `{ ws }` and the id props. Fill the center pane. 2. Load data with `api` and the live hooks. Open other resources with `useNav().open`. Open list rows with `{ preview: true }`, and open explicit actions in a normal tab. 3. Add a resource variant in `web/src/lib/resource.ts`. For a workspace page, add the name to `WorkspacePage` and `PAGES`. For a new type, add a `Resource` variant and a case in `parseResource`, `resourceId`, `resourcePath`, and `resourceFromPath`. 4. Add a child route under `/w/:ws` in `routes` in `web/src/App.tsx` if the URL has a new first segment. The `*` child already serves other paths, as it does for `d/:key`. 5. Add a case to `ScreenFor` in `web/src/screens/index.tsx` with `key={id}`, and export the screen. Add the id prefix to `selfScrolling` if the screen scrolls itself. 6. Add the tab label, icon, and crumbs in `resourceMeta` in `web/src/shell/meta.ts`. The switch has no `default` branch, so the compiler reports a missing case. For a workspace page, also add it to `PAGE` in `meta.ts` and to `PAGE_TITLE` in `web/src/mobile/MobileShell.tsx`. 7. Add a case to `MobileScreenFor` in `web/src/mobile/screens.tsx` and a title case in `mobileTitle`. Add the id prefix to `mobileFills` if the screen scrolls itself. A phone screen can reuse the desktop screen, as `DocsScreen` does. 8. If the screen needs a new endpoint, add `#[ts(export)]` to the Rust type and run `cargo test -p ostra-core export_bindings`. Then add `export type *` for it in `web/src/api/types.ts`. 9. Add the function to `httpApi` in `web/src/api/client.ts`. Add the same method to `mockApi` in `web/src/api/mock/mockApi.ts` with fixtures. The type check fails until you do. 10. Load Monaco, the diff view, or xterm only through their lazy wrappers. 11. Add the path to the case list in `web/src/App.test.tsx`. Add unit tests for pure logic. Update the table in `web/src/screens/README.md`. 12. Run `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, and `npm run check` in `web/`. ## What happens when - **A component uses an unknown icon name.** The type check fails, because `IconName` is the key type of `ICONS`. - **A dialog has no `onClose`.** The user must answer it. Escape and the scrim do nothing. - **A gate kind is not in the `GateKind` union.** `GateCard` shows the icon `circle-pause`. - **The user prefers reduced motion.** Animations and transitions take 1 ms. - **A menu loses focus to another element.** The menu does not take the focus back, because it restores focus only when the focus fell to `document.body`. - **A page loads `index.css` without `data-theme`.** The dark theme applies. ## Limits and defaults | Name | Value | Where | | --- | --- | --- | | Control heights | 22, 28, and 32 px | `design/src/tokens/spacing.css` | | `Dialog` width | 560 px default | `design/src/components/feedback/Dialog.tsx` | | `Icon` size and stroke | 16 px and 1.75 | `design/src/components/core/Icon.tsx` | | `Spinner` and `StatusDot` size | 12 px and 7 px | `design/src/components/feedback/` | | Durations | 60, 100, 160, and 240 ms | `design/src/tokens/effects.css` | | Reduced motion duration | 1 ms | `design/src/tokens/base.css` | | `@font-face` rules | 42 | `design/src/tokens/fonts.css` | | `ContextMenu` margin | 8 px | `design/src/components/navigation/ContextMenu.tsx` |
