sections.title: Unit, integration, and conformance tests
sections.summary: Where the Rust tests live, how to run one crate, one file, or one test, and how the conformance harness folds an event history and asserts the planner steps.
sections.body:
## Choose a test layer for a change

A change to the planner, the engine, the policy, or the server can break a rule that the compiler does not check. The project uses separate test layers, because each layer catches a different failure at a different cost. This page covers the layers that `cargo test --workspace` runs. The page "Live evals, the browser security suite, and Windows probes" covers the layers that this command does not run.

| Layer | Location | Command | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Unit tests | Inline `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in a source file, or a sibling `tests.rs` | `cargo test -p <crate>` | Nothing |
| Engine integration tests | `crates/ostra-engine/tests/` (`runner.rs`, `pause.rs`, `recover.rs`) | `cargo test -p ostra-engine --test <file>` | Nothing |
| Server integration tests | `crates/ostra-server/tests/` (`e2e.rs`, `mcp.rs`) | `cargo test -p ostra-server --test <file>` | `web/dist` and `git` |
| Policy tests | `crates/ostra-policy/tests/policy.rs` | `cargo test -p ostra-policy --test policy` | Nothing |
| Sandbox test | `crates/ostra-sandbox/tests/env_scrub.rs` | `cargo test -p ostra-sandbox --test env_scrub` | macOS |
| Planner conformance | `tests/conformance/main.rs` | `cargo test -p ostra-engine --test conformance` | Nothing |

Use the lowest layer that can show the failure:

- To test one function, write a unit test next to it.
- To test what the planner decides after a known history, write a conformance fixture.
- To test the real runner with the store, write an engine integration test.
- To test HTTP, cookie sign-in, and the whole stack, write a server end-to-end test.
- To test one guard decision, write a policy test.

## Run one crate, one file, or one test

The command `cargo test --workspace` runs every layer in the table. It also runs the offline checks of the eval suites. The live evals are `#[ignore]` tests and do not run. Narrow the run with these commands:

```bash
cargo test --workspace
cargo test -p ostra-engine
cargo test -p ostra-engine --test conformance
cargo test -p ostra-engine --test conformance j1_
cargo test -p ostra-policy --test policy build_streak
cargo test -p ostra-server --test e2e yolo_implement_session_end_to_end -- --nocapture
```

The last word before `--` is a substring filter on the test name. Most conformance fixtures start with their rule ID in lower case, so `j1_` runs every fixture of rule group J1. The flag `--nocapture` prints the output of the test, which helps when a test polls a running engine.

Call `cargo fmt --all` before you commit. The repository has no `rustfmt.toml`, so rustfmt uses its defaults.

### What happens when a build step is missing

- If `web/dist` is absent, `ostra-server` does not compile. The file `crates/ostra-server/src/assets.rs` embeds that folder with `#[derive(RustEmbed)]` at compile time. Build the web UI first with `cd web && npm run -s build`, after `npm ci` at the repository root.
- If `git` is not on `PATH`, the offline check of the coordination evals fails, because it copies the repository into a scratch git repository.
- If the platform is not Unix, `e2e.rs` skips the tests that carry `#[cfg(unix)]`, and `test_stage_evals.rs` compiles to nothing.
- A test run in `ostra-core` also writes the TypeScript bindings into `web/src/api/gen`. The page "Build, run, and format" explains this side effect.

## Unit tests next to the code

Most source files hold their unit tests in an inline `#[cfg(test)]` module. Four modules use a sibling file instead: `crates/ostra-agents/src/tests.rs`, `crates/ostra-exec-native/src/tests.rs`, `crates/ostra-sandbox/src/tests.rs`, and `crates/ostra-core/src/doc/tests.rs`. A sibling file keeps a long test module out of the production source.

The crates `ostra-store`, `ostra-providers`, `ostra-code`, and `ostra-mcp` also have integration tests in their own `tests/` folders. The two provider tests that need a live API key carry `#[ignore]` with a reason that names the key variable. The language server tests in `crates/ostra-code/tests/lsp.rs` carry `#[ignore]`, and one of them needs `gopls` on `PATH`. Run an ignored test with `cargo test -p <crate> -- --ignored`.

## Engine integration tests with a scripted executor

The engine tests run a real `Engine` with a real runner and a real `WorkspaceDb`, but they replace everything outside the engine. Without these tests, a bug in the drive loop, the recovery code, or the pause code would appear only in a live session. Each test file defines two stand-ins:

- A `Fake` type implements `Services`. It returns a fixed `GlobalConfig` and `WorkspaceSettings`, hands out the scripted executor, uses `AgentsFactory` as the spawn factory, and answers each judge call from the JSON schema of the call.
- A scripted type implements `Executor`. It returns a canned submit for each agent and writes the files that the submit names.

### Engine test files

| File | Tests | What it proves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `runner.rs` | 5 | An `IMPLEMENT` session under YOLO runs to completion. An init session notifies project changes. Subagents wake each other and pair loops continue. A pinned session holds only its pinned projects (Rule O6). A `DOCS` session writes the book (Rules B1, B5, B6). |
| `pause.rs` | 8 | Pause interrupts a run and resume continues it (Rules P1, P2). Three containment signals pause the session (Rule P3). Context sent now restarts running work (Rules C1, C2). Attached files must be inside a project. Uploads stay in the session. |
| `recover.rs` | 2 | After a restart, a running execution becomes `Interrupted`, keeps its cost, and its step runs again. An offline stop prevents the rerun. |

The test `implement_session_runs_to_completion_under_yolo` is the widest. It creates a session with `yolo: true` and polls `engine.state` until `is_terminal()`, with a 20-second deadline. It then asserts the order of agents: `Explore`, `GenerateSpec`, `FactCheck`, `Plan`, `FactCheck`, `Implementer`, `CodeReviewer`. It also checks that the implementer spawn block holds `Phase file:` and `Report file:` lines, that the status is `Completed`, and that the notice `Session complete` was sent.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Test
    participant Engine
    participant Fake as Fake Services
    participant Exec as Scripted executor
    participant DB as WorkspaceDb
    Test->>Engine: create_session(CreateSession)
    Engine->>Fake: judge(classify schema)
    Fake-->>Engine: category IMPLEMENT
    Engine->>Exec: run(ExecutionSpec)
    Exec-->>Engine: ExecutionResult with submit
    Engine->>DB: append events
    Test->>Engine: state(session id)
    Engine-->>Test: SessionState folded from events
    Test->>DB: events(session id)
    DB-->>Test: stored events for assertions
```

### What happens when an engine test recovers a session

- In `recovery_keeps_usage_and_reruns`, the first engine runs an executor that spends $0.50 and then waits for cancel. A second `Engine` opens the same database file, as a restarted process does, and calls `recover()`. The test expects one `ExecutionFinished` event with status `Interrupted`, a cost of $0.50, and a second `ExecutionStarted` event for the explore step.
- In `offline_stop_prevents_rerun_on_recovery`, the test calls `stop_session_offline` on the database before the second engine starts. The call returns `1`. After `recover()`, the session has `failed` set, only one execution exists, its status is `Cancelled`, and its cost is still $0.50.
- The helper `until` in `pause.rs` polls every 20 ms and panics after 200 polls, which is 4 seconds.
- In `containment_signals_pause_the_session`, the executor emits five refused egress deltas. A refusal of a public host is no signal. The log holds exactly 3 `ContainmentSignal` events and stops at the pause.

## Server end-to-end tests

The file `crates/ostra-server/tests/e2e.rs` runs the whole stack in one process: a real listener on `127.0.0.1`, the REST routes with cookie sign-in, the engine, the native loop, the policy, the tools, and git staging. It has 24 tests. The model is a `ScriptedProvider` registered as `mock`. Its responder `respond` plays each agent: it writes the files of the agent with the Write tool and then calls the submit tool. A second function `judge` answers the judge calls.

The function `boot` starts the server in these steps:

1. Set `OSTRA_CONFIG`, `OSTRA_DATA_DIR`, `OSTRA_MASTER_KEY_FILE`, `OSTRA_SANDBOX_CACHE`, and `OSTRA_MODELS_DEV_URL` (empty) for a temporary root.
2. Save a `GlobalConfig` with all four native tiers set to `mock:m`.
3. Bind `127.0.0.1:0` and call `ostra_server::app::build`.
4. Register the `mock` provider and serve `ostra_server::api::router`.
5. Post the token from `app.auth.sign_in_url()` to `/api/auth/exchange` and expect status `204`. The client keeps the cookie.

The server reads its paths from the process environment. For this reason, each test holds the static `SERIAL` mutex while its server runs, and the tests of this file run one after another. A test that skips `SERIAL` can read the paths of another test.

The tests fall into these groups:

- **Session flow:** `yolo_implement_session_end_to_end`, `ended_sessions_lose_leftover_caches_at_start`, `an_approved_project_is_created_initialized_and_built`, `a_missing_route_is_fixed_in_one_call`.
- **Workspaces and projects:** `setup_wizard_creates_a_workspace_in_one_call`, `deleting_a_workspace_keeps_projects_and_session_folders`, `live_or_starting_work_blocks_removing_a_project_or_the_workspace`, `projects_clone_and_pull_with_a_saved_git_credential`.
- **Approvals and sandbox settings:** `folder_commands_run_only_after_approval`, `a_new_workspace_needs_no_approval_for_its_own_commands`, `a_workspace_network_choice_and_hosts_build_on_the_global_sandbox`.
- **Browser boundary and sign-in:** `the_browser_boundary_refuses_page_content_and_other_sites`, `a_loopback_server_lives_at_its_private_name`, `sign_in_sessions_are_listed_and_revoked`, `the_bridge_socket_serves_only_harness_callbacks`.
- **Files, artifacts, books, skills:** `uploads_are_kept_in_the_session_and_downloadable`, `workspace_artifacts_are_tagged_hidden_edited_and_deleted`, `workspace_books_are_listed_read_and_deleted`, `skills_are_listed_edited_adopted_and_deleted`.
- **Terminal and git:** `terminal_streams_over_the_socket`, `the_git_dock_stages_commits_pushes_and_switches_branches`, `harness_login_runs_in_a_setup_terminal`.
- **Settings and credentials:** `onboarding_flag_and_ui_state_round_trip`, `provider_credentials_saved_from_the_browser`.

The file `crates/ostra-server/tests/mcp.rs` has one test, `workspace_mcp_servers_end_to_end`. It starts a remote MCP server stub with the tools `echo` and `secret`. The stub needs `Bearer static-secret`, or a token from its own authorization server when OAuth is on. The test covers settings, discovery, the status API, the OAuth sign-in through the browser callback, and a native agent that calls a tool of the server.

## Policy and sandbox tests

The file `crates/ostra-policy/tests/policy.rs` has 50 tests. It ports the guard cases of the Ultracode project (scope, bash scope, artifacts, ledgers, tool self-protection, reports, lesson gate, build streak) and adds tests for the permission model. The page "Two layers and the guard catalog" explains the rules that these tests check.

Each test calls `fx()`, which makes a temporary tree under `CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR` with a repository, a workspace, a session directory, a fake `ostra` binary, and a config file. The method `Fx::ctx(agent)` builds an `ExecContext` in `PermissionMode::Bypass` with `enforce_tool_calls: true`. The method `Fx::policy(agent)` wraps it in an `ExecutionPolicy`. Four helpers keep the assertions short:

- `allowed(&policy, &call)` fails when the decision is not an allow.
- `denied(&policy, &call, pattern)` fails when the decision is not a deny or the reason lacks the pattern. It returns the reason.
- `guard_of(&policy, &call)` returns the name of the rule that denied the call.
- `outcome(text)` builds a `ToolOutcome` for `observe`, which feeds the build streak.

The test `build_streak_forces_escalation_at_five` shows the style. It sends five failing build commands. It expects a note after the third failure and lesson recall from the second failure. After the fifth failure, it expects a deny with the text `5 consecutive build or test failures`, and an allow for `cat`. A passing build resets the streak to 0 and sets `lesson_pending`. A timed-out command does not count as evidence.

The file holds one `#[cfg(unix)]` test and eight `#[cfg(windows)]` tests. The Windows tests check spellings of a path, such as junctions, MSYS paths, and PowerShell. They run only on Windows. The helper `shp` makes a path safe for a bash command on both platforms.

The file `crates/ostra-sandbox/tests/env_scrub.rs` has one test and compiles its body only on macOS. The test `startup_env_is_not_readable_from_another_process` runs the test binary again as a child with `OSTRA_SCRUB_TEST_CHILD` set. The child calls `ostra_sandbox::scrub_startup_env()` and prints `scrubbed`. The parent then reads the child arguments with `sysctl(KERN_PROCARGS2)` and expects that the secret is gone. The test has its own file because the scrub rewrites the whole environment of the process.

## Conformance harness: events in, steps out

The planner is a pure function, `next_steps(&SessionState, &PlanCtx) -> Vec<Step>` in `crates/ostra-engine/src/plan.rs`. It reads a session state and returns the steps to start. It starts no process. A test therefore needs no executor, no provider, and no clock. Without a conformance suite, a change to one rule can break another rule, and no test names the rule that broke.

The file `tests/conformance/main.rs` holds 126 fixtures. The file is registered as a test target of `ostra-engine` in `crates/ostra-engine/Cargo.toml`:

```toml
[[test]]
name = "conformance"
path = "../../tests/conformance/main.rs"
```

The header of the file says that each fixture belongs to one rule ID of the design brief. The code cites the same IDs in comments such as `// Rule D3a`. The design brief file `HANDOVER.md` is deleted from the working tree of this checkout, so the fixtures are the live statement of each rule.

### The history helper H

The struct `H` holds a `SessionId`, a list of `StoredEvent`, and a `PlanCtx`. Each fixture builds a history, folds it, and checks the steps. These methods do the work:

- `H::new(projects, options)` appends a `SessionCreated` event. It also sets a format command `fmt-<project>` for each project in `PlanCtx::format_commands`.
- `h.ev(event)` appends a `StoredEvent` with `seq` equal to the length plus 1 and `at` equal to `Utc::now()`. It does not check that the runner could write this event.
- `h.state()` returns `SessionState::fold(id, &events)`.
- `h.steps()` returns `next_steps(&state, &ctx)`, and `h.summaries()` maps each step through `Step::summary()`.
- `h.decide(judge, subject, output)` appends a `DecisionMade` event. `h.classify(category, projects)` is a short form for the `Classify` judge.
- `h.start(prefix)` finds the spawn step whose summary starts with the prefix and appends `ExecutionStarted`. `h.finish(id, status, submit)` appends `ExecutionFinished`. `h.run(prefix, submit)` does both with status `Ok`.
- `h.open_gate(kind)` finds the step `gate <kind>` and appends `GateOpened`. `h.answer(gate, answer)` appends `GateAnswered`. When the answer has content, `answer_needs_route` marks it as routed, and the fixture must call `h.route` or `h.deliver` to give the judge decision (Rule J1).
- `h.command(purpose, project)` appends a `CommandRan` event with exit code 0.

The canned flows build common prefixes. `H::explored` runs classify, one explore per project, and the `Track` judge with `full`. `H::spec_approved` adds the spec, its fact-check, and an approved gate. `H::plan_approved` adds the `Stakes` judge, the plan, its fact-check, and an approved gate. The methods `pass_phase(n)` and `accept()` finish one phase and the implementation review.

The coordination fixtures at the end of the file add `ask`, `reply`, `wait`, `wake`, and `start_on`. The method `wake` copies the runner: it reads `next_delivery`, appends `MessageDelivered`, and then appends `ExecutionResumed`.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["H::new and h.ev append StoredEvent"] --> B["SessionState::fold"]
    B --> C["next_steps with PlanCtx"]
    C --> D["Step::summary strings"]
    D --> E{"assert_eq on the list"}
    E -->|match| F["append the next events"]
    F --> B
    E -->|differ| G["pretty_assertions diff"]
```

### The step summary format

A fixture asserts on strings from `Step::summary()` in `plan.rs`. The string shows the kind of the step and its key fields, so a fixture reads as a list of what the planner wants next.

| Step | Summary | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Judge` | `judge <kind> [subject]` | `judge sufficiency 0` |
| `Spawn` | `spawn <agent> <purpose>`, plus ` (continues)` when it resumes a run | `spawn implementer phase 1 fix (continues)` |
| `OpenGate` | `gate <kind>` | `gate review_cap` |
| `YoloAnswer` | `yolo-answer` | `yolo-answer` |
| `Command` | `command <purpose> <project>` | `command format api` |
| `Autofix`, `AnnounceBlocked` | `autofix phase N`, `blocked phase N` | `blocked phase 1` |
| `FinishInit`, `RecordInitProblem` | `finish-init <project>`, `init-problem <project>` | `finish-init app` |
| `WriteBook`, `Complete`, `Fail`, `Deliver` | `write-book <book>`, `complete`, `fail`, `deliver <kind>` | `fail` |

The purpose part of a spawn summary comes from `purpose_summary`. Examples: `explore#0`, `spec#1`, `fact-check-spec#1`, `phase 1 initial`, `review phase 1 #2`, `docs a`.

```rust
#[test]
fn d1_explore_leads_to_spec_never_plan() {
    let h = H::explored(&["p"], SessionOptions::default());
    let s = h.summaries();
    assert_eq!(s, vec!["spawn generate-spec spec#1"]);
}
```

### Coverage by rule group

Banner comments divide the file into groups. Each group checks one family of rules:

| Group | What the fixtures prove |
| --- | --- |
| D1, D2, D3, D3a, D3b | `IMPLEMENT` always passes through the spec. The spec waits for every explore and the `Sufficiency` judge. Open questions come before the fact-check. Prior findings are `none` once and then verbatim. A source check refetches only on the first pass. |
| D4, D5, D10 | The plan reads only the spec. A plan fact-check needs `PASS` before approval. A requirement change after the plan restarts at the spec. |
| D6, D7, M2 to M6, D8, T1 to T7, D9 | One pipeline per project, phase dependencies, format once per project, one closing gate per project, tests and docs after the gate. A failed phase removes its dependents. |
| C1, C2, P1 to P4 | Context files and delivery, pause and resume, containment signals. Three signals from one execution pause the session. Two signals, or signals from different executions, do not. |
| Hard 4, 13, 21 | A missing submit is a failure. The review loop splits autofix and fix and caps at 3 passes. `BLOCKER` findings go alone to the fix agent, with no cap, and block docs. |
| HANDOFF, STUCK, YOLO | A stuck run goes to rescue, never to a plain retry. Under YOLO the review budget rises to 10 passes, then the `ResolveReview` judge decides, then the phase blocks if the findings do not converge. |
| Resume, other categories, quick answer, quick change | Interrupted runs run again. `RESEARCH`, `QUICK_ANSWER`, `QUICK_CHANGE`, and `TEST` end sooner than `IMPLEMENT`. |
| B1 to B7 | Documentation books. At most `MAX_DOCS_WRITERS` (4) documentation spawns run at once. The architecture run needs two or more projects. |
| Cost controls | A session budget turns the next spawn into the `budget_reached` gate. YOLO leaves that gate open. With no budget, there is no limit. |
| Tracks, F1, J1 | `IMPLEMENT` is light by default and the `Track` judge can escalate. After the last phase, the user reviews until they accept. Every answer with content goes through the judge. |
| O2 to O6, I1 | A created project gets its init first. The advisor reads a failed init step first. Pinned projects are the whole scope. Existing skills can skip the init scouts. |
| H1 to H9 | Subagent coordination. A helper answers and the asker wakes in place. Asks are bounded by `MAX_HELPERS_PER_RUN` (3). A conversation stops continuing at `MAX_CONVERSATION_RUNS` (6). A waiting subagent holds completion. |

### What happens when a fixture fails

- If `spawn_step(prefix)` finds no spawn that starts with the prefix, it panics with the prefix and the full list of summaries.
- If `open_gate(kind)` finds no step `gate <kind>`, it panics with the list of summaries. The planner did not plan that gate at this point of the history.
- If an `assert_eq!` on the summaries fails, `pretty_assertions` prints a diff of the two lists.
- If a rule changes on purpose, change the planner and the fixture of that rule in the same commit. If the rule does not change, fix the planner.
- Because `h.ev` uses `Utc::now()`, a fixture must not depend on the exact time of an event.

## Add a conformance fixture

Follow these steps when you add a planner rule or change one:

1. Find the banner comment of the rule group in `tests/conformance/main.rs`. Add the fixture under it, or add a new banner with the rule ID.
2. Name the test `<rule id>_<what it proves>`, for example `j1_a_research_answer_runs_explore_before_the_spec`.
3. Start from the shortest canned flow: `H::explored`, `H::spec_approved`, or `H::plan_approved`.
4. Add events with `h.run`, `h.decide`, `h.answer`, and `h.command`. Use `h.ev` only for events that no helper builds.
5. Assert on `h.summaries()`. Assert on `h.state()` only for a field that a summary does not show.
6. Cite the rule in the planner with a one-line `// Rule <id>` comment.
7. Run `cargo test -p ostra-engine --test conformance <rule id>_`.

A fixture is the fastest way to test engine behavior, because it needs no async runtime and no files. Use an engine integration test only when the behavior depends on the runner, the store, or a real executor call.

## Limits and counts

| Item | Value | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Conformance fixtures | 126 | `tests/conformance/main.rs` |
| Policy tests | 50 | `crates/ostra-policy/tests/policy.rs` |
| Server end-to-end tests | 24 plus 1 MCP test | `crates/ostra-server/tests/` |
| Engine integration tests | 5 + 8 + 2 | `crates/ostra-engine/tests/` |
| Engine test deadline for a full session | 20 seconds | `runner.rs` |
| `until` poll limit | 200 polls of 20 ms | `pause.rs` |
| Docs writers at one time | `MAX_DOCS_WRITERS` = 4 | `crates/ostra-engine/src/plan.rs` |
| Helpers for one run | `MAX_HELPERS_PER_RUN` = 3 | `crates/ostra-core/src/coord.rs` |
| Runs in one conversation | `MAX_CONVERSATION_RUNS` = 6 | `crates/ostra-core/src/coord.rs` |

A scheduling fixture with two projects and four phases.
Cost control: the budget gate and the YOLO rule.
Registers the conformance file as a test target.
The summary strings that fixtures assert on.
A full YOLO session with the scripted executor.
Restart recovery with a second engine on the same database.
Containment signals pause and resume a session.
How the end-to-end server starts and signs in.
The build streak test with the helper style.
The macOS-only environment scrub test.

sections.title: Live evals, the browser security suite, and Windows probes
sections.summary: The four paid live eval suites with their variables and offline checks, the Playwright browser security suite with its guard fixture, and the standalone Windows probe crate.
sections.body:
## Suites that `cargo test --workspace` does not run

Some checks need a real model, a real browser, or a real Windows machine. These checks cost money or time, or they need a platform that most developers do not have. Without them, a prompt change, a CSP change, or a Windows sandbox design can break with no failed unit test. The project keeps three such suites outside the default test run:

| Suite | Location | Runs on | Cost |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Live evals | `tests/evals/*.toml`, `crates/ostra-server/tests/*_evals.rs` | Real models through the provider API | Money for each model call |
| Browser security suite | `tests/browser/` | Chromium and a scratch server | Build time and about 1 server process |
| Windows probes | `tests/windows-probes/` | A throwaway Windows VM | Manual work |

The repository has no `.github` folder, so no CI file runs these suites. A developer starts each one by hand. The page "Unit, integration, and conformance tests" covers the layers that run by default.

## Four live eval suites and what each one checks

A live eval measures how a model behaves in a role of Ostra. Model answers vary from run to run, so an eval reports pass counts and spread. It does not assert that a model answers correctly. Each suite has one case file in `tests/evals/` and one test file in `crates/ostra-server/tests/`:

| Suite | Case file | Cases | Test file | Live test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Judge routing | `tests/evals/judges.toml` | 83 | `judge_evals.rs` | `judge_routing_evals` |
| Advisor | `tests/evals/advisor.toml` | 13 | `advisor_evals.rs` | `advisor_evals` |
| Coordination | `tests/evals/coordination.toml` | 11 | `coordination_evals.rs` | `coordination_evals` |
| Test stage | `tests/evals/test_stage.toml` | 13 | `test_stage_evals.rs` | `test_stage_evals` |

### Judge routing evals

Each case in `judges.toml` is a request about the source of Ostra with the answer that a careful engineer would pick. The test builds the session state that the judge would see, with the same `SessionState::fold` and `judge_input` that the engine uses. It then calls the judge `OSTRA_EVAL_RUNS` times for each model. The test scores the answer by exact expected fields. No grader model takes part.

The 83 cases cover six judges: `classify` (23), `feedback` (16), `route_answer` (25), `stakes` (3), `sufficiency` (2), and `track` (14). A case names one of three workspaces: `one` (52 cases, Ostra as one project `ostra`), `split` (28 cases, projects `server` and `web`), and `triple` (3 cases).

### Advisor evals

The advisor helps when a step of the init of a created project fails (Rule O5). Each case lays out a failed step on disk as the engine leaves it. The default project is `notes-mcp`, a Rust MCP server, unless a case sets `[case.project]`. The test builds the advisor spawn with the engine function `advisor_request` and the spawn factory, and it runs the real advisor in the native loop with the policy and the sandbox.

A run passes when three checks hold: the action matches (`retry` or `escalate`), the text names every required fact, and the grader model finds the rubric met. The 13 cases cover the init steps detect, scout, propose, generate, inventory, and the harness sign-in. Many cases come in pairs with the same surface problem and opposite answers. An advisor that matches the problem text and does not read the files fails one case of each pair.

### Coordination evals

Each case runs a real `Engine` on a snapshot of the source of Ostra, with scripted judges. A router executor sends the runs that the case lists in `live` to the native loop on the model under test. The router plays every other run from the `actor` entries of the case. For this reason, wakes, consult runs, pair-loop continuations, and freed slots go through the engine code, and only the live runs cost tokens.

A run address has the form `agent[:kind][#n]`. The fields `stop_after` and `stop_before` end the session at a matching run. A run passes when every code check holds (asks, answers, statuses, submits, files, continuations, cache reads) and the grader finds the rubric met. The 11 cases fall into three tiers:

- **Tier 1 (4 cases), answering:** a consult run or a woken run answers the question of another subagent.
- **Tier 2 (4 cases), deciding:** whether to ask, whom to ask, and what to ask. Control cases check that asking is wrong when everything traces.
- **Tier 3 (3 cases), loops:** several live runs of two agents wake each other through the engine.

The snapshot comes from `git ls-files -co --exclude-standard`. It leaves out `tests/evals/coordination.toml`, `crates/ostra-server/tests/coordination_evals.rs`, and every `*_HANDOVER.md` file. The reason is that the live model must not read the expected answers.

### Test stage evals

These cases put the execution path analyzer (`epa`), `write-test`, or both on a live model. Each case is a real session on a small project from `tests/evals/test_stage/projects/` (`notes`, `shop`, `storefront`). The case starts in one of two modes. In mode `phase` (9 cases), a scripted implementer applies a change and the engine stages it. In mode `request` (4 cases), a new `TEST` session asks for tests, and no implementer runs.

An analyzer run passes when its report is at the declared path, it changed no project file, the report holds each expected fact (`epa.has` groups, with one alternative of each group needed, and `epa.lacks`), and the grader finds the rubric met. A `write-test` run passes when all of these hold:

- Its status is the expected status.
- It changed only test files and listed all of them.
- Each expected level (`levels` group) got a test.
- The test types in `run` pass.
- Every planted mutant of the source fails those tests. A mutant is a small change to the source that a good test suite must catch.
- The files in `files` keep their text.
- The grader agrees.

The 13 cases split into tier 1 (3), tier 2 (4), and tier 3 (6). The report names a `write-test` run on a golden analysis `write-test`, and a run after a live analyzer `stage`.

## Run a live eval

Caution: run a live eval only when you accept the cost. Each run calls real models, and no code caps the spend. The number of calls is the number of cases, times the number of models, times `OSTRA_EVAL_RUNS`. A judge eval with the defaults makes 83 × 1 × 3 = 249 judge calls. The advisor, coordination, and test stage suites also call the grader model for each run.

Set the provider credentials before you start, for example `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. Use `--ignored`, not `--include-ignored`. The live tests set process environment variables without a lock, and the comment in the code says that the offline test of the same binary is not run in the same process.

```bash
OSTRA_EVAL_MODELS=anthropic:claude-opus-5-5,anthropic:claude-sonnet-5-5 OSTRA_EVAL_RUNS=5 \
  cargo test -p ostra-server --test advisor_evals -- --ignored --nocapture
```

Replace `advisor_evals` with `judge_evals`, `coordination_evals`, or `test_stage_evals` for the other suites.

### Environment variables and defaults

Each live test reads the same variables. Models are a comma list of `provider:model`. The test splits the list on commas, trims each item, and drops empty items. A value for `OSTRA_EVAL_RUNS` or `OSTRA_EVAL_JOBS` that does not parse as a number falls back to the default.

| Variable | Advisor | Judge | Coordination | Test stage |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `OSTRA_EVAL_MODELS` | `anthropic:claude-opus-5-5`, `anthropic:claude-sonnet-5-5` | `anthropic:claude-opus-5-5` | Opus, Sonnet, and `anthropic:claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` | Same as coordination |
| `OSTRA_EVAL_RUNS` (runs per case and model) | 5 | 3 | 3 | 3 |
| `OSTRA_EVAL_JOBS` (runs at one time) | 4 | none | 3 | 3 |
| `OSTRA_EVAL_GRADER` | `anthropic:claude-opus-5-5` | none | `anthropic:claude-opus-5-5` | `anthropic:claude-opus-5-5` |
| `OSTRA_EVAL_CASES` | Substring of the case ID, comma list | Same | Same | Same |
| `OSTRA_EVAL_TIERS` | none | none | Tier list such as `1,2` | Same |

An empty `OSTRA_EVAL_CASES` selects every case.

## Eval reports, scratch files, and failure rules

Each live test prints a table with accuracy, cost, and time for each model, and writes a JSON report to `target/evals/`. The file names are `advisor-<stamp>.json`, `judges-<stamp>.json`, `coordination-<stamp>.json`, and `test-stage-<stamp>.json`, where `<stamp>` is the UTC start time. The report holds pass counts, the spread of answers, the cost of the runs, and the cost of the grader. The coordination report also holds the share of input tokens that the prompt cache served.

The live tests of the advisor, coordination, and test stage suites isolate themselves from your own Ostra data:

- They set `OSTRA_CONFIG`, `OSTRA_DATA_DIR`, `OSTRA_SANDBOX_CACHE`, and `OSTRA_MODELS_DEV_URL` (empty) to a folder under `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/ostra-evals/` or `~/.cache/ostra-evals/`. The test removes the folder at the end.
- They put the case scenarios under `CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR` in the target folder, never in `/tmp`.
- The reason for both rules is that the sandbox mounts its own `/tmp` and its egress socket paths must stay short.
- They read prices from the cached `models.dev` catalog of the server, when the cache exists.

### What happens when a live eval fails

The live test fails only when the run itself is broken. A wrong model answer does not fail the test.

- Advisor: fails when no advisor run finished. The message says to check the provider credentials and the sandbox.
- Judge: fails when every judge call failed.
- Coordination: fails when no live run happened.
- Test stage: fails when no run had a cost or a time above 0.
- If the case filter selects no case, the list of outcomes is empty and the test passes.
- If a run has an infrastructure error, the report records it, and the grader does not score that run.

## Offline checks for the eval cases

Each suite has a test without `#[ignore]` that runs in `cargo test --workspace` and costs nothing. A broken case file fails here, before anyone pays for a live run.

| Test | What it checks |
| --- | --- |
| `eval_cases_build_their_sessions` (judge) | Each case folds into the state its judge expects. The request is in the judge input. The items, research, notes, answers, and expected fields that the judge kind needs are present. |
| `advisor_cases_build_their_spawns` | Case IDs are unique. The action is `retry` or `escalate`. The first message holds the labels `Failed step:`, `Problem:`, `Step inputs:`, `Step context:`, and `Repo root:`. No placeholder such as `{ws}` stays unfilled. The system prompt holds `# Advisor Agent`. The project is a git repository. |
| `coordination_cases_run_dry` | Case IDs are unique and the tier is 1 to 3. The track is `light` or `full`. The case replays with stand-in actors. Every live run is reached, the session stops where the case says, and continued runs continue. No scripted run fails. The snapshot holds no expectation file. |
| `test_stage_cases_run_dry` (Unix only) | The replay uses the golden analysis and the golden tests. Every live run is reached and graded clean. The project tests let every mutant survive, and the golden tests kill every mutant. |

The test stage replay skips a case when the machine lacks the runner for its tests. The project `notes` needs `node`, and the other projects need `python3`. The skip prints a line that starts with the case ID.

## Browser security suite

The browser suite proves in a real Chromium that the browser-facing defenses hold. It covers the render paths of agent and repo text, the terminal, the cross-origin boundary, the sign-in token, uploads, and browser storage, in the console and in the site. The suite is its own npm package with its own `package-lock.json`. It is not part of the root npm workspace, and Biome ignores it.

```bash
cd tests/browser && npm test
```

The command `npm run test:fast` sets `PW_SKIP_BUILD=1` and skips the builds. Use it to rerun after a spec change. The site pages still rebuild, because the test page names the port of the fake model. The console shot inside them does not rebuild.

### What global-setup builds

The file `tests/browser/global-setup.ts` runs once before all specs. Nothing leaves the machine: the model API is a local fake, the harness is a stub script, and the MCP server is a stub. The steps are:

1. Build the web UI with `npm run build` in `web/`, and build `ostra-server` with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target-browser`. `PW_SKIP_BUILD` skips both.
2. Stop an older scratch server, but only when the pid in `/tmp/pw-browser/server.pid` names a process whose command line holds `ostra` and `serve`. The check reads `/proc`, so it does nothing on macOS.
3. Refuse to continue when the scratch root `ROOT` does not start with `/tmp/`. Delete `/tmp/pw-browser` and create the folders `home` and `data`.
4. Start the fake model API (`lib/fake-model.ts`, which counts canary hits) and the attacker page server (`lib/attacker.ts`).
5. Build the site into `/tmp/pw-browser/site` with a docs page of test strings (`VITE_TEST_DOC`), and serve it as plain files on `ostra-site.localhost`.
6. Write a repository, a stub harness, a stub MCP server, and a config.
7. Start `ostra serve --no-open --port <free port> --bind 127.0.0.1` with a private environment: `HOME`, `OSTRA_CONFIG`, `OSTRA_DATA_DIR`, and `OSTRA_MASTER_KEY_FILE` under the scratch root, `OSTRA_MODELS_DEV_URL` empty, `OSTRA_LOG=info`, and `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`.
8. Wait up to 60 seconds for the server and for `data/server.json`.
9. Sign in with a minted one-time URL, and check that the origin ends with `.localhost:<port>`.
10. Create a workspace and a project, complete onboarding, and add an MCP server, a lesson, a skill, and four uploads. Three uploads are `evil.svg`, `evil.html`, and `evil.md`. The fourth has a file name with an `onerror` payload.
11. Start a YOLO session whose agent outputs carry test strings, and wait up to 120 seconds for `completed`, `failed`, or `stalled`.
12. Write the documentation book `pw_book` to `.ostra/docs/pw_book/book.json` in the scratch workspace.
13. Save `state.json` and return the teardown function. The teardown sends `SIGTERM` to the server, unless `PW_KEEP_SERVER` is set, and closes the fake model, the attacker server, and the site server.

### The guard fixture

Every test string would set `window.__pwned` or request `<fake>/canary/<id>` if it ran or loaded. The `guard` fixture in `tests/browser/lib/guard.ts` watches for both. Every spec imports `test` and `expect` from this file, not from Playwright. The fixture records a `Finding` with one of six kinds:

| Kind | Trigger |
| --- | --- |
| `pwned` | Code sets `window.__pwned`. An init script defines it as a setter that reports through the console, which a CSP cannot block. |
| `csp` | A `securitypolicyviolation` event on the app origin. The detail names the blocked URL, whose ID names the render path. Violations on an attacker origin do not count. |
| `dialog` | A dialog that the test did not list in `expectedDialogs`. The guard dismisses every dialog. |
| `navigation` | A main frame leaves the allowed origins, or a subframe goes to a `javascript:`, `data:`, or `vbscript:` URL. |
| `popup` | A second page opens, unless the test sets `allowPopups`. |
| `canary` | The fake model received a request on `/canary/<id>` after the test started. |

After the test body, the fixture waits 500 ms for late loads, then fails the test if `findings` is not empty. The helper `domProblems` in `lib/audit.ts` adds static checks on the DOM: event-handler attributes, script URLs, frames, plugins, inline or foreign scripts, and images from another origin.

### Specs and what each covers

| Spec | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| `00-smoke` | The app loads signed in, and the page shows text that starts with `PW-` within 20 seconds. |
| `render` | Agent messages, tool output, artifacts, the completion report, titles, repo file names and contents, branches, commits, MCP metadata, memory, skills, decisions, search, the quick answer. |
| `mobile` | The same render paths in the phone layout (`web/src/mobile/`), at a viewport of 412 by 880. |
| `terminal` | OSC 52, OSC 8, title sequences, and device queries through xterm.js. The PTY input must match a run with no browser attached. |
| `cross-origin` | Attacker pages on another localhost port and on another site: forms, fetch, WebSocket, tags, frames, and a navigation to every GET route in `api.rs`. DNS rebinding. Page content that reaches `/api`. |
| `signin` | The token leaves the URL, no request carries it, and the profile keeps only spent values. |
| `uploads` | SVG and HTML uploads never render inline, through chips, the artifact view, or raw links. |
| `storage` | `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, IndexedDB, and Cache Storage hold no transcripts, tokens, or keys. |
| `shortcuts` | The web app manifest and icons load under the CSP. A recorded shortcut stays in the `localStorage` entry of its workspace and runs. |
| `site` | Docs Markdown with test strings, Mermaid diagrams with hostile labels, every docs page, search, the homepage and its console shot under their meta CSP, and messages from another origin. |
| `books` | A book with test strings in every field: the Docs list, each reader page, diagrams, search, and the exported HTML file, which must hold no script and render under its meta CSP with nothing blocked. |

The cross-origin spec gets its list of routes from `apiRoutes()` in `tests/browser/lib/routes.ts`. The function reads the text of `crates/ostra-server/src/api.rs` between `pub fn router(` and `.merge(crate::bridge::internal_routes())`, and it parses every `.route(` call. A new route is therefore tested without a change to the suite. The function throws when it parses fewer than 60 routes.

### Configuration and limits

| Setting | Value | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Workers | 1, with `fullyParallel: false` | `playwright.config.ts` |
| Test timeout | 90 seconds | `playwright.config.ts` |
| Expect timeout | 15 seconds | `playwright.config.ts` |
| Trace | Kept on failure, in `test-results/` | `playwright.config.ts` |
| Reports | `list` in the terminal, `html` in `playwright-report/` | `playwright.config.ts` |
| Server wait | 60 seconds | `waitFor` in `global-setup.ts` |
| Session wait | 120 seconds | `global-setup.ts` |
| Scratch root | `/tmp/pw-browser` | `lib/env.ts` |
| Server binary | `OSTRA_BIN`, default `target-browser/debug/ostra` | `lib/env.ts` |
| Browser binary | `PW_CHROME`, default `~/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-1217/chrome-linux64/chrome` | `lib/env.ts` |
| Attacker host | `evil-ostra.test`, mapped to `127.0.0.1` with `--host-resolver-rules` | `lib/env.ts` |

The suite uses one worker because it has one scratch server and one PTY, and specs that type into the PTY must not overlap.

### What happens when a browser run fails

- If the file at `PW_CHROME` or the default path does not exist, the config passes no `executablePath`, and Playwright uses its own browser.
- If `site/` is absent, `buildSite` throws and every spec fails. The `site/` workspace is named by the root `package.json`, but this checkout does not contain it. The `site` spec needs it.
- If you set `PW_SKIP_BUILD` before a first full run, `target-browser/debug/ostra` or `site/public/console` is missing, and setup fails. The error for the site says to run the suite once without `PW_SKIP_BUILD`.
- If the YOLO session ends with a status other than `completed`, setup prints a warning, and the specs render what exists.
- If the server does not answer within 60 seconds, setup throws `timed out waiting for server`.
- Set `PW_KEEP_SERVER=1` to keep the scratch server after the run. Stop it with the pid in `/tmp/pw-browser/server.pid`.

## Windows probes

The folder `tests/windows-probes` holds a separate Cargo package, `winprobe`. It checks the assumptions of the Windows sandbox design on a real Windows machine, before the design is built. The root `Cargo.toml` lists it in `exclude`, it has its own `Cargo.lock`, and `.gitignore` ignores its `target/` folder. It contains no Ostra code and depends only on `windows-sys` 0.61. For this reason, `cargo build --workspace` and `cargo test --workspace` never build it.

The file `.cargo/config.toml` of the crate sets `-C target-feature=+crt-static`. The static C runtime lets the single exe run on a bare VM without the Visual C++ runtime. The release profile uses `opt-level = "z"`, `lto`, `strip`, and `panic = "abort"` to keep the exe small.

Caution: run `winprobe setup` only on a throwaway Windows VM. The command creates the local users `OstraProbeA` and `OstraProbeB`, an ACL test tree under `C:\ostra-probe`, and per-user firewall filters.

`main.rs` picks a role from `argv[1]`:

| Command | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `winprobe setup` | Create the probe users, the test tree, and the firewall filters. Run it elevated. |
| `winprobe run` | Start the confined probes as the probe users, run the host-side checks, and write `C:\ostra-probe\results.md`. |
| `winprobe cleanup` | Remove everything that `setup` created. |
| `winprobe asuser <group> <out>` | Run one check group as a probe user. The `run` role starts this role. |
| `markself`, `medspawn`, `sleeper`, `openone`, `spinjob`, `netfilter` | Small helpers that the other roles start. |

Any other first argument prints the list of roles and exits with code 2. Build the crate from `tests/windows-probes` with `cargo build --release`, and copy the exe to the VM, for example with `scp`.

### The recorded results

The file `tests/windows-probes/results-full.md` records one run on Windows Server 2025 Datacenter Evaluation, build 26100. It has 54 rows in 17 verify groups. The status key is:

| Status | Count | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PASS` | 43 | The design assumption held. |
| `FAIL` | 3 | A gap that the later implementation must handle. |
| `INCONCLUSIVE` | 4 | The VM cannot decide the check. |
| `NEEDS_CLIENT` | 4 | The check needs a Windows 11 client or the antivirus machine. |

The three `FAIL` rows show two gaps. Windows Firewall does not filter loopback or own-IP traffic, so the sandbox cannot restrict loopback to only the proxy port without a raw WFP filter (verify 7). Processes of the same sandbox user are not isolated from each other, and a restricting SID does not change that (verify 8, two rows). The page "Windows support and the probe results" explains how the sandbox design uses these results.

The four `NEEDS_CLIENT` rows are desktop and input isolation (verify 9), ConPTY fidelity per harness CLI (13), Git Bash as the sandbox user (14), and mitigation policies against developer toolchains (15). The comments of the crate cite a `WINDOWS_HANDOVER.md` file. That file is ignored by git and is not in the repository.
