topics.title: Orientation and development workflow
topics.scope: Covers what Ostra is, how the 15 crates depend on each other, the core terms, and how a developer builds, formats, and changes the code. It does not explain one subsystem in depth.

topics.title: Session lifecycle and the event-sourced engine
topics.scope: Covers how one session runs from request to completion, the event log and the fold, the planner and the runner, failure and restart behavior, and the engine constants. It stops at the catalogs of judges and gates, at the loops inside a phase, and at the settings files.

topics.title: Judges, gates, and user context
topics.scope: Covers the 10 judges, the 14 gate kinds with their answers and YOLO behavior, and how uploads, attached files, and added context reach agents. It stops at the console forms for gates and at the loops that open gates.

topics.title: Work loops, closing stages, and agent coordination
topics.scope: Covers the implement and review loop of a phase, autofix, rescue, blocked phases, the closing gate, the test stage, the documentation stage, the completion report, and how agents ask each other questions. It stops at the catalogs of judges and gates and at the tool inputs.

topics.title: Shared types, settings, and routing
topics.scope: Covers the three settings files with every setting, default, and storage place, the save-time validation rules, route resolution, and the shared types for ids, paths, usage, pricing, and wire shapes. It stops at the trust mechanism and at the executor contract.

topics.title: Stores, workspaces, and trust
topics.scope: Covers the three SQLite stores, the sealing of credentials, the life of a workspace from create to delete, project import and removal, and the approval of commands that come from folder files. It stops at the choice of the master key and at the engine fold.

topics.title: Agents, prompts, and the spawn contract
topics.scope: Covers the embedded assets, prompt rendering for each executor, the typed spawn contract, the repo brief, the catalog of 14 agents with their submit payloads, and the typed research, spec, and plan documents. It stops at the book model and at the executors that run the agents.

topics.title: Documentation books
topics.scope: Covers the book model, the submit rules, the book id, the merge, the files on disk, and the ranked search that the `DocsSearch` tool uses. It stops at the documentation stage flow and at the console reader.

topics.title: Executor contract, native loop, and model providers
topics.scope: Covers the types that the engine hands to an executor, the native turn loop with submit and compaction, and the Anthropic and OpenAI providers with retry and streaming. It stops at harness executors and at the pricing formula.

topics.title: Harness executors: Claude Code, Codex, Grok, and Antigravity
topics.scope: Covers how Ostra launches and supervises an installed command-line harness in a terminal, the hook bridge, the MCP shim, the adapters, usage reading, and the failure matrix for both executor families. It stops at the native loop and at the policy rules.

topics.title: Policy engine
topics.scope: Covers how every tool call passes the guards and then the permissions, every guard, the permission modes and rule forms, the Bash command parser, the ask flow, containment signals, the build streak, and the lesson gate. It stops at the sandbox and at the tool implementations.

topics.title: Sandbox
topics.scope: Covers the sandbox profile, the bubblewrap and Seatbelt backends, the egress proxy, the decoy files, the sandbox settings, the failure cases, process trees, and the Windows status with the probe results. It stops at the policy rules.

topics.title: Native tools and code navigation
topics.scope: Covers the native tool catalog and its shared behavior, the project, coordination, and MCP tools, the code index, the code providers and language servers, and the eight code tools for agents. It stops at the policy rules and at the loop that calls the tools.

topics.title: Server: startup, auth, API, and integrations
topics.scope: Covers server startup, the request guard, sign-in and the master key, the REST and WebSocket protocol, the files, git, artifact, skill, and command routes, the external MCP client, Web Push, and how to run, install, and extend the server. It stops at the engine and at the harness bridge protocol.

topics.title: Web console and design system
topics.scope: Covers the React console, its shell and routing, the REST and socket clients, live state, gate forms, the book reader and export, shortcuts, the palette, push install, and the design package. It stops at the server behavior behind the console.

topics.title: Test suites and evals
topics.scope: Covers the unit and integration tests, the planner conformance suite, the live evals, the browser security suite, and the Windows probes, with the command and purpose of each. It stops at the rules that the tests check.

glossary.definition: The JSON in the registry row `workspace_access:<root>` that holds the registry-only settings of one workspace.
The pure reducer `applyDelta` that turns execution deltas into display entries and ignores a delta at or below the last seq.
Code that translates the hook payload and response shapes of one harness to and from the canonical tool call of Ostra.
A `workspace.toml` that already exists in a folder when a user creates a workspace there, so Ostra builds on it and approves nothing in it.
A leaf model worker with its own prompt that ends its run with a `submit_<agent>` call.
Text, files, or uploads that the user adds to a running session, recorded as a RequestAmended event.
The error type of REST handlers. It holds a status code and a body with a message and a list of field issues.
The SHA-256 hex text of the command content that Ostra stores in the registry when the user approves a folder file.
The scope text of a lesson, such as `orders::Service`, where `::` separates a sub-scope.
The folder `<data dir>/assets` where Ostra copies the references, skills, and agent instructions at startup.
A file or folder of a project or a workspace artifact that the user names as context with an @ tag.
The step that applies findings from their exact Fix text with no model call.
The code that renders a profile into a command that the kernel enforces: bubblewrap on Linux or Seatbelt on macOS.
The name of an external MCP tool without the `mcp__` prefix, in the form `server__tool`.
The highest finding severity. It marks unsafe code, goes alone to the fix agent, and has no review cap.
A ranking formula that rewards rare query words, limits the reward for repeated words, and normalizes by text length.
A set of Markdown files and one `book.json` that cover one set of projects, written by the engine from submit payloads.
The folder name of a book. It joins the sorted project keys with `_` and ends in a hash when it is longer than 80 bytes.
The process-wide mutex `BOOK_LOCK` that serializes every read-merge-write and every removal of a book.
What one session adds to a book: parts, architecture, and glossary entries, all built from the event log.
The Linux backend. It uses the `bwrap` command to give a command its own mount, pid, IPC, and network namespaces.
The budget_reached gate that opens when the spend of a session reaches its limit and blocks new spawns.
The planner rule that drops spawn steps when the finished executions of a session have spent its budget.
A build or test command of the project, taken from the commands in `project.toml`, or from a fallback pattern when none are set.
The count of consecutive failing build commands in one execution. It drives the recall, the warning, and the block.
A host rule from Ostra, such as a package registry or a model host. It must resolve to a public address.
A URL of the form `<fake>/canary/<id>` in a test string. A request to it shows that hostile content loaded.
A tool call in which `canonical_call` made paths, the shell directory, and the URL absolute, so the policy and the tool see one target.
The name `mcp__<server>__<tool>` that the native loop, the policy, and permission rules use for an external MCP tool.
A value of the `Capability` enum that an agent definition lists and that grants one tool or one family of tools.
The kind of request, one of 10 values of `Category`, chosen by the classify judge.
A named stream of live messages, such as `session:<id>` or `home`, that a client subscribes to.
The function that reads the document files at the tool boundary and refuses a submit that has errors or wrong counts.
The program of a harness that Ostra starts in a terminal and supervises.
The gate titled Tests and documentation that asks, for each project, whether to write tests and documentation.
A source of answers to the four code requests: `file`, `usages`, `deps`, and `symbols`.
The parts of a folder file that start a program or loosen a check, and so need approval.
A code provider that runs the `code_provider` program of a project once for each request.
The replacement of a long conversation by a summary when the context window is nearly full.
The judge that writes the markdown report that ends a session.
The `**Complexity:**` value of a plan phase: `low`, `medium`, or `high`. Work with no phase file counts as `low`.
The per-execution folder `harness/<execution id>` that holds the generated files of a launch and the terminal transcript.
A test in `tests/conformance/main.rs` that builds an event history, folds it, and asserts the steps that the planner returns.
The React single-page app in `web/` that shows sessions, executions, artifacts, files, and documentation books.
The tables of `workspace.db` that the engine writes beside the event log so the web console can query current state.
The React context that both shells provide, with `nav`, `shell`, and `workspace` parts.
A new execution that continues the conversation of a subagent that ended, so that it can answer a question without changing files.
The check that a project-relative path, after symlinks, stays inside the project root.
An event that looks like an attempt to leave the sandbox: a guard denial, a local egress refusal, or a decoy open. The third signal of one execution pauses the session.
The number of tokens that a model accepts in one request.
A phase that gets tests: it has no plan file, or its test policy is Required.
A project that an agent made with `ProjectCreate` during a session and that joined the scope of that session.
The owner-only folder that holds `registry.db`, `server.json`, `server.log`, and other server state. `OSTRA_DATA_DIR` sets it.
The stored result of one judge call, kept as a DecisionMade event with its reason.
A fake credential file in the sandbox. An open of the file is a containment signal.
A message that wakes a waiting execution: the answer to its question, or a question for it to answer.
A CSS custom property for a color, size, shape, or motion value, defined in `design/src/tokens/`.
The set of project paths that changed since the last query. A partial sync reads these paths again.
The choice of a judge for one answer item: deliver, remember, or discard.
The enum of the 3 document kinds, each with an owner agent and a file name prefix.
The agent tool that searches the documentation books of the workspace and returns matching passages.
A structured JSON document of pages that the docs stage writes and the console renders as Markdown pages.
The result of `create::draft`: the settings that a create request would write and every issue found, with no write done.
The Tokio task of one live session that calls the planner and starts a task for each new step.
The word of a simple command that actually runs, after assignments and wrappers such as `sudo` and `env`.
The reasoning level of a model request: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, or `max`.
The only way out of a private network namespace. It checks the host, port, address, and TLS server name of each connection.
The execution path analyzer, an agent that reports the paths of a phase that tests must cover.
The report of the `execution-path-analyzer` agent that assigns one check and one test level to each test.
A difficulty level, 1 to 3, that a coordination or test stage case declares. `OSTRA_EVAL_TIERS` filters by it.
One value of `SessionEvent` that the engine appends to the log of a session.
The append-only `events` table of `workspace.db`, which is the source of truth for the state of each session.
The snapshot of settings and identity that the engine builds for one execution and that the policy reads.
One run of one agent. Each execution has its own `ToolEnv`.
One streamed event of an execution, such as text, a tool call, a usage total, or a status line.
The trait of callbacks that an executor uses to send deltas, ask permission, store messages, and wait for a wake message.
The object that holds the policy state of one execution and judges each tool call with `check`.
A type that implements the `Executor` trait and runs one execution.
A rule that a check which cannot finish gives a deny, not an allow.
A group of languages that share definition and import rules, such as `Jvm` or `Data`.
The screen of the web console that shows project files with colors, an outline, usages, dependencies, and a graph.
One issue in the submit of `code-reviewer`, with a severity, a file, a rule id, a description, and a fix text.
The first user message of an execution: the spawn block, a separator, and the repo brief.
The hook `useFocusTrap` that keeps Tab inside a modal and restores the previous focus on close.
The function `SessionState::fold` that applies the stored events of a session in order and returns the session state.
A `workspace.toml` or `project.toml` file that lives in a folder and can change when a repository or an agent changes.
A model call with a tool named decide and tool_choice set to that tool, so the model must return JSON.
A check of every listed file against its size and modification time. It runs when the file list changes and every 30 seconds.
A stop in a session where the user must decide before the planner goes on.
The component that shows one open gate and builds a valid answer for it.
A guard object that lets only one clone, pull, or git operation run in a project folder at a time.
The file `config.toml` that holds machine-wide settings: providers, tier tables, harness commands, permission rules, server, and sandbox.
A model that the evals call to judge a run against the rubric of a case. `OSTRA_EVAL_GRADER` sets it.
The middleware `guard` that checks the host, the origin, and the cookie of every request before a handler runs.
The Playwright fixture in `tests/browser/lib/guard.ts` that fails a test on any sign that a test string ran or loaded.
The test struct in the conformance file that holds an event list and a `PlanCtx` and offers methods to append events and read steps.
An optional trait object in `ToolEnvConfig` that gives a tool access to server state: `code`, `mcp`, `manage`, or `coord`.
A submit status that says the agent needs a specialist. The engine runs `prompt-generation` and then resumes the agent.
An installed command-line program that runs a model for Ostra: Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build, or Antigravity.
The `/internal/policy` and `/internal/mcp` endpoints that harness hooks and the MCP shim call with a per-execution bearer token.
An external agent program that Ostra launches in a PTY: Claude Code, Codex, Grok, or Antigravity.
An executor that drives an installed CLI, such as Claude Code, in a pseudo-terminal.
A new `explore` agent that `SubagentAsk` starts to research a question and to give its findings as the answer.
A file or folder that the user hid. Everything inside it lives in the data dir, out of reach of agents.
A command that a CLI runs before or after a tool call or at a turn end, with a JSON payload on standard input.
The pair of `ostra hook` and the `/internal/policy` handler that sends each hook event to the policy engine.
One step of a graph walk from a file or definition to a file or definition that uses it or that it uses.
One `allowed_hosts` entry: a name, `*.domain`, an IPv4 address, or `[v6]`, with an optional port.
The broadcast channel `App.hub` that carries engine notices from every workspace to the WebSocket loops.
A file such as `lib.rs`, `index.ts`, or `__init__.py` that gathers and re-exports a folder. The graph does not follow import-only edges into it.
The set of step keys of a session whose task has not ended. The driver skips a step with a key in this set.
A phase that has no plan file and is made from the request, for example on the light track.
A read-only reopening of an ended harness session. The bridge denies every tool call in it.
An engine-made stop of a running execution because of a pause, new context, or a created project.
A Windows kernel object that holds processes. With `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE`, it kills them when its last handle closes.
A model call with a system prompt from `assets/judges/` that returns one decision through the `decide` tool.
One structured model call that returns a decision through the forced `decide` tool.
The route key judge that selects the model of every judge call and always uses the native executor.
A part of an answer that the judge keeps for later stages, stored as a UserNote with an ID such as N1.
Fullscreen plus the Keyboard Lock API, so that browser-reserved key combinations reach the console.
The registry table that maps text keys to bytes and holds approvals, access records, sign-in records, and sealed credentials.
One column of the session board. Each stage belongs to one of the 9 lanes.
A program that speaks the Language Server Protocol and answers code questions for the languages in its settings entry.
The program, arguments, environment, files, and links that start one CLI for one execution.
The set of guards. A guard refuses a tool call, and nothing overrides it.
The permission layer. It uses a permission mode and allow, ask, and deny rules to return Allow, Ask, or Deny.
A short text about a project, filed under an area, that agents record and recall in the project lesson store.
The guard `lesson-gate`. It refuses an `ok` submit and an unexplained `Report` until the agent records a lesson after a verified recovery.
An `#[ignore]` test that calls real models and costs money, and reports pass counts and spread instead of asserting correct answers.
One JSON message from the WebSocket that patches a snapshot.
The in-memory record of a running harness execution: token, recorded submit, session id, Stop counts, and activity time.
The enum that names what a work loop does next, such as `Work`, `Review`, `Autofix`, `Stage`, `Done`, or `Blocked`.
The pool that starts, reuses, limits, and stops language servers for all projects.
A 32-byte key that seals credential rows in the registry with AES-256-GCM. It lives in the OS keychain or in a file.
The Model Context Protocol. A client lists and calls the tools of an MCP server with JSON-RPC messages.
The program `ostra mcp-stdio`. It serves the Ostra tools to a CLI and forwards each message to `/internal/mcp`.
The server component that keeps one MCP connection for each workspace root and server name and handles OAuth sign-in.
The value that holds the listeners and decoys of one sandboxed invocation and kills its leftover processes on macOS.
One SQL entry in a `MIGRATIONS` list that Ostra applies once and records with `PRAGMA user_version`.
A mode with `VITE_MOCK=1` in which fixtures replace the REST client and the socket.
One request to the model and the handling of the tool calls in its answer.
A field of `Parsed`. It is false when the shell text has a statement, such as `export` or a loop, that the command list does not model.
The public JSON price list at `https://models.dev/api.json`. Ostra caches it in `models-dev.json` and refreshes it every 24 hours.
A planted change to project source in a test stage case. A good new test suite must fail against it.
The executor that runs the agent loop against a model API with an API key.
The built-in code provider that answers from the tokenizer and the index. It is always last in the chain.
The value of `[sandbox] network`: `none`, `allowlist`, `public`, or `host`.
A line that Ostra types into the terminal, or a Stop block, to remind the agent to call its submit tool.
A test without `#[ignore]` that validates or replays the cases of an eval suite with stand-ins and no model cost.
A random 64-character value in the sign-in link. The server accepts it once within 15 minutes and stores only its hash.
A CSS class from `components.css` that a design component renders. Plain HTML can use it too.
The list of definitions that a file holds, with kinds, lines, and containers.
A file outside the project, such as a library source or a jar class, that a language server pointed at.
A folder that holds a package manifest, or the top folder. The graph groups files by package unit.
A repeat of two agents on the same work, where each new execution continues its own earlier conversation.
The contribution of one project to a book: an overview and a list of sections.
A short labeled text cut from a unit. The search scores passages and shows only the ones that matched.
The state of a folder file whose command content has no matching approval, so Ostra removes that content from effective settings.
A 64-character random bearer token that proves a hook call comes from the CLI of one live execution.
The gate that the engine opens for an Ask decision. The call waits until a user answers or the execution ends.
One of `default`, `acceptEdits`, `plan`, and `bypass`. It decides a call when no rule matches.
A string such as `Bash(npm test *)` in the allow, ask, or deny list. It uses the syntax of Claude Code.
The answer to a permission gate: `AllowOnce`, `AlwaysInWorkspace`, or `Deny`.
One numbered unit of build work, taken from the plan or created inline when no plan exists.
A tab that sits before all other tabs and survives the bulk close actions.
Proof Key for Code Exchange. The sign-in sends a hash of a secret verifier first and the verifier itself at the code exchange.
The facts outside the log that the planner reads: the format command of each project and the session budget.
The pure function `next_steps` that reads a session state and returns the steps to run next.
The result of a policy check: Allow, Ask, or Deny, with a `RuleRef` that names the layer and the rule.
For one name, the sorted ids of the files that mention it. The usage search reads only these files.
The one italic tab that the next preview open replaces.
A random host name `ostra-<hex>.localhost` that serves the app on a loopback bind. It keeps the cookie away from other local ports.
The standalone Windows program in `tests/windows-probes` that measures whether a future Windows sandbox design can work.
A child process and every process that it starts, stopped as one unit through a process group or a Job Object.
The description of the boundary of one execution: mounts, environment, egress policy, and decoys, without a backend name.
A folder with code that agents change, listed as a `ProjectEntry` in the workspace settings and mirrored in the `projects` table.
The per-project store of names, definitions, imports, and supertype records, built by the tokenizer and the outline pass.
The file `project.toml` that the initializer agent writes. It holds commands, test types, skills, conventions, and review rules of one project.
A vendor cache of the start of a request. Reads and writes have their own token prices.
A type that implements the `Provider` trait and sends chat requests to one model vendor.
A pseudo-terminal. Ostra starts the CLI in a PTY and keeps a screen model of it.
A browser record with an https endpoint and two keys. The server uses it to send an encrypted notification.
A `ServerMsg` that the server itself starts, sent on `App.push` with the list of channels that must receive it.
A command in the allowlist whose every flag and argument Ostra understands, so it runs without a question in every mode.
The SQLite file `registry.db` in the data dir. It holds workspaces, sign-ins, sealed credentials, and push subscriptions.
A workspace setting, such as the permission mode or the limits, that Ostra keeps in the registry and never reads from a folder file.
The markdown sections that `augment` appends below the spawn block: profile facts, project instructions, artifacts, books, and workspace instructions.
The object that turns an import spec into a project file or folder with the file list and the manifests.
A string such as `session:<id>` or `file:<key>:<path>` that names anything that opens in a tab and maps to one URL.
The number of review passes that a loop can run before it needs a user answer, 3 by default and 10 under YOLO.
A file per loop where the fix agent records FIXED or WONTFIX for each finding and the reviewer reads it on the next pass.
The canonical paths of one execution that the guards compare each target path with.
The result of `resolve_route`: an executor, a model, and an optional tier.
The name that route settings use for an execution: an agent name or `judge`. There are 15.
A gate answer or an amendment with content that waits for the route-answer or feedback judge before the fold applies it.
A short code such as `D3a`, `J1`, or `H4` that names one planner rule in code comments and in conformance fixture names.
A pair of a layer (`guard` or `permission`) and a rule text that shows which rule made a decision.
The code in `runner.rs` that runs steps, appends events, and keeps one driver task for each live session.
A file, such as `.envrc` or `.github/workflows/*`, that makes a tool run a program after the session ends. A write to it always takes the mode default.
The kernel-enforced boundary of bubblewrap on Linux or Seatbelt on macOS in which agent commands run.
The text `${ostra_secret}` that `workspace.toml` holds in place of a literal MCP header or env value saved in the registry.
A private host directory that the sandbox shows as `/tmp` under bubblewrap and uses as `TMPDIR` under Seatbelt.
The `ostra serve` process that the browser suite starts under `/tmp/pw-browser` with its own config, data folder, and master key.
A React component that fills the center pane for one resource id.
A test `Executor` that returns a canned submit for each agent and runs no model.
The type that encrypts and decrypts credential values with AES-256-GCM and the row key as associated data.
The macOS backend. It applies an SBPL policy to a command through `/usr/bin/sandbox-exec`.
The paths that no agent reads: the data dir, the master key file, and the entries of `HOME_CREDENTIALS`.
The list of exact keys and key prefixes of registry rows that hold credentials and must be sealed.
One unit of work in a part, with a purpose, assumptions, and optional diagrams, tables, and code references.
A tool that the model vendor runs, such as web search, in place of a tool that Ostra runs.
The script `web/public/sw.js` that shows push notifications and opens their link on click.
The trait that the server implements to give the engine settings, executors, judges, and notices.
One user request that the engine carries from the request text to a completion report.
A rule that the running policy adds in memory when a user answers `AlwaysInWorkspace`.
A Markdown index of the session that the engine rewrites from the event log so that a revision phase reads a file and not a conversation.
The `ostra_session` cookie that a browser gets after the token exchange. It is valid for 30 days unless the user revokes it.
The folder `<workspace>/.ostra/sessions/<session id>/` that holds the artifacts of one session.
An agent that the write-scope guard confines to its session dir and the OS temp folder.
A change that Ostra can apply to remove one validation issue, such as a `default` route for a new agent.
A class that gives all readers of one key one fetch, one socket subscription, and a reload after each reconnect.
The frame around the screens: title bar, sidebar, tab strip, quick-question dock, and status bar. The phone has its own shell.
The console build for the site homepage, with `VITE_SHOT=1`, a memory router, and a postMessage bridge.
A record in the registry that shows one browser signed in. It holds an id, times, the user agent, and the IP.
One command of a shell line after the parser splits lists, pipelines, and substitutions. It has words, assignments, and redirects.
A `SKILL.md` file with instructions for agents. Ostra skills live in `.agents/skills/<name>/`.
A counter value that one agent execution holds. The count for a workspace cannot pass `limits.max_parallel_executions`.
The data that one REST request returns. It is the truth for a screen.
The `Label: value` lines that a spawn struct renders at the start of the first message.
The typed `Label: value` block that the engine gives to an agent as the start of its first message.
Server-sent events: the streamed HTTP response format that both providers read.
One node kind of the pipeline, a value of `StageKind`.
A file in a book folder that the latest write did not produce. `remove_stale` deletes it.
An atomic flag that becomes true when a response starts to produce output. After that, the retry policy does not retry.
One value of the enum `Step` that the planner returns and the runner runs, for example a judge call or a spawn.
The compact string from `Step::summary()` that a conformance fixture compares, for example `spawn explore explore#0`.
A hook event that reports the end of a turn of the CLI. Antigravity does not send it.
The reason that a model answer ended, as a `StopReason` value such as `EndTurn` or `MaxTokens`.
An event with its sequence number `seq` and its time `at`, as the store keeps it.
One key press with its modifiers, written as `ctrl+alt+shift+meta+<key>`.
A batch of watcher events that includes a file or folder that was created, removed, or renamed, so the file list is stale.
A submit status that says the agent hit a failure it cannot solve. It starts the Rescue judge.
A child of a section. It has the same fields as a section but has no children and no file of its own.
A conversation of executions. Its id is the id of its first execution.
The string of a Step::Judge that names what the decision is about, such as a gate ID or a phase key.
The call to `submit_<agent>` that gives the result of a run. The engine reads only this call.
The tool `submit_<agent>`. The agent calls it to end the execution with typed data that the engine reads.
The rendered text of the agent prompt for one executor, with the output rules and the guides.
A model class with four values: `fast`, `balanced`, `advanced`, and `frontier`.
The key that selects the column of an executor in `tool-mapping.toml` and in `[effort]`: `native`, `claude`, `codex`, `grok`, or `agy`.
A lowercase, stemmed word that `tokens` makes from text. An identifier also gives its camelCase and snake_case parts.
A named function that a model calls with a JSON input and that returns text.
A request from the model to run one tool with one input.
The setting `tool_enforcement` (Rule G1). When it is `enabled`, layer 1 also checks write scope, the report path, and self-protection.
A template variable such as `tool_read` that Ostra replaces with the tool name of the executor.
The section at the start of a harness prompt that maps each capability to the tool name of that harness.
The result of a tool call: text, an error flag, an optional exit code, a duration, an optional diff, and a coordination end.
A record that an execution wrote a file in a project. The server batches touches into `project_fs_changed` messages.
The value `light` or `full` that sets how much of the pipeline an `IMPLEMENT` request runs.
The stored list of `(role, content)` messages of one native execution. A resume rebuilds the conversation from it.
The recorded hash of folder-file content that lets Ostra start the programs which that content names.
A host rule from the user, such as an `allowed_hosts` entry or a harness base-URL host. It can resolve to a private address.
The Rust crate that writes a TypeScript type for each type that has `#[ts(export)]`. The files go to `web/src/api/gen/`.
A TypeScript type in `web/src/api/gen/` that ts-rs writes from a Rust type with `#[ts(export)]`.
TypeScript files in `web/src/api/gen/` that the command `cargo test -p ostra-core export_bindings` generates from Rust types.
A research document, spec, or plan stored as JSON, with markdown that Ostra renders from it.
A part of a book that a search hit points at: an overview, a section, a sub-section, a glossary term, or an architecture aspect.
A write whose target the parser cannot name, because of a variable, a glob, a substitution, or a dynamic folder.
A file that the user sends from the user computer, staged in the workspace and then claimed into the session uploads folder.
The token, cost, and time counts of one execution.
The usage that earlier runs of the same execution already spent. The engine adds it to the usage of the executor.
One problem of the settings, with a dotted `path` and a `message` that starts with the correction.
The Web Push scheme in which the server signs a short-lived ES256 token with its own P-256 key to prove its identity to the push service.
A passing build command after at least 3 consecutive failures, when the last failure had a diagnostic signature.
The 5 list items or table rows that one passage holds.
The standalone Windows crate in `tests/windows-probes` that checks the assumptions of the Windows sandbox design.
The `RwLock` in `WorkspaceRt` that requests hold for read when they start work and removals hold for write.
The cycle of work, review, and repair of one phase, stored as a `WorkLoop` with a `LoopNext` state.
The kind of a work pass: `Initial`, `Fix`, `BlockerFix`, `Resume`, `Rescue`, or `Rerun`.
A folder with `.ostra/workspace.toml` and `.ostra/workspace.db` that has a row in the registry and groups projects, settings, and sessions.
A file that the user keeps for every session of a workspace. Visible artifacts are in `.ostra/artifacts/`.
The settings of one workspace, kept in `workspace.toml` plus ten values that Ostra keeps in the registry.
The trait that gives a workspace the registry, global config, environment status, and engine services from the process that opens it.
The runtime of one open workspace: its settings access, database, engine, host, clone list, and work lock.
A path that a simple command creates, overwrites, moves, or deletes.
A session option in which Ostra answers approval asks itself instead of showing a card to the user.
